# Invariant Registry

## ACTIVE — issue #2799 (web privacy proof runs on production artifacts)

### I-2799-WEB-PRIVACY-PROOF-PRODUCTION-ARTIFACTS (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** The required #2771/#2795 browser privacy lane must measure production artifacts, not share each scenario's unchanged 45-second budget with cold development compilation. Business receives one keyed clean Expo export in `mingla-business/dist`, which the existing bundle guards and `expo serve` both reuse; Marketing receives one keyed production build and `next start`. Sibling-cookie evidence is scoped to storage visible at the page's exact URL, consent readiness waits for the exact `consent_granted` event, and the #2769 fixture generates its own bundle instead of depending on stale cache. No retry, timeout increase, sleep, skip, catch-and-pass, or assertion relaxation may substitute for readiness.
- **Enforcement:** `playwright.issue2771.config.ts`, the implementation and independent adversarial #2771 specs, the #2795 real-SDK alias oracle, the keyed export and existing ORCH-1083/#1627/ORCH-1137 artifact guards in `web-build-check.yml`, plus two distinct exact-head fresh-runner Web Build passes.
- **Fails on revert:** Restoring unscoped context cookies invents a sibling leak from the granted origin; restoring generic data-layer readiness observes zero `consent_granted` events; removing self-generated #2769 setup makes the cold production lane exhaust the unchanged test ceiling. Each true mutation failed independently and byte-exact restoration returned green.
- **Established:** ACTIVE after independent P0–P4-zero PASS at candidate `f6b42c0e71b519eb7cf1088dc14c9143fdb48957` on 2026-08-29, including a cold-cleared 16/16 production-artifact lane followed by a 16/16 repeat, #2769 16/16, two distinct fresh-runner Web Build passes, terminal CI, and zero review threads.

## ACTIVE — issue #2771 (web analytics starts only after explicit grant)

### I-PROPOSED-2771-NO-WEB-ANALYTICS-BEFORE-GRANT (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** On both Mingla web roots, absent, pending, malformed, unreadable, or denied consent forbids all non-essential analytics/attribution SDK import and initialization, vendor or extension/config script loading, cookie/local/session persistence, pageview/event/identity/exception/survey/replay/pixel activity, client attribution request/storage, and network to PostHog, Google Analytics, or ad vendors. Only a valid explicit `granted` choice may start those paths, once, and PostHog consent/storage must remain local to that exact origin rather than a parent domain visible to undecided sibling aliases. Essential consent preference storage and separately governed Sentry diagnostics are excluded.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2771-no-web-analytics-before-grant.mjs` (self-testing), its independent adversarial gate, append-only Business controller suites, the #2771 request/storage oracle, the #2795 real-SDK same-browser-context alias-isolation oracle, and fresh production proof after release.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent implementation, adversarial, mutation, request, and storage proofs established the blocking enforcement on both web roots. Exact-SHA release and fresh isolated production verification remain mandatory close evidence; this invariant strengthens and supersedes the insufficient enforcement—not the historical record—of `I-PROPOSED-1187-CONSENT-GATE-BEFORE-COOKIES`.

## ACTIVE — issue #2714 (campaign open analytics remain honest and isolated)

### I-2714-CAMPAIGN-OPEN-TRUTH (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Campaign email uses only `campaigns.usemingla.com`, with send-time eligibility stored atomically beside the provider message ID; transactional email remains on the untracked `usemingla.com` apex and campaign sending never falls back across that boundary. Historical eligibility and opens are never inferred or backfilled. Delivery and open coverage remain independent, open numerator and percentage use only eligible delivered mail, and absent or unhealthy evidence renders unknown rather than a fabricated zero. Signed campaign events that arrive before message-ID persistence reconcile idempotently and stale unmatched delivery/open debt is observable and withholds affected metrics.
- **Enforcement:** Forward migration `20270606002714_issue_2714_campaign_open_tracking_truth.sql`, the dedicated campaign sender/readback contract, `resend-webhook` retryable reconciliation handling, complete ID pagination in both reporting services, `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2714-campaign-open-truth.mjs`, and the existing `issue-1995-contact-book-blast.yml` CI lane.
- **Regression:** Append-only SQL, Deno, and Jest suites prove defaults/no backfill, sender isolation and Reply-To preservation, atomic eligibility, provider-first/message-first reconciliation, repeated-open monotonicity, eligible-denominator math, exact copy/helper, privacy disclosure, complete pagination, unknown-history rendering, and fail-closed unhealthy evidence across the shared Business iOS/Android/web analytics contract.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after PR #2722 merged all-green, the privacy disclosure and isolated provider/DNS configuration were verified in production, migration and edge receipts matched merged main, a controlled campaign produced matched sent/delivered/opened truth with zero unmatched or stale debt, transactional source remained untracked, and the product owner approved the binding runtime-evidence amendment recorded on issue #2714.

## DRAFT — issue #2148 / Phase 0 issue #2431 (CI topology remains bounded)

### I-PROPOSED-2148-CI-TOPOLOGY-BOUNDED (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Ordinary issue work adds tests and gates to stable shared registries; it never adds a new `.github/workflows/issue-*`, `orch-*`, or `meta-*` pull-request wrapper. A new capability-named workflow requires an issue-cited approval in a commit touching that file and must prove a unique runner/runtime, trust, production-operation, service-container, or required-context boundary that existing profiles cannot supply. Existing workflow modification and deletion remain allowed; test deletion does not.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2148-ci-topology-bounded.mjs` runs self-test then live in strict-grep class A, its committed issue #2431 happy-path proof executes in the same batch, and `.github/workflows/strict-grep-mingla-business.yml` triggers on every workflow-only diff.
- **Comparison (DRAFT, issue #2681):** the added-workflow set is computed against the MERGE BASE of the
  base branch and the head (`git diff --diff-filter=A A...B`), never against the base branch tip. Token
  attribution (`git log A..B`) and the base-registry lookup (`registryAt(base)`) are deliberately NOT
  merge-base-rebased: authorization is a property of the branch being merged INTO. A tip-to-tip added
  set both blames a stale branch for deletions it never made and hides an addition at a path the base
  branch already carries.
  **Caveat, measured under #2681 and NOT a structural guarantee:** the safety of this on a shallow
  clone rests on `git merge-base` returning the exact fork point or nothing. That holds while the base
  branch is LINEAR — which `main` is, being squash-only. With merge commits on both sides, a truncated
  window can return an older ancestor, and the gate then reports a clean added-set for a branch that
  genuinely adds a wrapper. Not reachable today; recorded so nobody reads the guarantee as unconditional
  if `main`'s history model ever changes.
- **Status:** DRAFT until the full #2148 consolidation programme reaches its final topology, completeness, required-context, and performance budgets. Phase 0 prevents new wrappers without deleting any existing workflow or test.

## DRAFT — issue #2148 / Phase 1 issue #2435 (CI execution registry is complete)

### I-PROPOSED-2148-SUITE-EXECUTION-COMPLETE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every historical CI origin has exactly one recorded disposition, and every executable migrated suite has exactly one reachable class route, typed invocation, pinned runtime/setup profile, real working directory, and real expected files. An omitted, duplicated, stale, empty, unknown, or live-plus-batched origin fails closed; registry discovery may prove completeness but never decides what executes.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/ci-batch/MANIFEST.json` schema v2, `.github/scripts/ci-batch/validate-manifest-v2.mjs`, and the issue #2435 strict-grep adversarial and implementor happy-path proofs in Class A. The amended Phase 1 locks are 199 origins, 23 executable suites, and 89 externally referenced live workflow providers; #2399's five checks moved from a standalone wrapper into the approved batch without losing assertion coverage.
- **Status:** DRAFT. Phase 1 records and guards current truth without deleting a workflow or test, changing a suite command, or changing required-context/trust behavior.

### I-PROPOSED-2148-SETUP-SINGLE-OWNER (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Each active registry suite names one setup profile, and that profile explicitly owns every class through which the suite can run. Unknown profiles, classes missing from the workflow matrix, matrix classes missing from the registry, and suites routed through a profile that does not own their class are hard failures.
- **Enforcement:** the same schema-v2 validator cross-checks `setupProfiles`, `classes`, every suite record, and the unchanged `.github/workflows/ci-batch.yml` matrix; its self-test mutates each boundary red before the live check is trusted.
- **Status:** DRAFT pending later #2148 phases that consolidate live wrappers and establish final required-check/performance budgets.

## DRAFT — issue #2148 / Phase 2 issue #2436 (CI execution is isolated and attributable)

### I-PROPOSED-2148-ONE-SETUP-PER-SHARD (DRAFT)

### I-PROPOSED-2148-SUITE-EXECUTION-ISOLATED (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every registered suite runs in a clean detached worktree under its own enforced deadline and process group. Failure or timeout kills descendants, cleans declared generated output, rejects unexpected mutations, and never prevents later suites from executing.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/ci-batch/run-suite-batch.mjs` plus the issue #2436 runtime regression covering continuation, missing inputs, mutation detection, generated-output cleanup, and descendant-process timeout.
- **Status:** DRAFT pending independent verification and the later #2148 wrapper and required-check phases.

### I-PROPOSED-2148-SUITE-RESULTS-HONEST (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Each shard emits machine-readable JSON and a GitHub summary naming setup/install executions and every expected suite's status, command fingerprint, duration, command counts, timeout, reason, and cleanup. Missing setup, files, directories, classes, result artifacts, or expected-versus-executed equality is red rather than skipped.
- **Enforcement:** the Phase 2 runner, artifact upload with `if-no-files-found: error`, and the Class A reporting regression.
- **Status:** DRAFT until the complete #2148 consolidation programme establishes final topology and performance budgets.

## ACTIVE — issue #2411 (free orders remain visible and countable without currency)

### I-PROPOSED-2411-ZERO-MONEY-ORDER-CURRENCY-NULL (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** A zero-money order may carry null currency and must map and count normally without a fallback. Any positive order, line, or succeeded-refund money requires a real, consistent currency or the entire event-order read fails closed.
- **Enforcement:** the #2411 implementor raw-row regression, the independent mixed-row/refund adversarial regression, and the shared `orderCurrencyContract` used by Host order mapping and money summaries.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent tester CONDITIONAL PASS, exact fail-on-revert proof, mobile runtime parity, and merge of PR #2420 (2026-08-21). The tester's two P4 limitations concern organizer-session and browser-tool provenance, not the protected contract.

### I-PROPOSED-2411-ORDER-READ-STATE-NOT-ZERO (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** No event-order consumer may convert disabled, loading, or error into empty, zero, false, or not-found. Only a successful ready-empty payload represents zero; a background failure retains the last truthful data and exposes an explicit stale-error signal.
- **Enforcement:** the #2411 implementor state-matrix regression, the independent rendered/source adversarial regression, and discriminated `EventOrdersRead` propagation across Host Home, Hub, event, order, guest, reconciliation, experience, and trip surfaces.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent tester CONDITIONAL PASS, exact fail-on-revert proof, mobile runtime parity, and merge of PR #2420 (2026-08-21). Production read-only truth at close was 6 orders and 12 valid free tickets, all legitimately zero-total with null currency.

## ACTIVE — issues #2264 / #2265 / #2253 (the buyer was told nothing, then told something false)

### I-2264-CHECKOUT-STATUS-ANSWER-NOT-DISCARDED (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Every caller of `ticket-checkout-status` consumes its TERMINAL verdict, not only `order.orderId`. A response typed narrowly enough that `{status:"failed", error:"paystack_charge_abandoned"}` is indistinguishable from "no order yet" is a discarded answer, and it costs the buyer the full poll budget followed by a message that is not true.
- **Enforcement:** `scripts/ci/check-checkout-status-consumers.sh`, wired into the class-D lane with `--self-test` running FIRST, plus `issue_2264_checkout_outcome_honesty.test.ts` and the tester-owned hostile-input suite. Scope is honest and bounded: the gate registers `ticket-checkout-status` callers only — the reservation and venue-ordering rails are #2289, not this.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after tester FAIL → rework → all conditions cleared, hardware confirmation by Seth on the 1.1.5 OTA (2026-08-19), and verified merge of PR #2288.

### I-2265-CHECKOUT-PENDING-SURFACE-SURVIVES (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** From the moment a buyer commits until there is an outcome, the surface they committed on stays up and visibly says so, and cannot be dismissed by ANY route. `BaseBottomSheet` dismisses by four: the close button and the backdrop go through props; hardware-back and `onRequestClose` call `onClose()` DIRECTLY and never touch a prop. A guard that pins only the prop routes leaves Android hardware-back able to kill a pending sheet while staying green.
- **Enforcement:** `issue_2265_pending_surface_survives.test.ts` pinning all four routes individually, plus the runtime-proven swipe refusal. The pending state itself was already built at `TicketCartSheet.tsx:910` and had never rendered a frame in production because `setCartVisible(false)` ran one line before `handleBuy`.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after hardware confirmation and verified merge of PR #2288.

### I-2253-NATIVE-CHECKOUT-SINGLE-FLIGHT (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** `useNativeCheckoutFlow` refuses a second concurrent call for the same cart ON ITS OWN. Safety does not depend on every screen remembering to guard it — that arrangement is what produced #2242 (a five-site migration that moved four) and #2227 (five call sites, four never run on iOS).
- **Enforcement:** T-12 calls the returned function twice **directly, with no screen and no component**, and asserts exactly one `ticket-checkout-create`. Verified against real production rows: a full paid journey produced one session; a UI rapid double-tap produced zero extras.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after verified merge of PR #2288.

### I-2264-NATIVE-CHECKOUT-ERRORS-TOTAL-MAPPER (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** The return-leg mapper is TOTAL against hostile input, not merely against expected input. A lookup table carrying `Object.prototype` returns a Function for `toString`, `constructor`, `valueOf` and `__proto__`, which `?? fallback` cannot catch. Tables reached by an untrusted key are `Object.create(null)` AND own-property guarded — the guard fixes the call site, the missing prototype fixes every one added later.
- **Enforcement:** `issue_2264_checkout_outcome_honesty.test.ts` T-2 covering ten prototype keys behaviourally, the tester's `issue_2264_return_leg_hostile_inputs.tester_adversarial.test.ts`, and a parity assertion pinning that neither the consumer nor business mapper resolves anything it does not own.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after rework and verified merge of PR #2288. The repo had already written this trap down — #2229's adversarial suite warns of it in the same module — and we walked into it one function further down the same file, out of the pin's reach.

### I-PROPOSED-PAYSTACK-ABANDONED-ONLY-AFTER-BROWSER-CLOSES (DRAFT — owned by #2250)
- **Rule:** Paystack records a transaction as `abandoned` from initialize onward, BEFORE the buyer types anything. So a poll running CONCURRENTLY with an open browser must never honour the terminal abandoned token — it would tell a buyer mid-payment that they walked away. This repo's own bank transfer (`06fd4518…`, created 01:37:50, paid 01:41:05) is a 3m15s window of exactly that exposure.
- **Enforcement:** Protective comment planted at both poll sites, pinned by source position rather than by comment text. Flips ACTIVE with #2250, which cannot restructure auto-close without honouring it.
- **Status:** DRAFT. Runtime-supported: T-19 confirmed a Transfer buyer who closes the browser is NOT told they left, because Paystack held the charge non-terminal throughout. USSD and Bank channels remain unfired.

## ACTIVE — issues #2242 / #2227 / #2229 (Explorer buyers could not load tickets from a link, and could not pay at all)

### I-2242-CART-READS-THE-SCREENS-TICKET-SOURCE (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** On `ConsumerEventDetailScreen`, `<TicketCartSheet tickets=…>` reads the same canonical-first source the page body reads, and never reads `ticketsQuery.data` directly. The binding is to `coldReadPlan.canonical`, never to `canonicalQuery.data`, and it is held in a NAMED local (`cartTickets`) — the inline expression is a prefix substring of the body's own line, so a guard written against the inline form is satisfied by the body alone and passes on a fully reverted cart. That is not hypothetical: it is what happened.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-1929-hidden-direct-checkout.mjs` (three assertions, two self-test mutations), `app-mobile/src/screens/Event/__tests__/issue_2242_cold_route_cart_ticket_source.test.ts` (T-01..T-07), and the tester-owned adversarial suite that compiles the real production expressions with `new Function` and runs them across every reachable state.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after tester PASS with zero findings, a before-shot captured on verbatim pre-fix code (cart still spinning at 15s), and verified merge of PR #2247 on 2026-08-18.

### I-2242-GUARD-NAMES-WHAT-IT-CHECKS (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** A strict-grep assertion whose failure message names an invariant asserts on EVERY site that invariant covers, and its `--self-test` carries a mutation for each site. A guard that names more than it inspects is worse than no guard: it converts an unchecked site into a site everyone believes is checked.
- **Enforcement:** The repaired `issue-1929-hidden-direct-checkout.mjs`, proven by execution to exit 1 against verbatim pre-fix code where it previously exited 0.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after verified merge of PR #2247 on 2026-08-18. This is the generalisation of the defect that made #2242 possible — the gate whose failure message read "cold tickets not bundle-owned" had never inspected the cart.

### I-2227-NATIVE-PROVIDER-REDIRECT-IS-NEVER-AN-HTTPS-AUTHSESSION (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** No native call site hands an `https` URL to `openAuthSessionAsync`. On iOS 17.4+ `expo-web-browser` maps that to `ASWebAuthenticationSession(callback: .https(...))`, which Apple permits only with a `webcredentials:` Associated Domain — absent in both apps and absent from the served `apple-app-site-association`. iOS then rejects the session at `start()` and completes it with `canceledLogin`, which the system prints as the misleading line `SFAuthenticationSession was cancelled by user`. Provider pages open with `openBrowserAsync`.
- **Enforcement:** `scripts/ci/check-native-authsession-redirects.sh`, wired as its own steps in the class-D lane with `--self-test` running FIRST, plus `app-mobile/src/payments/__tests__/issue_2227_*` and the tester-owned adversarial suites. Falsifiability proven from CI's literal `run:` command, not from a test that shells out to the same script: with the defect restored at the business call site, 32 of 34 behavioural assertions still passed and only the gate caught it.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after tester CONDITIONAL PASS with all three conditions cleared, confirmation on physical iPhone hardware by Seth on the 1.1.5 OTA, and verified merge of PR #2249 on 2026-08-18.

### I-2229-NO-BUYER-EVER-SEES-A-MACHINE-TOKEN (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Every bounded error token `ticket-checkout-create` can emit reaches the buyer as a human sentence stating whether money moved. The mapper is TOTAL: an unrecognised token, an empty string, and null all resolve to the generic message, and the mapper never returns its input. Safety comes from totality, not from the enumeration being correct — the tester derived the token set from live source and found 39 where the spec had transcribed 37, and `sign_in_required` appears in no hand-written list in the repo.
- **Enforcement:** `app-mobile/src/payments/checkoutErrorMessages.ts` plus `issue_2229_native_checkout_error_messages.test.ts` and the tester-owned totality suite, which drives all 39 tokens × 15 statuses through the mapper and × 7 statuses through the real flow to `outcome.message`.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after verified merge of PR #2249 on 2026-08-18.

## ACTIVE — issue #2180 (get-app link opens the installed app and strands the user)

### I-2180-CLAIMED-LINK-NEVER-DEAD-ENDS (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Every URL either mobile app can be handed by the OS resolves to a screen the user can act on. A link on a claimed domain whose path the app does not serve resolves to `/`, which gates home versus sign-in. No incoming link may terminate on `+not-found`, on expo-router's `Unmatched` view, or on any screen without a visible, tappable exit. The decision is taken in `app/+native-intent.tsx` before the origin is stripped, on cold start (`initial: true`) and warm foreground (`initial: false`) alike; host matching is exact parsed-hostname equality, never `includes`, `endsWith`, or a regex over the raw URL.
- **Enforcement:** `mingla-business/__tests__/issue_2180_native_intent.implementor.happy.test.ts` (T-1..T-7, T-10, T-11), the tester-owned `issue_2180_native_intent.tester_adversarial.test.ts` (device URL parser, exhaustive over-blocking sweep, idempotence), and the allowlist-to-route-tree sync assertion that reds the build when a route is added without registering its segment.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after tester CONDITIONAL PASS with all three conditions cleared, and verified merge of PR #2219 on 2026-08-18.

### I-2180-BRAND-IMAGE-EXPLICIT-DIMENSIONS (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Any React Native `<Image>` rendering a `@mingla/brand-assets` master declares an explicit numeric `width` AND an explicit numeric `height`. `aspectRatio` is never used in place of a `height`, and the rule applies to every style member that can reach the element — including members composed through a ternary, `&&`, or `??` — not merely to their merged result. The masters are up to 2000x2000 at scale 1, so an under-constrained Image lays out at 2000 pt and silently pushes its siblings off-screen.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2180-brand-image-explicit-dimensions.mjs` (repo-wide across `mingla-business` and `app-mobile`, per-style-member, with a frozen shrink-only two-file exemption list and a self-test covering both conditional operators), its tester-owned adversarial suite, and the not-found structure tests that drive the full iOS Dynamic Type multiplier range so both branches of the conditional are genuinely rendered.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after proof by execution — the height deleted from each of four brand-image styles across both `+not-found.tsx` files in turn, each reddening only the branch it belongs to — and verified merge of PR #2219 on 2026-08-18.
## DRAFT — issue #2321 (Explorer account deletion never deleted, and said it had)

### I-2321-RETAINED-AUTH-CANNOT-CLAIM-DELETED (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** No deletion surface may render its fully-deleted success copy on a response with `authRetained === true`. Concretely: in `app-mobile/src/components/profile/AccountSettings.tsx` the render branch reachable when `authRetained === true` must not reference `settings:delete.success_title`, `success_body` or `success_sub`; and for every one of the 29 shipped locales, `delete.retained_title !== delete.success_title`. In `mingla-business/app/account/delete.tsx` the retained branch must not render the non-retained headline string.
- **Why a rule and not a preference.** The server has reported `authRetained` since #668 and the consumer client discarded it for the entire life of the feature, on a shipped app, in a flow Apple 5.1.1(v) and Play's deletion policy both audit. The failure is invisible to types (`authRetained` is optional), to lint, and to any test that only asserts the happy path — the two branches render the same component with the same styles, so nothing structural distinguishes them. Production logs show `authRetained: true` on all four of the reporter's real attempts, over a render path that had no branch at all.
- **Distinct-string form, not a boolean check.** Asserting "there is an `if`" would pass if both arms rendered the same key. Asserting that the two title strings differ, per locale, cannot pass vacuously (#2113) and fails if a locale is added without the new key — the gate pins the locale count at 29 for exactly that reason.
- **Corollary — the client states the outcome, not the server's sentence.** Neither app may echo the edge function's `message` as its user-facing outcome copy. Investigation F-6 proved that message can be false: a brand-new account with no Business side was told "Your business login is unchanged."
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2321-retained-auth-cannot-claim-deleted.mjs` (A1/A2/A5, self-test wired, Class A) and `app-mobile/src/components/profile/__tests__/issue_2321_retained_branch_cannot_claim_deleted.implementor.happy.test.ts` (lifts the real handler conditional out of the source and executes it with `new Function` across every reachable payload, then asserts on the keys the selected branch actually contains). The Business branch is structural and is therefore guarded by A5 rather than a prohibited source-only Jest pin.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2321 SPEC 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge and merged-main verification.

### I-2321-SIDE-GATE-IS-FALSIFIABLE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every exported `userHasActive*Side` predicate in `supabase/functions/_shared/accountDeletionSides.ts` must have a reachable `return false` on its terminal path, must reference only columns that exist in the production schema, and must not treat a query error as an absence of rows. The identity-scrub UPDATE in `purgeExplorerSideData()` must bind its result and throw on error.
- **Why.** `userHasActiveExplorerSide()` shipped with a bare `return true` after every check, making six probes decorative; three of those six additionally referenced columns that do not exist (`boards.user_id`, `pairings.user_id`, `preferences.id`), so they would have carried no information even without the trailing return. A predicate that cannot return false is not a check. Combined with a `profiles.explorer_deleted_at` column that was never applied to production, this made `shouldDeleteAuthUser()` return false for every user on both sides — no Explorer account was ever deletable in production — while the identity scrub failed wholesale and silently for the same missing column.
- **Absence is not failure.** A count probe that errors must throw, never resolve to zero. That distinction is the whole difference between "this user has no friends" and "this query 400'd", and reading the second as the first is what let the gate look thorough while proving nothing (#2113 class).
- **Enforcement:** the same gate file (A3/A4), plus `supabase/functions/_shared/__tests__/issue_2321_account_deletion_sides.implementor.happy.test.ts`, which executes the real module against a fake PostgREST client: the predicate returns false for an empty user, returns true for each of the five real row sources, throws on a forced probe error for every one of them, and the scrub throws on a forced write error.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2321 SPEC 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge and merged-main verification.

## ACTIVE — issue #2262 (campaign composer responsive layout)

### I-2262-MEASURED-NOT-COMPUTED-LAYOUT (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** In a full-height screen, no element's height may be produced by subtracting a hardcoded chrome constant from — or taking a fraction of — a viewport height (`useWindowDimensions()`, `Dimensions.get(...)`, `window.innerHeight`, `visualViewport.height`). Remaining space is claimed with `flex: 1` + `minHeight: 0`. Where a child genuinely cannot flex (a WebView-hosted rich-text editor), it is fed a value **measured** by `onLayout` on its own container — never estimated — and that measured value may be consumed only by that child.
- **Why:** #2262 proved `CHROME_CONTENT_PX = 376` was short by a structural term (the ungated 56pt route TopBar + 8pt padding) plus 12pt, making the campaign composer overflow by a device-independent ~76pt on every iOS device before a character is typed, with no scroll recovery on native. The constant was not mistuned; it was the wrong instrument.
- **Boundary (what this rule does NOT forbid):** a `minHeight` floor on a child that claims its space with `flex: 1` is permitted — it participates in no subtraction, reads no viewport, and is bounded by a parent carrying `minHeight: 0` + `overflow: 'hidden'`. What is forbidden is a height DERIVED from a viewport by subtraction or fraction, and any floor or clamp applied to such a derivation. `Math.max(120, windowHeight - 376)` is a violation; `minHeight: composerSheetMinHeight` on a flexed sheet is not.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/i-2262-composer-measured-not-computed-layout.mjs` (self-test wired, Class A) plus `composerBandContract.issue2262.render.test.tsx` (react-test-renderer) and `composerViewportFit.issue2262.web.render.test.tsx` (the REAL react-native-web resolver, with a V-0 vacuity guard).
- **Scope at establishment:** the campaign composer file set. The #2262 blast-radius sweep found exactly ONE live site of this shape in the whole Business app, so the rule is stated generally and enforced narrowly; widening the gate's target list is an append-only change.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2262 SPEC 2026-08-18; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge and merged-main verification.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent tester PASS (P0: 0, P1: 0) — narrow web re-measured at 0px commit-bar offset across 1/4/8/16/32 paragraphs at 320x568, 390x750 and 768x1024, with the real Personalize panel, keyboard-open visualViewport and SMS all at 0; a byte-for-byte revert of the P1-1 fix turning 38 tests red; Seth's operator verification on the iOS simulator including the long-draft case; and verified merge of PR #2282 on 2026-08-19.

### I-2262-ACTION-ROW-NEVER-LEAVES-THE-VIEWPORT (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** The campaign composer's primary action row (`ComposerFooter`) is an in-flow flex sibling carrying `flexShrink: 0` on all four surfaces — Business iOS, Business Android, desktop web and mobile web — and carries no `position: absolute` on any branch. Every region that can grow (expandable insertion panels, media strips, Dynamic Type, the editor body) lives inside a single preceding sibling band that is `flex: 1, minHeight: 0, overflow: 'hidden'`, so growth is absorbed by that band and can never displace the action row. On web the screen's flex chain is rooted in a host pinned to `useWindowDimensions().height` (SSR-guarded `> 0`), because the CSS layout viewport does not shrink for a soft keyboard and `react-native-keyboard-controller` is a verified no-op on web.
- **Failure-mode corollary:** a wrong `onLayout` measurement can only mis-size the editor. It is structurally incapable of moving the action row, because no ancestor, sibling or footer style reads the measured value.
- **Additional clauses (reconciled with the #2262 DESIGN contract):** the action row may never be a descendant of a scroll container on any surface — where a responsive recovery scroll exists, it wraps the flexible band only. The action row is never a step in the responsive shed ladder: it is the last thing standing. Any scrim or fade above it is an in-flow `flexShrink: 0` sibling, never absolutely positioned over the composing surface. Its `paddingBottom` is `Math.max(insets.bottom, spacing.md)`, never a bare `insets.bottom`, because `insets.bottom` reads 0 on mobile web (no `viewport-fit=cover`).
- **Why:** #2262 measured the footer 89px below the fold at 390x750, 181px at 320x568, overlapping the body by 129px at 1024x700 and 9px at 1440x900, and floating 285px away from the last SMS control at 1440x900 — one component with two contradictory layout contracts, neither responding to what was on screen.
- **Enforcement:** the same strict-grep gate, plus `playwright/issue2262/composer-viewport-fit.spec.ts` (real Chromium, four viewports, real clicks, keyboard-open visual-viewport simulation).
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2262 SPEC 2026-08-18; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge and merged-main verification.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent tester PASS (P0: 0, P1: 0) — narrow web re-measured at 0px commit-bar offset across 1/4/8/16/32 paragraphs at 320x568, 390x750 and 768x1024, with the real Personalize panel, keyboard-open visualViewport and SMS all at 0; a byte-for-byte revert of the P1-1 fix turning 38 tests red; Seth's operator verification on the iOS simulator including the long-draft case; and verified merge of PR #2282 on 2026-08-19.

### I-2262-EDITABLE-OWNS-THE-BOX (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** For the web rich-text composer, the height, padding, font-size, line-height, box-sizing and overflow of the typing surface are declared on the **contenteditable** (`.mingla-composer-editor` / `.ProseMirror`) via the injected stylesheet — never on Tiptap's `EditorContent` wrapper, which renders a container the contenteditable is appended into. The editable carries a `min-height` floor derived from its own type scale and padding (16pt horizontal / 8pt vertical), never a bare pixel literal, and declares its own `::selection` colour so the brand selection highlight is not the browser/WebView default. A wrapper-level click handler may exist only as a backstop that no-ops when the click already landed inside `.ProseMirror`.
- **Why:** #2262 measured a 23px focusable `.ProseMirror` inside a 480px box on desktop web and inside a 450px box on mobile web: 95% of the message box was inert, `document.elementFromPoint` returned an inert DIV at 50% and 90% down, and a real click at the box's centre left `document.activeElement` on `BODY`. Native pell has no equivalent because its own template already emits `.pell-content { height: 100% }` under `box-sizing: border-box`.
- **Enforcement:** `composerEditableFillsBox.issue2262.test.ts` (parses the real `COMPOSER_CHIP_CSS` export, not a source grep) plus the real-Chromium click and fill assertions in `composer-viewport-fit.spec.ts`.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2262 SPEC 2026-08-18; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge and merged-main verification.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent tester PASS (P0: 0, P1: 0) — narrow web re-measured at 0px commit-bar offset across 1/4/8/16/32 paragraphs at 320x568, 390x750 and 768x1024, with the real Personalize panel, keyboard-open visualViewport and SMS all at 0; a byte-for-byte revert of the P1-1 fix turning 38 tests red; Seth's operator verification on the iOS simulator including the long-draft case; and verified merge of PR #2282 on 2026-08-19.

- **Rule:** Explorer native and Host native/web logged-out welcome screens keep one presentation owner per app; the regular orange `MINGLA_WORDMARK` is fully contained in the compact white capsule, exact two-line product promise and legal text remain white with restrained shadow, and every idle auth action remains a white surface with dark content above an always-present local poster and 74% black veil. Native bundles require only the approved portrait media and Host web only the approved landscape media. Reduced motion, save-data, lifecycle pause, unsupported video, and playback failure stay poster-safe and never own or block authentication or navigation.

### I-2262-CONTROL-STATE-MUST-BE-REACHABLE (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** A control that renders a distinct state (active / selected / on) MUST be bound to a source capable of actually producing that state, and a regression test MUST prove the RENDERED treatment changes when the source flips — not merely that the prop is no longer a literal. Asserting `active={...}` is not `active={false}` is satisfied by binding it to an expression that can never be true.
- **Why:** #2262 found `InsertionBar.tsx:187,196,206,216` hardcoding `active={false}` for the bold / italic / underline / link controls while the sibling panel toggles at 225/234/242 bind real state. The formatting controls have never been able to show state on any surface. On web the source is one line (`editor.isActive('bold')`); on native it is new plumbing, because `COMPOSER_SELECTION_TRACKER_JS` saves the live range into the WebView's own `window` and reports nothing back to React Native — there is no `postMessage`, no `ReactNativeWebView` and no `onMessage` handler in that graph.
- **Class:** this is the UI form of the repo's "checks that carry no information" bug class (#2113). A state that can never fire carries exactly as much information as a test that can never fail.
- **Enforcement:** a behavioural render assertion (mock the selection source, flip it, assert the rendered fill changes), never a source grep.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2262 SPEC AMENDMENT 2026-08-18 (reconciliation with the DESIGN contract, constraint 10.10); flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge and merged-main verification.
- **Status:** ACTIVE after independent tester PASS (P0: 0, P1: 0) — narrow web re-measured at 0px commit-bar offset across 1/4/8/16/32 paragraphs at 320x568, 390x750 and 768x1024, with the real Personalize panel, keyboard-open visualViewport and SMS all at 0; a byte-for-byte revert of the P1-1 fix turning 38 tests red; Seth's operator verification on the iOS simulator including the long-draft case; and verified merge of PR #2282 on 2026-08-19.

## ACTIVE — issue #1914 (elapsed RSVP writes fail closed and RSVP appears in brand Upcoming — CLOSED 2026-08-11, PR #1917, production database + Edge Function deployed)

> Registered DRAFT at issue #1914 IMPLEMENT and activated at CLOSE after independent tester PASS, the all-green merge, surgical production migration apply, exact merged Edge deployment, and read-only production verification.

### I-RSVP-WRITE-MASTER-END-GATED (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every call to the nine-argument `public.submit_event_rsvp` resolves exactly one canonical master `event_dates` row inside the transaction before capacity, RSVP identity/upsert, guest, QR/pass, acknowledgement, outbox, or delivery work. Missing or invalid master data raises exact SQLSTATE `P1902` with message `rsvp_date_unavailable`; `master end_at <= clock_timestamp()` raises exact SQLSTATE `P1901` with message `rsvp_event_ended`. `submit_event_rsvp_with_delivery` remains the sole Edge-called wrapper and cannot enqueue anything when the guarded base RPC raises. `public-submit-rsvp` maps only `error.code`: P1901 to HTTP 410 and P1902 to HTTP 409; raw database messages/details/hints and PII never enter the new response or structured rejection log.
- **Enforcement:** Forward migration `20270322001902_issue_1902_public_event_lifecycle.sql`, the unchanged delivery-wrapper dependency, service-role-only base-RPC grant, `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-1902-rsvp-backend-safety.mjs`, and `.github/workflows/issue-1902-rsvp-backend-safety-tests.yml`.
- **Regression:** Implementor Deno and PostgreSQL 17 suites pin guard ordering, exact SQLSTATE/message pairs, equality/after-end rejection, missing-master rejection, pre-end success, wrapper reachability, grant posture, and zero rejected-write deltas across RSVP, guest/pass, notification/outbox, and delivery tables. The independent tester adds distinct duplicate/ambiguous-master, auth-mode, race, and real-handler HTTP attacks before activation. Every proof is append-only and CI-wired.
- **Scope:** Backend prerequisite serving Consumer iOS, Consumer Android, buyer/anonymous web, Business iOS/Android public preview, and Business web preview. No client renderer, Business Hub management, Admin UI, ticket checkout, production fixture, deploy, or OTA behavior is changed by this invariant.
- **Established:** ACTIVE 2026-08-11 at #1914 CLOSE (independent tester PASS, PR #1917, production migration and byte-identical Edge Function deployment verified).

### I-PUBLIC-BRAND-UPCOMING-INCLUDES-RSVP (ACTIVE)

## ACTIVE — issue #1881 (business native sign-in failures are classified, bounded-retried, and never render raw error values)

> ACTIVE at #1881 CLOSE. This is the `mingla-business` parity contract for the already-ACTIVE `I-PROPOSED-1875-SIGNIN-FAILURE-CLASSIFIED-AND-OPAQUE`; activation followed independent runtime-visible TEST evidence, two different fails-on-revert guards, all-green PR #1908, and merged-main verification at `330414a9dc7990337f0cc29bd629a4ea09a566e5`.

### I-PROPOSED-1881-BUSINESS-SIGNIN-FAILURE-CLASSIFIED-AND-OPAQUE (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every native Google or Apple sign-in failure surfaced from `mingla-business/src/context/AuthContext.tsx` MUST be classified by the single named predicate `classifyAuthFailure` and rendered from the fixed keyed auth-copy registry — NEVER from `error.message`, `err`, `code`, `status`, `name`, a URL, an error code, `audienceHint`, or any value derived from a caught error. **An unrecognised error is `permanent` and is never retried**; that default is the rule, not a fallback. Automatic retry is permitted ONLY on the Supabase `signInWithIdToken` leg, ONLY for `transient-transport*`, with exactly two extra attempts after 400 ms and 1200 ms, bounded by a counter compared against the frozen constant `TRANSPORT_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. The provider leg (`GoogleSignin.signIn()` / `AppleAuthentication.signInAsync()`) is NEVER auto-retried because doing so re-presents the account picker or Apple system sheet. Retry is cancelled at checkpoints before and after each backoff when the provider unmounts or `AppState.currentState === "background"`; cancellation suppresses the user-facing `Alert` ONLY, never the #1044 `reportNonFatal` capture, return value, or existing engineering telemetry. The pre-existing Google existing-user/session reconciliation retry remains a distinct mechanism and MUST NOT be counted, rewritten, or removed by this transport policy.
- **The trap this invariant exists to keep closed:** `classifyAuthFailure` MUST NOT reference `statusCodes.INTERNAL_ERROR`, `statusCodes.NETWORK_ERROR`, or `statusCodes.TIMEOUT`. The installed Business dependency is `@react-native-google-signin/google-signin@16.1.2`, whose frozen `statusCodes` has exactly five names — `SIGN_IN_CANCELLED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PLAY_SERVICES_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`, and `NULL_PRESENTER`; the three tempting names do not exist. Comparing a possibly-undefined code with one of those undefined members matches every codeless error and recreates the #1038 blind spot that `I-1044-AUTH-FAILURE-REPORTED` closes. Android provider-transient classification keys only on the numeric strings emitted by the bridge (`"7"`, `"8"`, `"15"`) and only when `Platform.OS === "android"`. `"10"`, `"getTokens"`, `"12500"`, `"14"`, every iOS Google code, every Supabase API error, and every unknown/codeless shape remain permanent. Supabase transport classification keys on `err.name === "AuthRetryableFetchError"`, never `instanceof`.
- **Surface boundary:** This rule covers Business iOS and Business Android native paths. Business web preview exits each callback before the native `try`/`catch` and uses Supabase `signInWithOAuth` redirect; it MUST remain byte-equivalent outside the declared native regions and MUST NOT acquire native retry, native Alert copy, Google SDK calls, or provider-modal replay. Consumer iOS/Android remain owned by #1875. Buyer/anonymous web and admin web are outside this authentication path.
- **Enforcement:** `classifyAuthFailure`, frozen retry constants, the two native token-exchange loops, cancellation checkpoints, and fixed key-to-copy resolution in `mingla-business/src/context/AuthContext.tsx` plus its scoped copy registry. A dedicated #1881 workflow runs the append-only implementor happy-path suite and the independently-authored tester adversarial suite unconditionally. Both suites execute slices of the REAL shipped source; neither may test a hand-retyped implementation. The frozen #1044 Business suites may be amended only where their expected Alert copy, pre-change catch baselines, and dependency maps necessarily change; every such edit is marker-gated and no capture, `extra`, fingerprint, ordering, cancellation, or failure-safety assertion may be weakened.
- **Regression test:** Fails on true line deletion. Deleting either transport loop yields one token-exchange call instead of three; restoring raw `e.message`/`${msg}${audienceHint}` leaks a Supabase URL into the alert; changing the default from `permanent` retries unknown errors; swapping numeric strings for the nonexistent `statusCodes.*` names misclassifies codeless errors; deleting the counter bound never terminates; deleting either cancellation checkpoint produces extra attempts and a stale visible modal; retrying a provider call re-presents it and violates the exactly-once provider assertion; suppressing `reportNonFatal` on cancellation yields zero captures. The tester must add a genuinely different angle, including a human-visible runtime assertion rather than DOM/source presence alone.
- **Relationship to `I-1044-AUTH-FAILURE-REPORTED` (ACTIVE):** Strictly additive. `shouldReportAuthFailure` and `reportNonFatal.ts` remain byte-identical; capture remains the first catch action, with the same Google five-key / Apple four-key `extra` allowlists and fingerprints. A transient exchange that later succeeds emits no failure capture; an exhausted or cancelled retry emits exactly one. The full original error remains engineering evidence and never becomes user copy.
- **Established:** ACTIVE at #1881 CLOSE 2026-08-11 after independent tester PASS, physical-device and real-browser visibility proof, all-green PR #1908, and merged-main verification at `330414a9dc7990337f0cc29bd629a4ea09a566e5`. Contract source: #1875 / PR #1884 / merge `892a07fbf`, ported against Business google-signin `16.1.2` and Supabase JS/Auth `2.103.0`.

## ACTIVE — issue #1875 (native sign-in failures are classified, bounded-retried, and never render raw error values)

> ACTIVE at #1875 CLOSE. Root cause (#1875 investigation, F-3 + F-4, operator-locked scope): `app-mobile/src/hooks/useAuthSimple.ts` treated a transient transport failure identically to a permanent authentication failure — no retry, no offline-aware path — and then rendered `error.message` verbatim to the user. For a 502/503/504 that message is `JSON.stringify(Response)`, because `@supabase/auth-js`'s `_getErrorMessage` falls through to `JSON.stringify(err)` when the argument is a `Response` — so a one-second connectivity blip dead-ended the user behind a modal containing our Supabase project URL and a blob id. Constitution rule 3 (a failure that surfaces, but uselessly).

### I-PROPOSED-1875-SIGNIN-FAILURE-CLASSIFIED-AND-OPAQUE (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every native sign-in failure surfaced to a user in `app-mobile/src/hooks/useAuthSimple.ts` (`signInWithGoogle` AND `signInWithApple`) MUST be (a) classified by the single named predicate `classifyAuthFailure`, and (b) rendered from a fixed i18n key — NEVER from `error.message`, `err`, `code`, `status`, `name`, a URL, an error code, or any value derived from a caught error. **An unrecognised error is `permanent` and is never retried** — that default is the rule, not a fallback. Automatic retry is permitted ONLY on the Supabase `signInWithIdToken` leg (where the provider ID token is already held and no UI is re-presented), ONLY for the `transient-transport*` classes, bounded by a counter compared against a frozen constant rather than by a predicate over the error, and cancelled at the two checkpoints around each backoff when the hook unmounts or `AppState.currentState === "background"`. The provider leg (`GoogleSignin.signIn()`, `AppleAuthentication.signInAsync()`) is NEVER auto-retried, because retrying re-presents a system account picker the user did not ask for. Cancellation suppresses the user-facing `Alert` ONLY — never the `reportNonFatal` capture, never `logger`/`console`/Mixpanel, never the return value.
- **The trap this invariant exists to keep closed:** `classifyAuthFailure` MUST NOT reference `statusCodes.INTERNAL_ERROR`, `statusCodes.NETWORK_ERROR` or `statusCodes.TIMEOUT`. `@react-native-google-signin/google-signin@16.0.0`'s `errorCodes.js` destructures exactly four native constants — `SIGN_IN_CANCELLED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PLAY_SERVICES_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` — so those three names are `undefined`, and comparing a possibly-`undefined` `code` against an `undefined` constant matches EVERY codeless error. That is the exact F-7 trap `I-1044-AUTH-FAILURE-REPORTED` was written to prevent, and it would land inside the fix for it. The Android transient set is keyed on the numeric string literals the native bridge actually produces (`ErrorDto.kt`: `this.code = codeInt.toString()`) — `"7"` NETWORK_ERROR, `"8"` INTERNAL_ERROR, `"15"` TIMEOUT — and is gated on `Platform.OS === "android"`. `"10"` DEVELOPER_ERROR, `"getTokens"`, `"12500"`, `"14"` INTERRUPTED and every iOS `kGIDSignInErrorCode` stay permanent. The Supabase transient set is keyed on `err.name === "AuthRetryableFetchError"` — a plain string set explicitly by `CustomAuthError`'s constructor — never `instanceof`, which is unreliable under Metro's module resolution and unavailable inside the `new Function` test harness.
- **What this invariant does NOT claim:** it guarantees the user-facing string is drawn from a fixed key set, not that the copy is good. It does not cover `mingla-business`, whose `src/context/AuthContext.tsx` carries both defects verbatim and is tracked as a separate parity issue. It does not cover the web OAuth redirect flow, which has no native catch block.
- **Enforcement:** `classifyAuthFailure` + the two bounded retry loops + the four copy states in `app-mobile/src/hooks/useAuthSimple.ts`, plus the five new keys in `app-mobile/src/i18n/locales/en/auth.json` (English-only; `fallbackLng: 'en'` serves the other 28 locales, per the #1642 precedent). Guarded by `.github/workflows/issue-1875-google-signin-transient-failure-tests.yml` running the implementor happy-path suite `app-mobile/src/hooks/__tests__/useAuthSimple.transientSignInFailure.issue1875.test.ts` and the tester adversarial suite `…transientSignInFailure.adversarial.issue1875.test.ts`. Both slice and EXECUTE the REAL shipped source via `new Function` rather than a retyped copy — ORCH-1373 P2-2 proved a replica test stays green while the real guard is deleted. Registered explicitly by path, never by glob; no strict-grep MANIFEST entry is added, so MANIFEST totality, `expectedStrictGrepMjsFiles` and `selfTestWiredFloor` are untouched.
- **Regression test:** fails-on-revert. Restoring `Alert.alert("Google Sign-In Failed", error.message)` makes the anti-leak matrix (SC-19) fail with `gqnoajqerqhnvulmnyvv.supabase.co` present in the alert arguments. Deleting the retry loop makes SC-8/SC-9 fail as `expected 3 calls, actual 1`. Swapping `"8"` for `statusCodes.INTERNAL_ERROR` makes SC-5/SC-6 fail, because every codeless error then classifies transient. Flipping R6's default from `permanent` to transient makes SC-6 fail. Removing the counter bound from the loop condition makes the termination test hang. Deleting the C1/C2 cancellation checkpoints makes SC-13/SC-14 fail with 3 calls instead of 1 and a spurious alert. Conditionalising `reportNonFatal` on cancellation makes SC-13 fail as `expected 1 capture, actual 0`. Append-only.
- **Relationship to `I-1044-AUTH-FAILURE-REPORTED` (ACTIVE):** strictly additive, never weakening. `shouldReportAuthFailure` is byte-identical to `origin/main`; `reportNonFatal.ts` is byte-identical; the capture stays the FIRST statement in each catch, before every early return; the `extra` allowlist stays exactly `{provider, code, platform, osVersion, webClientIdSuffix}` for Google and four keys for Apple; the fingerprint stays `["auth-signin", <provider>, <code>]`. Because the retry loop lives inside the `try` and the capture inside the `catch`, exactly ONE `reportNonFatal` fires per user-initiated sign-in no matter how many transport attempts ran — and a transient failure that succeeds on retry fires ZERO, which is correct: it was not a failure. Implementing this invariant necessarily amends the two frozen #1044 suites' expected-Alert-copy values, their `PRE_*_CATCH` differential baselines and their dependency-injection maps; those amendments are marker-gated `[TEST-MOD-APPROVED #1875]` and may change NOTHING about any capture, `extra`, fingerprint or failure-safety assertion.
- **Established:** ACTIVE at #1875 CLOSE 2026-08-11 after independent tester CONDITIONAL PASS (0 P0, 0 P1) with physical-device runtime on a Galaxy A72, and an all-green PR #1884 merge `892a07fbf`. Live-fire highlight: a real Google configuration refusal whose error message was itself a URL reached the user as a fixed i18n string with no URL, code or object in it. Two of four copy states (`STATE 1` offline, `STATE 3` retry-exhausted) are proven against the shipped source and copy file but were unreachable on that handset, whose APK is signed with a certificate not registered against the OAuth client — recorded as `probable`, not claimed as proven.

## ACTIVE — issue #1860 (public tables with row-level security disabled)

> ACTIVE at issue #1860 CLOSE 2026-08-11 — independent tester CONDITIONAL PASS (zero P1s) after three adversarial rounds, all-green merge (PR #1868, squash `3745ea19f`), migration applied to production via the Management-API surgical lane, and verified at RUNTIME: unauthenticated reads that previously returned tens of thousands of rows now return `content-range: */0`. Production RLS-off count 12 → 1, the remaining one being the documented `spatial_ref_sys` exemption. Split out of the #1827 privilege audit, which found twelve tables in `public` running with `relrowsecurity = false` while the schema default grant made row-level security the only constraint that existed.

### I-1860-PUBLIC-TABLES-RLS-ENABLED (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every table in the `public` schema has row-level security ENABLED. The exemption set is exactly one name — `public.spatial_ref_sys`, which the PostGIS extension owns and we do not, and which holds published coordinate-system reference data. Nothing else may be exempt. On the tables this issue fixed, "RLS enabled with zero policies" IS the denial: `anon` and `authenticated` match no row on any command, while `postgres` and `service_role` continue to bypass by design (`rolbypassrls`), which is how every live reader reaches them. `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is deliberately absent on those tables — FORCE subjects the OWNER to RLS, and the owner is the role their SECURITY DEFINER readers run as. Proved at runtime on PostgreSQL 17.10 at #1860 TEST: plain `ENABLE` still serves a `SECURITY DEFINER` reader owned by the table owner; `FORCE` does not.
- **Which half is authoritative, stated because a green CI check is what people actually read:** the two enforcement halves are NOT equals. The strict-grep gate is the **EARLY** half — static, no database, runs on every PR, tells you in seconds that a migration forgot an `ENABLE`. It works by **parsing text**, so its accuracy is bounded by how well it models PostgreSQL's literal and dynamic-DDL grammar, and that grammar is larger than any regex sweep of it. It has known blind spots (below) and should be assumed to acquire more. The SQL suite is the **AUTHORITATIVE** half: it reads `pg_class.relrowsecurity` on the schema the chain actually produced, so it is immune to every parsing limitation by construction — it does not parse anything. Whatever a `DO` block, an `EXECUTE`, an `E'…'` or a string concatenation did, the catalog records the result. **A green static gate is the weaker statement of the two and must never be read as the stronger one.**
- **Known limits of the static half, written down rather than chased:** (1) a DDL statement assembled by concatenation — `EXECUTE 'CREATE TABLE public.' || quote_ident(v) || ' (…)'` — produces no complete match in any single fragment, so it yields neither an event nor an "unresolvable" and C7 stays silent; the fail-closed rule covers the `%I` placeholder form and the fully-opaque `EXECUTE v_sql` form, not this middle case. Today's chain has three such statements and all three build `CREATE TRIGGER`/`CREATE POLICY`, so no table is currently hidden by it — a fact, not a defence. (2) More of the same class should be assumed to exist. "Prose read as DDL" has been found three times on this ground — in the predecessor audit, then as F-1, then as G-1/G-2 — and each fix was correct while the next corner of the grammar was still there. The right response to the next one is to add it to the gate and rely on the catalog test, not to conclude the static half was ever the guarantee.
- **What this invariant does NOT claim, stated so nobody is reassured by it:** it guarantees RLS is **PRESENT**, not that RLS **CONSTRAINS**. A table with RLS enabled and a permissive `USING (true)` policy reads exactly like an open table to `anon` while `pg_class.relrowsecurity` still reports true — demonstrated at runtime at #1860 TEST. Neither enforcement half models policy CONTENTS for the schema at large, and deliberately should not: plenty of tables legitimately carry public-read policies, and deciding which are legitimate is separate work. **A green gate here is not a proof of access control.** The twelve tables this issue fixed are additionally asserted to carry ZERO policies, but that assertion covers only those twelve. This paragraph exists because the `used_trial_phones` comment that read "No RLS = service-role only access" was the same kind of reassuring falsehood, and this migration was right to correct it.
- **Why it is an invariant and not a convention:** convention already failed here. The predecessor audit (`scripts/audit/rls-coverage.mjs`) had a nine-name allowlist, an unbounded `_archive_` prefix skip, AND `CREATE`/`DROP` patterns that matched only the double-quoted dump style, so every table created since the baseline was invisible to it. It was green because it barely looked. It has been **retired and deleted** at #1860 rather than narrowed: two audits of unequal strength claiming the same ground is the condition that produced this issue. `scripts/audit/rls-allowlist.json` survives it as the one reviewed exemption list.
- **Enforcement:** Migration `20270321001860_issue_1860_enable_rls_on_unprotected_public_tables.sql` turns RLS on and drops nothing. Two independent halves keep it that way, and neither is sufficient alone. **Static, every PR:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-1860-public-tables-rls-enabled.mjs` (manifest `batch:A`, self-test + plain) replays the chain in filename order as ORDERED EVENTS — a `DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` or a drop-then-recreate clears the enabled state, so a later event always wins. Its parsing rules are the load-bearing part, and each is a defect it has already had: comments are never DDL; string literals are never DDL **including inside `DO` bodies**, in all three spellings — `'…'`, dollar-quoted `$tag$…$tag$`, and `E'…'`, which honours backslash escapes and, until it was handled, could mis-end and let a top-level `COMMENT ON TABLE … IS E'…'` hide a live table with no `DO` block involved; dynamic DDL is read ONLY from the executed statement, which is the **first adjacent-literal run** after `EXECUTE` and nothing after it, because `format()` arguments and `USING` parameters are DATA and reading them as DDL let a `%L` argument spelling an enable report an unprotected table as protected; placeholders resolve against the enclosing `FOREACH … ARRAY[…]` loop; only `DO` blocks count as executed, never a `CREATE FUNCTION` body; and unresolvable dynamic `CREATE`/`ENABLE`/`DISABLE` **fails closed** (C7) while an unresolvable dynamic `DROP` does not, because the first direction hides a table and the second only risks a false red. It further pins the exemption file to exactly `spatial_ref_sys` by equality (C2 — the file is never consulted when deciding violations, so it can fail but never excuse), refuses an exemption for a table this repo creates (C3), and fails if the live half is un-wired (C5), if the retired audit returns (C6), or if the tester-owned adversarial suite is deleted or un-wired (C8). C5 and C8 read COMMENT-STRIPPED yaml. **Live catalog, containerised Postgres:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_1860_public_rls_coverage.test.sql`, registered by explicit filename in `.github/workflows/supabase-migrations-and-stripe-deno.yml`.
- **Regression:** The gate's `--self-test` is 47/47 and includes the case that matters — a table created with RLS off makes the gate FAIL — plus one fixture per laundering style: a `RAISE NOTICE`, a variable assignment, a `RAISE EXCEPTION` and a dollar-quoted literal inside a `DO` block each failing to fake an enable; a drop sentence inside a `DO`-body string failing to hide a live table; a `FOREACH`-created table being visible; unresolvable dynamic DDL failing closed in the unsafe direction and not in the safe one; a later `DISABLE` re-opening a table; and comment-only workflow wiring failing C5 and C8. G-1 and G-2 each carry a fixture per laundering style: a `%L` argument spelling an enable, a `%L` argument spelling a drop, a `USING` parameter spelling an enable, and — the necessary other half — a genuine template still resolving when data arguments follow it; an `E'…'` `COMMENT` body at top level failing to hide a table, an `E'…'` inside a `DO` body failing to fake an enable, and a `U&'…'` literal still masked, so the escape-string fix is not over-applied. Three of the 47 are anchored to the REAL chain (T-32/T-33/T-42): the chain must be clean, removing the #1860 migration must make it fail, and the chain must actually contain the `E'`-string and multi-run-`EXECUTE` shapes the G-1/G-2 fixtures guard — otherwise those fixtures would be defending dead code. Two of the 47 are anchored to the REAL chain (T-32/T-33): the chain must be clean, and removing the #1860 migration must make it fail — added because the #1860 tester proved a fixture-only suite stays green when the real fix is deleted. The independent tester suite `scripts/issue-1860/issue-1860-public-tables-rls.tester.adversarial.test.mjs` (10/10, run by `.github/workflows/issue-1860-rls-coverage-tests.yml`, kept alive by C8) attacks the same claims from the real chain. The SQL suite carries its own falsifiability proof: T-1860-05 BECOMES `anon`, reads a planted row and requires zero, then DISABLEs RLS inside a savepoint and requires the row back. A catalog assertion proves a switch is flipped; only that probe proves anything is refused.
- **Scope:** Backend only — table privilege posture, CI, and the invariant. No client code path changes on any surface.
- **Explicitly NOT in scope:** dropping the dead tables. Nine of the twelve are abandoned archive/backup remnants and an absent table cannot regress, but a drop is destructive, irreversible, and the operator's call. Enabling RLS is non-destructive and trivially reversible, which is why it is the first move. Also not in scope: policing policy contents (see the second bullet), and the schema-wide grant design, which remains #1827.
- **Established:** DRAFT at issue #1860 IMPLEMENT 2026-08-11; rewritten at #1860 REWORK 2026-08-11 after the tester's FAIL (F-1 `DO`-body masking, F-2 dynamic creates, F-3 `DISABLE`, F-4 prefix-skip spelling, F-5 scope wording); parser closed at #1860 RETEST REWORK 2026-08-11 (G-1 `EXECUTE` arguments are data, G-2 `E'…'` escape strings) with G-3 recorded above as a known limit rather than chased.

## ACTIVE — issue #1856 (dangerous public-schema table grants)

> Activated at issue #1856 CLOSE after independent tester PASS, an all-green merge, production migration application, and live catalog verification.

### I-1856-PUBLIC-TABLE-GRANTS-FAIL-CLOSED (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** `PUBLIC`, `anon`, and `authenticated` may never regain a table privilege that exceeds the relation's intentional client contract. In particular, neither `anon` nor `authenticated` may hold `TRUNCATE`, `REFERENCES`, `TRIGGER`, or PostgreSQL 17 `MAINTAIN` on `qr_spots`, `menu_modifier_groups`, `menu_modifiers`, or `venue_ordering_settings`; the thirteen repaired public views remain read-only; and any write grant on an auto-updatable owner view that is not `security_invoker` is an un-baselineable RLS-bypass finding. `venue_ordering_settings` is authenticated-readable but service-role-writable under ordering ruling OQ-7.
- **Why the catalog is authoritative:** `information_schema.role_table_grants` is filtered through the current role, does not model the effective `PUBLIC` inheritance boundary cleanly, and does not cover PostgreSQL 17 `MAINTAIN`. The guard therefore reads `pg_class.relacl` through `aclexplode()` and tests effective privileges separately. A frozen baseline records the pre-existing grant backlog but is not an allowlist: new findings and all `rls_bypass_view_write` findings are never excused by it.
- **Enforcement:** Migration `20270322001856_issue_1856_ordering_table_grants_and_grant_class_guard.sql` narrows the four ordering-table grants, removes writes from the thirteen read views, and installs service-role-only `public.audit_overbroad_table_grants()`. The migration self-check hard-fails a target regression or owner-view bypass and surfaces any newly overbroad grant. `.github/workflows/supabase-migrations-and-stripe-deno.yml` executes both the implementor and independent tester SQL suites against PostgreSQL 17.
- **Regression:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_1856_ordering_table_grants_and_grant_class.test.sql` proves target privileges, required product access, class detection, baseline behavior, and a real TRUNCATE revert. Independent `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_1856_grant_guard.tester_adversarial.test.sql` mutates live ACLs, proves the exact TRUNCATE regression fails with the offender named, behaviorally inserts through an owner view over deny-all RLS, proves the `security_invoker` twin is refused with `42501`, and verifies the audit function is executable only by `service_role`.
- **Scope:** Backend ACLs, catalog audit, migration assertions, and CI only. The broader pre-existing public-schema grant backlog remains explicit follow-up debt; this invariant prevents growth but does not silently revoke unreviewed product access. Conditional PostGIS-owned `geometry_columns` and `geography_columns` exceptions survive only while their owner is not manageable by the migration role.
- **Established:** DRAFT at issue #1856 IMPLEMENT 2026-08-11; ACTIVE at CLOSE 2026-08-11 after independent tester PASS, all-green PR #1864 merge `056ae4030`, production migration `20270322001856`, and four live read-backs proving one migration stamp plus zero target-grant, repaired-view, new-finding, or RLS-bypass failures.

## ACTIVE — issue #1817 (Free-plan offering invitation send completion)

### I-OFFERING-PROVIDER-ACCEPTANCE-1 (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** A canonical OneSignal Create Message ID is durable Sent/provider-accepted truth, never device-delivery truth. Free-plan offering invitations settle from `sending` to `sent` on that acceptance without Event Streams; an earlier or later terminal callback may refine the lifecycle, but may never erase provider acceptance.
- **Enforcement:** The #1817 accepted-result recorder, callback reducer, and push adapter contract preserve exact claim/attempt/provider identity, project recipient and group status through the existing database owner, and reject non-canonical or ambiguous provider responses.
- **Regression:** The #1817 SQL transaction matrix, Deno adapter matrix, and batch-A strict guard pin callback-before/result, callback-after/result, replay, conflict, partial-failure, no-receipt, ACL/RLS, and fail-on-revert behavior.
- **Established:** ACTIVE at #1817 CLOSE after independent QA PASS, all-green PR #1825 merge `3feb629e6`, production migration `20270314001817`, exact-source Edge Function v11 deployment, and a controlled OneSignal live-fire proving 2 accepted/Sent, 0 Delivered, 1 honest no-subscription failure, 0 callback rows, and no second provider send on replay.

## ACTIVE — issue #1770 (Brand People and offering guest foundation)

### I-PROPOSED-BRAND-PERSON-1 (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** One brand-scoped person may accumulate many source records and contact methods without silently joining ambiguous identities; deterministic evidence links, ambiguous evidence creates a conflict, and every merge remains attributable and reversible when its partition is still provable.

### I-PROPOSED-OFFERING-INVITE-1 (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Offering invitations use opaque one-time material whose raw value is never stored; the database stores only a peppered HMAC, validation is event-bound and evidence-bound, and preview performs zero provider I/O.

### I-PROPOSED-OFFERING-PUSH-RETRY-1 (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** An offering push send group owns one immutable, token-free v1 push payload. Initial delivery, exact replay, and every homogeneous retry dispatch only the independently rehashed object returned by the database claim; caller content, current templates, inbox rows, and hashes without source bytes can never reconstruct or replace it.
- **Enforcement:** `marketing_send_groups.push_payload_v1/push_payload_hash`, the immutable trigger, locked retry copy/revalidation, `biz_claim_offering_push_provider_io`, and the `offering_invitation`-only persisted seam in `notifyV2`.

### I-PROPOSED-PERSON-SUPPRESSION-1 (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** A person suppressed for marketing or all messaging remains suppressed across every linked source and contact method; a new order, RSVP, ticket, merge, or re-ingest can never silently reactivate marketing eligibility.

### I-PROPOSED-SOURCE-FAILOPEN-1 (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Existing RSVP, order, and ticket writes remain authoritative if Brand People ingestion is unavailable; source writes enqueue work, the worker retries with bounded backoff, and only aggregate safe codes leave the boundary.
