## ACTIVE — issue #1815 (canonical current-issue approval-token grammar)

### I-1815-CANONICAL-ISSUE-TOKEN-GRAMMAR (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** The current GitHub-issue citation branch in both append-only override
  tokens is exactly `#[1-9][0-9]*`: one or more decimal digits, first digit 1–9,
  with no leading zero and no suffix. The independent legacy citation branch remains
  exactly `(?:META-)?ORCH-[0-9]{4,}(?:-[A-Z])?` and remains permanently accepted.
  The token wrapper, case, single-space separator, closing bracket, per-file
  whole-range commit attribution, absolute deletion refusal, and status dispatch are
  unchanged. No GitHub existence lookup is performed.
- **Output safety:** Operator-facing current-issue examples use the inert `#ISSUE`
  placeholder. Legacy examples remain visibly inert as `ORCH-NNNN` or
  `META-ORCH-NNNN` (an optional leg suffix may remain visible). Redaction is global
  and covers both current short issue citations and legacy lineage citations.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/test-append-only-check.js`, wired unchanged by
  `.github/workflows/tests-append-only.yml`. The embedded self-test is 92/92: direct
  current modification citations include `#1`, `#27`, `#922`, four digits and five
  digits; direct rename citations include `#1` and `#922`; T52 proves a same-file
  `#922` modification token remains valid beneath a later docs-only tip; T53 proves
  a `#922` rename end to end. Representative legacy scenarios and all prior guard
  behavior remain green.
- **Fails on revert:** Restoring only the current citation branch to its old
  four-or-more-digit minimum turns the new direct short-issue cases and T52/T53 red,
  while the representative legacy cases remain green; restoring the canonical branch
  returns the full 92/92 suite to green.
- **Established:** DRAFT at issue #1815 IMPLEMENT 2026-08-10. Flips ACTIVE only after
  independent tester PASS and CLOSE.

  fail.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #1903 IMPLEMENT. The orchestrator flips this invariant ACTIVE only
  at CLOSE after independent tester PASS, exact compatibility rollout proof, and a verified
  schema-v3 value-blind mutation that leaves Paystack authority false.

## I-1807-PAYOUT-HOLD-LEDGER-APPEND-ONLY-AND-RAIL-TRUTHFUL — ACTIVE

- **Rule:** `public.payout_hold_cutover_migrations` is the append-only audit trail for
  every payout-hold cutover decision. Two properties must always hold. (1) **Append-only,
  enforced not assumed:** `service_role` holds exactly `SELECT, INSERT`; `authenticated`
  holds exactly `SELECT` (load-bearing — the `payout_hold_cutover_migrations_admin_read`
  RLS policy is `FOR SELECT TO authenticated` and an RLS policy still requires the
  underlying table GRANT, so revoking it silently breaks Admin's ledger view); `anon`
  holds nothing. RLS alone is insufficient: `service_role` bypasses RLS. (2) **Rail
  truthful:** no row may name a provider artefact that does not exist for that brand.
  `prior_interval`/`new_interval` are Stripe payout-schedule concepts and MUST be NULL
  when `p_stripe_account_id IS NULL`, on the flip, rollback AND idempotent-skip paths;
  a Paystack stamp failure records `stamp_failed`, never `flip_failed`, which stays
  reachable only from the Stripe lane; and the recorded outcome is the value the RPC
  actually returned, so a concurrency loser is audited as a skip, not a flip.
- **Why it is not merely hygiene:** the ledger is append-only, so a wrong row is
  permanent and uncorrectable. It is the audit of a switch that changes when a real
  business receives its money.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/20270317001807_issue_1807_paystack_cutover_ledger_truth.sql`
  carries in-transaction self-asserts (exactly ONE `result` CHECK — the #1173 constraint
  was created inline and unnamed, so an auto-name mismatch would have made the
  `DROP … IF EXISTS` a silent no-op and left a stale constraint still rejecting
  `stamp_failed`; every prior `result` value retained; `service_role` retains SELECT;
  `authenticated` retains SELECT), so a failed assertion rolls the whole migration back.
  Regression suites, all registered in the `migration-chain` job of
  `.github/workflows/postgres-contract-suites.yml` (they moved there at #2591, which
  deleted the per-issue wrapper this line used to name)
  and run against a clean PostgreSQL 17 database with the full migration chain applied:
  implementor `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_1807_paystack_ledger_truth.test.sql`
  and `supabase/functions/admin-payout-hold-migrate/__tests__/issue_1807_paystack_lane.test.ts`;
  independent tester `…/issue_1807_paystack_ledger_truth.tester_adversarial.test.sql`
  (A1–A9) and `…/issue_1807_paystack_lane.tester_adversarial.test.ts`. The concurrency
  proof uses two genuinely concurrent psql processes driven by the workflow
  (`issue_1807_tester_adversarial_race_{setup,a,b}.sql`) — NOT dblink: `dblink_connect`
  and `dblink_connect_u` are the same C function differing only in `SECURITY DEFINER`,
  it gates on `superuser()`, and `supabase/postgres` de-superusers `postgres`, which
  also owns the extension, so the bypass is inert. Three vacuity guards fail the build
  if fixtures are absent, if the race produced no ledger rows, or if the running user
  cannot actually assume `service_role` (an unprivileged UPDATE under RLS affects zero
  rows silently rather than erroring, so the runtime refusal check would otherwise pass
  without ever attempting the UPDATE).
- **Fails on revert:** restoring `GRANT ALL` fails the catalog assertion, the runtime
  `service_role` UPDATE-refused assertion and tester A6 independently; revoking
  `authenticated`'s SELECT fails with `#1807(e): authenticated lost SELECT — the
  admin_read RLS policy needs the table GRANT`; restoring the hardcoded
  `'daily','manual'` literals fails A1 with `prior=manual, new=manual`; narrowing the
  `result` CHECK fails with `result CHECK rejected the allowed value stamp_failed`;
  deleting the `FOR UPDATE` lock fails with `the race produced 2 flipped ledger rows for
  one brand`. Verified at `809a1ef98`.
- **Adjacent, deliberately NOT fixed here:** the same schema-default widening applies to
  every table in `public` — a migration can write a narrow GRANT that is inert while
  reading as protective in review. Tracked as #1827; #1807 fixed only the table its own
  correctness claim depends on.
- **Established:** ACTIVE at #1807 CLOSE 2026-08-10 — full-chain CI pass (SQL + Deno),
  merged as `5fb06dd77`, migration applied to production via the Management API surgical
  lane and the resulting grant matrix verified in production
  (`authenticated|SELECT`, `service_role|INSERT,SELECT`, `anon` absent, `postgres`
  untouched), `admin-payout-hold-migrate` redeployed as v96 with `verify_jwt = true`.

## DRAFT — issue #1834 (the keyboard covers the field you are typing in when adding a Nigerian bank account)

> Registered DRAFT at issue #1834 SPEC. The orchestrator flips these entries to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS on a physical Android device AND a 375x667 iOS geometry.

### I-PROPOSED-1834-FOCUSED-FIELD-CLEARS-THE-DONE-BAR-NOT-THE-KEYBOARD (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** On every native `mingla-business` surface that renders the app-wide ORCH-1165 Done bar, the acceptance test for keyboard occlusion is clearance of the **Done bar's top edge**, never the OS keyboard's top edge. Clearing the keyboard alone is explicitly NOT a pass: issue #1834 cell Android/R2 cleared the keyboard by 5.7dp and sat 36.3dp under the bar, and cell iOS/R2 cleared the bar by 10pt on an iPhone 17 Pro and failed by 40pt on an iPhone SE3. A cell may not be declared healthy on large-device evidence alone — every cell is verified on a 375x667-class geometry, and any screen with a mode-dependent card height is verified in every mode.
- **The bar's occupied height is DERIVED, never hardcoded (issue #1834 AMENDMENT 1/2, 2026-08-11).** The bar is `KEYBOARD_TOOLBAR_HEIGHT = 42` tall but `react-native-keyboard-controller` mounts it at `offset.opened = opened + OPENED_OFFSET`, where `OPENED_OFFSET = -11` when `KEYBOARD_HAS_ROUNDED_CORNERS` (`Platform.OS === "ios" && parseInt(Platform.Version, 10) >= 26`). So `DONE_BAR_OCCUPIED = KEYBOARD_TOOLBAR_HEIGHT - OPENED_OFFSET` = **53 on iOS 26+, 42 elsewhere**, measured on an iPhone SE3 / iOS 26.5 at `keyboardTop - 53`. **The earlier form of this rule, which fixed `DONE_BAR = 42` and required `fieldBottom <= keyboardTop - 54`, is WITHDRAWN** — on iOS 26+ it budgeted 1pt of clearance while promising 12, which is the defect that failed #1834 at TEST. Any rule, test, or call site that re-types a bar height, or an offset total, instead of deriving it from the library's own constants is a defect by this invariant.
- **The predicate:** a focused input passes only when `fieldBottom <= keyboardTop - (DONE_BAR_OCCUPIED + INPUT_CHROME_BELOW_TEXT_FRAME + MIN_VISIBLE_CLEARANCE)`, with `MIN_VISIBLE_CLEARANCE = 12`. `INPUT_CHROME_BELOW_TEXT_FRAME` exists because `KeyboardAwareScrollView.maybeScroll` aligns the focused `TextInput`'s **inner text frame** (`absoluteY + height` from `useReanimatedFocusedInput`), not the `Input` primitive's bordered box; measured on glass at #1834 TEST as **13.5pt on iOS** (target 378 vs border box 391.5) and **3.16dp on Android** (target 440.93 vs border box 444.09). All three terms live in `mingla-business/src/wrappers/SmartScrollView.native.tsx` as separately named exports and sum to `DEFAULT_BOTTOM_OFFSET`.
- **Measurement space (issue #1834 AMENDMENT 3):** every figure is **screen space**. On Android `measureInWindow` is window-relative while `keyboardDidShow`'s `endCoordinates.screenY` is screen-relative; the app window starts 30.58dp below the screen origin on the reference Samsung SM-A725F, so comparing the two directly overstates clearance by 30.58dp and can report a comfortable pass on an occluded field. Proven three ways (`dumpsys window`, `uiautomator dump`, pixel scan). iOS has no such offset.
- **Enforcement:** `mingla-business/src/components/brand/__tests__/issue_1834_bank_field_smartscroll.render.test.tsx` (mounted-tree proof that the scroll host resolves to the wrapper, that its resolved `bottomOffset === DEFAULT_BOTTOM_OFFSET`, that it equals the three-term sum, and that a real visible gap survives both costs — **no numeric literal is pinned**) + `mingla-business/src/wrappers/__tests__/orch_1165_keyboard_toolbar_clearance.test.ts` (executes the wrapper module and holds the `>= KEYBOARD_TOOLBAR_HEIGHT` floor) + `issue_1834_paystack_host_completeness.adversarial.tester.test.ts` TA-2 (the measured criterion table, which fails if success is redefined as clearing the keyboard). All carry vacuity guards that FAIL on an empty scan rather than skip. **A mounted-tree unit test cannot see device geometry** — it enforces the wiring and the arithmetic; the runtime clearance itself is device-verified, on a 375x667-class geometry and a physical Android, in every mode.
- **Established:** DRAFT at issue #1834 SPEC 2026-08-11; amended at issue #1834 REWORK 2026-08-11 (AMENDMENT 1-3) before any ACTIVE flip.

### I-PROPOSED-KEYBOARD-TOOLBAR-CLEARANCE — AMENDMENT (DRAFT, issue #1834)
- **Amendment:** the ACTIVE rule names "Paystack bank-picker" among the bespoke-keyboard-padding surfaces that must add >=42dp keyed clearance. That listing is **withdrawn**. A 42dp Done-bar compensator is required ONLY in a native window that actually renders `<KeyboardToolbarRoot/>` — which, by the gate's own rule (A) in `.github/scripts/strict-grep/i-1047-biz-keyboard-toolbar-keyed-offset.mjs`, is exactly `app/_layout.tsx`, `src/components/ui/SheetMobile.tsx` and `src/components/ui/Modal.tsx`. The bank picker in `BrandPaystackOnboardView.tsx` is a raw `react-native` `<Modal>` — a separate native window that renders no toolbar — so its Android-only `bankListKbPad` compensates for a bar that is not present and is dead space (Constitution rule 8, subtract before adding).
- **Generalised rule:** compensating padding for the Done bar is forbidden in any native window that does not render the bar.
- **Enforcement:** `issue_1834_paystack_host_completeness.adversarial.tester.test.ts` TA-3 — the set of files carrying an Android-keyed 42 compensator inside a toolbar-less raw `<Modal>` must equal the declared set exactly; an empty scan FAILS.
- **Known remaining member of that set:** `mingla-business/src/components/partner/PartnerPaystackOnboardForm.tsx` (L133 / L386-387 / L527) carries the identical dead compensator. Out of scope for #1834 by orchestrator scoping; TA-3 pins it as a declared, visible exception rather than letting it pass silently.
- **Established:** DRAFT amendment at issue #1834 SPEC 2026-08-11.

## DRAFT — issue #1863 (an under-privileged team member was shown the whole payments surface)

> Registered DRAFT at issue #1863 IMPLEMENT. The orchestrator flips DRAFT → ACTIVE at CLOSE after independent tester PASS and an all-green merge. The issue was filed as "an error toast covers the bank-account field"; the investigation disproved all three halves of that framing (no Nigerian brand, no Stripe fault, no Mingla toast — the overlay was React Native's `__DEV__`-only LogBox) and found a client-side permission hole underneath it.

### I-PROPOSED-1863-CLIENT-PAYMENTS-PERMISSION-PARITY (DRAFT)

- **Rule, clause A — parity.** Any client surface that renders a brand payments control, or fires a request the server guards with `biz_can_manage_payments_for_brand`, must first evaluate the client mirror of that predicate: `canManageBrandPayments` in `mingla-business/src/utils/brandPaymentsPermission.ts`. The mirror is `role ∈ {brand_owner, brand_admin, finance_manager} AND accepted`. **It is a role-set MEMBERSHIP test and must never be written as a rank threshold** — `event_manager` (rank 40) outranks `finance_manager` (rank 30) and is denied, so no single `rank >= N` reproduces the table: `>= 30` wrongly admits `event_manager`, `>= 50` wrongly denies `finance_manager`, and both are wrong on a money surface. `BRAND_PAYMENTS_MANAGER_ROLES` must stay value-identical to `BRAND_PAYMENTS_ROLES` in `supabase/functions/_shared/stripeEdgeAuth.ts`. Adding a `MANAGE_PAYMENTS` entry to `src/utils/permissionGates.ts` — the obvious answer, which looks right and passes a casual review — is forbidden and gated.
- **Rule, clause B — terminality.** A permission denial is terminal. It is never retried by any React Query default or override, never classified as a transport failure, and never surfaced with copy that advises checking a connection. Detection is `isPermissionDeniedError` in `mingla-business/src/utils/edgeFunctionErrors.ts`; that is the ONLY place the shape of a denial is defined. The retry policy is a GLOBAL default, not a per-hook override: two per-hook overrides is exactly the shape that left `brand-stripe-balances` bleeding 606 denials while its twin `brand-stripe-refresh-status` was known and understood, and a global default also covers the third hook nobody has written yet.
- **Rule, clause C — direction of the mirror.** The client mirrors the server. The server is never relaxed to match the client. If they disagree, the client is wrong.
- **Which half is authoritative, stated so nobody is reassured by a green gate:** the SERVER is, always. The client gate is a UX and cost layer — it stops a wall of unanswerable requests and stops offering controls that cannot work. It is **NOT access control**, and a green gate here proves nothing about access. The 403 at `requirePaymentsManager` is what actually protects the money surface, and it must never be weakened to reduce the client's error rate. The server behaved correctly through all ~2,650 denials this issue is about.
- **Denied means visible-with-explanation: zero controls, zero money data, zero requests.** Not hidden (a redirect bounces a user who deliberately tapped Payments and breaks `router.canGoBack()` across three entry points) and not read-only — the server returns NO data to these roles, so a read-only surface would render `—` balance tiles and empty payout lists, which is fabricated emptiness on a money surface (Constitution rule 3), not a UX compromise.
- **Enforcement:** a required-field compile error on `BrandStripeStatusAuthGateInput.canManagePayments` (omission is a `tsc` error, not a runtime regression); `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-1863-payments-permission-gate.mjs` (manifest `batch:A`, self-test + plain, 13 true mutations) which additionally fails if either regression suite is deleted or un-wired; and the two suites below, deliberately different in mechanism so they cannot fail to run for the same reason.
- **Regression:** `mingla-business/src/components/brand/__tests__/issue_1863_payments_permission_gate.render.test.tsx` (RTL mount of the three REAL ROUTE components — mounting the views instead would go green with all three routes unwrapped — asserting per role on the mounted tree, on BOTH rails, that a denied role sees only the explanation card and that `supabase.functions.invoke` is called ZERO times through real queryFns and a real QueryClient) and `mingla-business/src/config/__tests__/issue_1863_permission_denied_terminal.tester_adversarial.test.ts` (default node config, so it runs on every PR: executes the SHIPPED retry policy, counts real `queryFn` invocations at 1 vs 3, drives BOTH services' real error paths, and asserts no rank threshold reproduces the role table).
- **The vacuity trap this invariant names in advance:** with the route gate in place a denied role never mounts `BrandOnboardView`, so a test that "proves" the `permission-denied` ViewState by rendering a denied role asserts nothing and passes forever. The ViewState's test MUST construct the client-ALLOW/server-403 case, which is genuinely reachable through the 30-second role-cache staleness window (`useCurrentBrandRole.ts` `STALE_TIME_MS`) after a mid-session demotion.
- **Scope:** `mingla-business` client only. Zero migrations, zero edge-function changes, zero edge deploys.
- **Explicitly NOT in scope:** the missing rail gate on `useBrandStripeStatus` (a Paystack-only NG brand still polls a Stripe endpoint every 30s); the `src/lib/search/registry.ts` `minRank: 30` payments entries, which are wrong against the server predicate and cannot be fixed by changing the number because 30 and 50 are both wrong; brand-state-derived payments CTAs; the `deleted_at` asymmetry on the server predicate's `finance_manager` branch (issue #1872); and the `appreview@usemingla.com` membership rank, which is a production database write and Seth's call.
- **Established:** DRAFT at issue #1863 IMPLEMENT 2026-08-11.

## ACTIVE — issue #1876 (business web asset routing and terminal chunk recovery; ratified 2026-08-12)

> Registered DRAFT at issue #1876 SPEC and activated after independent tester PASS, PR #1933 merge `bd38a0ee6`, Vercel READY, and production routing plus real-browser verification on 2026-08-12.

### I-PROPOSED-1876-BUILD-OUTPUT-NEVER-HTML (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Every directory in the `mingla-business` web build output that holds machine-fetched artefacts — currently `/_expo/static/` and `/assets/` — MUST be excluded from the `vercel.json` catch-all rewrite, so a missing or evicted file returns a real `404` and never a `200 text/html` SPA shell. The exclusion is a bare alternation inside `/((?!…).*)`; the `^`-anchored form is FORBIDDEN (the `^` is inert inside the compiled `^(?:/(…))$`, where the group is evaluated at index 1 and `^` can never match, so the catch-all silently resumes swallowing assets while looking correct), and the named-parameter form `/:path((?!…).*)` is FORBIDDEN (Vercel's compiler appends the unconsumed param, turning `"/"` into `"/?path=$1"`). The catch-all stays the LAST entry in `rewrites` and its destination stays `"/"`. **Adding a new build-output directory to the web export REQUIRES adding it to this alternation in the same PR.**
- **Relationship to `I-1485-STATIC-ASSET-NEVER-HTML`:** this rule **extends** it and does not replace it. #1485's rule remains the authority on `/_expo/static/`'s 404 behaviour, on the LAST-entry ordering requirement, and on the two forbidden forms; `_expo/static/` remains the FIRST alternate. This rule generalises the requirement to the rest of the build output.
- **Enforcement:** `ci-batch:issue-1485-web-missing-chunk-404-tests` (explicit `paths:` registry, never a glob), which now also runs the two #1876 suites. `mingla-business/scripts/ci/issue-922-business-web-actionable.mjs` independently hard-pins the same shipped string from the #922 gate, so a drift reds two workflows rather than one.
- **Regression test:** `mingla-business/__tests__/issue1876_assets_excluded_from_catch_all.test.ts` — compiles the catch-all FROM the shipped config (never from a local constant, so a revert cannot leave it green), proves every `/assets/**` shape the Expo export emits is excluded under all three plausible path-to-regexp wrappers, proves the exclusion is anchored at the first segment so `/assetsish`, `/venue/assets/create` and `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` still reach the shell, proves `/_expo/static/**` is unregressed, proves the nine SC-5 deep links still match, pins the `headers` block byte-identical, and proves BEHAVIOURALLY (not by string comparison) that the `^`-anchored form would reopen the defect.
- **Evidence:** pre-fix production returned `200 text/html` for missing `/assets/**`. After PR #1933 deployed, production probes on 2026-08-12 returned `404 text/plain` with `x-vercel-error: NOT_FOUND` for missing PNG and JavaScript assets; missing `/_expo/static/**` remained 404, three real hashed Expo bundles remained `200 application/javascript`, and protected deep links remained `200 text/html`.
- **Established:** DRAFT 2026-08-11 at issue #1876 SPEC; activated after independent tester PASS and production verification of PR #1933 merge `bd38a0ee6` on 2026-08-12.

### I-PROPOSED-1876-RECOVERY-HAS-TERMINAL-UI (ACTIVE)
- **Rule:** Business web's chunk-recovery path MUST terminate in a user-visible state, never a blank page. When the shared 10,000 ms cooldown suppresses a reload — or when blocked `sessionStorage` means no reload is ever attempted — and `#root` is STILL empty 1500 ms later, the injected `<head>` script MUST render `#mingla-boot-error` into `document.body` with a Reload control that calls `window.location.reload()` on the current URL. **Visible** means the card has non-zero visible area inside the viewport, is topmost and hit-testable at its centre, and its real Reload button is visible and tappable. The card is valid only while `#root` stays empty: any late successful mount MUST remove it promptly, stop its observer/poll resources, and leave the app DOM, URL, navigation history, and reload count untouched. It MUST NOT render into `#root` (React owns that node and must be able to mount over it untouched). Idempotence is bounded to at most one concurrent card and one pending timer, not a document-lifetime one-shot; the pending state resets whether its timer paints or finds a recovered app, and a survivable failure MUST leave terminal recovery available for a later genuine blank state. Exact-byte Jest evidence and real-browser layout evidence are both mandatory, and dirty uncommitted bytes are never activation evidence. **A `console.warn` or a DOM node outside the viewport is not a user-visible state.**
- **Why it is load-bearing:** the cooldown is the only no-loop guarantee and cannot be relaxed, so the suppression branch is a permanent dead end by construction. #1485 deferred it to "the ErrorBoundary's recoverable fallback", which is correct for a lazy ROUTE chunk and false for the ENTRY bundle — React never mounts, so no boundary exists. Without this invariant the dead end is a silent white page: Constitution rule 3.
- **Why the 1500 ms / empty-`#root` gate is not optional:** a card thrown over a working app is a WORSE bug than the blank page it replaces. The render decision is deliberately deferred so a slow-but-successful boot is never interrupted, and it is evaluated against live DOM state rather than against the failure that triggered it.
- **Compatibility constraints on the injected script (all CI-enforced):** `${…}` interpolation is limited to `CHUNK_RECOVERY_MARKER` / `CHUNK_RECOVERY_KEY` / `CHUNK_RECOVERY_COOLDOWN_MS`, because the #1485 suites rebuild the shipped bytes with a `new Function` bound to exactly those three names; the emitted body is ES5-only, backtick-free, and carries no navigation primitive other than `window.location.reload()`; and the DOM is reached through guarded `window.document` / `window.setTimeout`, never a bare `document`, because those harnesses execute the bytes against a synthetic window that has neither.
- **Enforcement:** `ci-batch:issue-1485-web-missing-chunk-404-tests`.
- **Regression test:** `mingla-business/__tests__/issue1876_terminal_recovery_ui.test.ts`, `mingla-business/__tests__/issue1876_false_positive_and_reachability.tester.adversarial.test.ts`, and `mingla-business/playwright/issue1876/boot-error-reachability.spec.ts` evaluate the exact shipped bytes and jointly guard the known-defect visibility-oracle vacuity, late-mount removal, supported polling fallback, pending-latch reset, generic rewrite-shadowing protection, and real Chromium visibility/tappability. The synthetic suites prove exact copy, blocked-storage recovery, no false card before the 1500 ms boundary, observer and fallback cleanup, later recovery after a survivable failure, no app-DOM or navigation mutation, and generic derivation of every shipped catch-all alternate; the real-browser suite proves a genuine blank boot is in-viewport, topmost, and clickable, proves a late healthy mount removes the card, and proves a pre-guard mount never paints it. Presence-only synthetic DOM evidence cannot satisfy this invariant.
- **Evidence:** the pre-fix deployment had no terminal UI. After PR #1933 deployed, production HTML contained `mingla-boot-error`, `watchBootRoot`, `bootErrorPending`, and `position:fixed`; Chromium at an iPhone 13 viewport proved the deployed card had non-zero in-viewport area, was topmost and tappable, disappeared after a late healthy mount, and never rendered when the app mounted before the guard.
- **Established:** DRAFT 2026-08-11 at issue #1876 SPEC; activated after independent tester PASS and production verification of PR #1933 merge `bd38a0ee6` on 2026-08-12.

## ACTIVE — issue #2594 (the class-A budget is checked, and static gates run no containers)

### I-PROPOSED-2594-CLASS-A-BUDGET-ADJUDICATED (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every conclusion of `Strict grep — static gates (class A)` is adjudicated out-of-band against Amendment 7's A7-SC1(1) bound of 600 seconds, by a check that never returns green for "could not look". A `success` over the bound fails. A lone `cancelled` at the 900-second cap is a timeout kill and fails; a `cancelled` alongside simultaneously-cancelled peers is a concurrency eviction and is neutral; anything unclassified is INCONCLUSIVE and exits non-zero. The adjudicator lives outside the job it measures, because A7-SC4 forbids a wall-clock threshold inside a gate and a timeout kill terminates class A before any step of its own can report.
- **Enforcement:** the `class-a-budget` job in `.github/workflows/strict-grep-mingla-business.yml` (`needs: [static-gates]`, `if: always()`) running `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2594-class-a-budget.mjs --enforce`; its `--self-test` covering all nine decision rows with 16 fixtures, checking row, verdict and exit code independently; and the wiring assertions in `issue-2437-node-wave-shadow-parity.implementor.test.mjs`, whose four mutants red on the job being deleted, `needs` dropped, `if: always()` removed, or the `--enforce` step substituted. Demonstrated failing at a real head on PR #2690: bound lowered to 60s produced `D3 FAIL … the measured job reported success but took 532s`, restored to 600s produced `D4 PASS … 79s of headroom`. This is a reporting check, not a required status context.

### I-PROPOSED-2594-STATIC-GATES-IS-CONTAINERLESS (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** The `static-gates` job runs no container and provisions no database. It declares no `services:`, invokes no `docker`, and installs no Supabase CLI. Database-backed contract proofs belong in `postgres-contract-suites.yml`, which owns the sole `supabase/postgres` service container and replays every migration from zero unconditionally.
- **Enforcement:** the SC-11 assertion in `issue-2437-node-wave-shadow-parity.implementor.test.mjs`, scanning every `static-gates` step for container and CLI verbs with each forbidden literal assembled from fragments so the guard cannot match its own source; plus `STATIC_CLASS_A_STEP_SHA256`, deliberately re-cut at #2594 from the 9-step `d89bf992…` to the 7-step `982cd176…`, so any step returning to that job moves the seal and must be declared. Mutants proven: restoring the replay step reds both the container scan and the seal; restoring the CLI action reds; adding a job-level service container reds.

- **Rule:** Tab settlement instruments never count and their children count once. Sales exclude tips, tax, and platform fees; when a partial refund cannot be allocated, the affected currency's money is withheld while exact refund and demand truth remains visible.
- **Enforcement:** the RPC's eligible-child spine and currency-withholding CTEs plus the issue #1795 implementor and tester PostgreSQL suites. Activated with the same #1795 independent PASS and production verification.

### I-PROPOSED-1795-MEASURED-COVERS-NO-INFERENCE (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Tier-A cover spend is distinct-reservation grain across every linked eligible session, with stored party size counted once. Claimed party size, proximity, buyer/contact matching, and cross-currency denominator reuse are forbidden.
- **Enforcement:** the RPC's reservation-currency aggregation and issue #1795 PostgreSQL fixtures. Activated with the same #1795 independent PASS and production verification.

## DRAFT — issue #2117 (public offering reads consistently respect offering visibility)

### I-PROPOSED-2117-ONE-OFFERING-VISIBILITY-GATE (DRAFT)

- **Scope — read this before flipping ACTIVE.** This invariant governs **the #2117 change set and every read path added or modified after it**. It is deliberately **not** a claim about the whole schema and must not be reworded into one.
- **Rule:** Within that scope, every read path that serves an unauthenticated or unauthorised caller and returns offering-derived data expresses the offering's public readability through the Offering Visibility Gate, never through a locally written predicate. Any **new or modified** such reader that writes the visibility rule locally is a violation. The rule the gate owns is **visibility and soft-delete only** — status is deliberately not folded in, because the readers do not share a status set and one per-audience status set cannot preserve both. Deliberate exceptions exist only in the four recorded forms E-1/E-2/E-3/E-4 and are recorded at the site.
- **Why the scope is qualified — measured, not asserted.** After this change the applied schema still contains **18 anon-executable `SECURITY DEFINER` objects that write a local visibility predicate** (comment-stripped derivation over the fully-migrated cluster; an independent test measured 19 — the difference is a matching edge case and does not change the conclusion). **Zero of them are in the #2117 change set**, and all four change-set readers express visibility **only** through the gate. Those objects *do* consult visibility, so the gap this issue exists to close is closed for them — but "exactly one expression of the rule exists in the schema" is **not true**, and an invariant flipped ACTIVE while false is worse than no invariant at all. They are recorded here as **known-conforming-but-local**: correct today, outside this issue's scope, and the natural population for a follow-up consolidation should one be opened.
- **Enforcement:** the #2117 migration's two gate forms and their adoption at every Class A and Class B site, plus the executable PostgreSQL suite (SC-1, SC-2, A-SC-4, SC-5, SC-6, A-SC-13), each criterion proven to red on its named revert mutation and green on the correct implementation against a real applied schema. A-SC-4 holds the public payload by two-directional `EXCEPT ALL` against the §4.5 siblings — the pre-change bodies verbatim, an in-cluster oracle — plus key-completeness, so a strip of the payload reds instead of satisfying a served/not-served boolean.

### I-PROPOSED-2117-GATE-CANNOT-DENY-ON-PRIVILEGE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** No gate used on a public read path may depend on the caller holding a privilege, and none may branch on the caller's role. A role-introspecting gate raises outside a `SET ROLE` session (the role GUC is literally `none`) and is the next outage rather than a defence against one.
- **Enforcement:** SC-1 and SC-2 execute both gate forms from a role stripped of every privilege on the offering relation, in the same run that proves a direct table read raises. A-SC-3 asserts the *property* — no changed object's result varies with the caller's role, measured across two distinct roles with the caller's identity claim held constant — rather than banning named mechanisms, because the named-mechanism form was independently forged twice during review and both forgeries pass a mechanism ban while leaking.
- **The comparison must be over the VALUE, never a summary of it.** A-SC-3 compares **full payload digests cell for cell**. An earlier form compared row *cardinality* for the set-returning readers and *null-ness* for the JSON readers; both are lossy projections, and a reader that quotes an anonymous buyer one price and a signed-in buyer another returns the same row count and the same not-null-ness to both — so that form greened on the exact forgery this invariant exists to kill. This is the same defect class the issue fought at the criterion level (assert over membership, not magnitude) reappearing one level in, inside the criterion that was itself the fix for a previous instance of it.

### I-PROPOSED-2117-VISIBILITY-NEVER-GATES-A-DECISION-INPUT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** No object whose result is consumed as an authorisation identity, a guard boolean or a capacity count may carry a **visibility gate**, and none may have its `EXECUTE` narrowed where any consumer is caller-evaluated. Both directions are outages and both are measured. Such an object is routed by the A-4.9 remedy ladder — visibility gate, `EXECUTE`-narrowing, authorisation arm, full exclusion — and the rung is chosen **per object by execution, never by kind**: two objects of the same kind take different rungs, and on one of them the rung correct for its twin is worse than the visibility gate. An object left at full exclusion carries a measured, recorded residual and a linked follow-up issue.
- **Enforcement:** A-SC-11 exercises every enumerated consumer, read path *and* write path with affected-row-count comparison, with an authorised caller at every visibility state; A-SC-12 demonstrates the empty value is observed as absence rather than a changed decision; A-SC-14 executes every change-set object as an unauthenticated caller and as a signed-in stranger and compares the result against the recorded residual in both directions, so the bottom rung cannot become a way to do nothing quietly.

## DRAFT — issue #2150 (a guest can mint duplicate free tickets by resubmitting)

### I-PROPOSED-2150-FREE-COMPLETED-SESSION-IDEMPOTENT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A COMPLETED **zero-total** ticket checkout session is never tombstoned. `biz_ticket_checkout_create_session` returns it verbatim — same `checkoutSessionId`, same `orderId`, status `free_completed` — and `ticket-checkout-create` answers with that same order's already-issued tickets without re-finalizing, without re-dispatching the confirmation and without re-firing the ad conversion. However many times a guest submits an identical free reservation, they hold exactly one order, one pass, one confirmation email and one SMS.
- **Scope, stated so it cannot be widened by accident.** The exemption is conjoined with `total_cents = 0` and applies to nothing else. `paid_completed`, `failed` and `expired` keep the ORCH-0791 tombstone verbatim, and the ORCH-0829-B D-1 past-expiry tombstone for abandoned non-terminal sessions is unchanged. **A session that took money must remain re-creatable** — that is what the tombstone exists for, and #2150 does not touch it. The exemption additionally requires `order_id IS NOT NULL`, `revoked_at IS NULL`, a buyer identity that matches (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`), and a surviving ticket in `('valid','used','transferred')`, so a cancelled, refunded or revoked reservation falls through to the pre-existing behaviour and the guest can reserve again rather than being handed a dead pass.
- **Why option 1 and not option 2.** The idempotency key already survives completion; `biz_ticket_checkout_create_session` is what destroys it. "Do not tombstone" and "make the key survive" are the same change, and making it here leaves `checkoutIdempotencyKey` derived purely from the cart — so #2160's day-aware `lineKey` composes with no further work.
- **Enforcement:** the executed PostgreSQL 17 suite `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2150_free_resubmit_idempotent.test.sql` (H-01..H-07 — four submits counted against real `orders`, `tickets` and per-channel `ticket_order_notifications` rows; H-03/H-04/H-05 prove the failed, completed-paid and past-expiry tombstones still fire), TA-13 of `issue_2136_free_checkout_no_value_arm.tester.adversarial.test.sql` asserting the same contract from the other side, the Edge suite `supabase/functions/ticket-checkout-create/__tests__/issue_2150_free_resubmit_idempotent.test.ts`, and the strict-grep gate `issue-2150-free-completed-session-returned-not-tombstoned.mjs`, which asserts the exemption, its `total_cents = 0` scope guard AND the surviving ORCH-0791 tombstone in the same migration so the two can never be traded off. All lanes run from `.github/workflows/issue-2150-free-resubmit-idempotent-tests.yml`, whose path filters cover every migration that has ever re-emitted the wrapper.
### I-PROPOSED-2150-ANON-FREE-REPLAY-REQUIRES-POSSESSION (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Being handed a completed free reservation — its order id, its checkout session id, or any QR payload — requires **proof of possession**, never proof of knowledge. A session bound to a `buyer_user_id` requires that authenticated identity; an **anonymous** session requires the `buyer_status_token` itself to be presented, compared as SHA-256 against `ticket_checkout_sessions.buyer_status_token_hash` by `public.issue_2150_free_replay_disclosure_authorized`. The idempotency key is derived from `(eventId, buyerEmail, buyerPhoneE164, lines, paymentPlanChoice)`, every part of which someone who merely knows the guest can type into the form, so the key alone is never sufficient.
- **Why this is not a nice-to-have.** Without it the fix would be a **regression in kind, not degree**. Before #2150 an attacker who knew a guest's email and phone minted their *own* second ticket and the guest's pass still worked. Handing that attacker the *guest's* pass lets them attend on it; `biz_ticket_scan` sets `status='used'`, and the real guest is then refused at the door as a `duplicate`. That is a denial of admission which did not previously exist, and it would have shipped in service of a feature whose primary use case is anonymous free reservations.
- **Refusing disclosure must never fall back to minting.** The create-session exemption declines to tombstone for **every** caller — that is the duplicate fix and it is not a disclosure. Only the disclosure is gated. A caller who cannot prove possession receives `free_already_reserved` carrying no order id, no session id and no QR; nothing is minted, nothing is destroyed, and the guest's own token is **not** rotated (the replay branch sits above the status-token UPDATE, which would otherwise invalidate the token the guest is about to prove with).
- **The concurrent double tap needs no token and is untouched.** While the first request is in flight the session is `pending_free`, so the pre-existing in-flight arm serves it and finalize dedupes under its own row lock. Only a resubmit *after* completion reaches the possession check.
- **Client obligation.** The web free path persists the buyer status token via the existing ORCH-0789/0790 `checkoutPersistence` helper and presents it on resubmit; before this issue it was never persisted on the free path at all, so no legitimate resubmit could have proven possession. Native surfaces do not present one and are therefore refused disclosure — safely, with no duplicate.
- **Enforcement:** H-08 (refused without a token; asserts specifically that **no QR payload** is returned, since an order-id-only assertion would pass while the pass still leaked), H-09 (the guest presenting their own token gets 1 order / 1 ticket / 1 email / 1 SMS), H-10 (random, foreign and empty tokens all refused), H-11 (concurrent double tap unaffected) in the executed PostgreSQL suite; REPLAY-01/04/05/06 in the Edge suite, including fail-closed on an authorization RPC error; `issue_2150_free_resubmit_client_guard.test.ts` for the token round-trip and the copy; and §4 of the strict-grep gate, which asserts the disclosure function and its token comparison survive anywhere in the migration chain.

- **Preserves ACTIVE `I-PROPOSED-AW CHECKOUT-SESSION-NEVER-REUSED-POST-TERMINAL` (ORCH-0791)** for every session that carried value, and `I-PROPOSED-2136-FREE-FINALIZE-REACHABLE` unchanged — the free finalize is still what mints the order; #2150 only stops it being asked to mint a second one.

## DRAFT — issue #2160 (a guest can attend MORE THAN ONE day of a multi-day event)

Flip to ACTIVE on CLOSE (orchestrator owns the flip). Every rule below is
enforced by the executed PostgreSQL suites listed at the end, not by review.

### I-PROPOSED-2160-A TICKET-IS-THE-DAY-AUTHORITY (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** The days a pass admits are the rows it has in `public.ticket_event_dates`, and nothing else. No other table, column or jsonb key may express which day a pass is valid for. **ZERO rows means "not day-scoped"** — today's any-occurrence admission window, verbatim — which is what every pass issued before #2160 has and must keep.
- **Why one table and not two representations.** The operator's requirement — "a scan records which day it admitted, and a pass is refused on a day it was not issued for" — is a SINGLE invariant. Two representations (a column for per-day, a ledger for all-days) cannot both be the authority for "which day did this scan admit": the scan ladder would carry three branches and every downstream reader (roster, per-day head count, CSV, confirmation, consumer calendar) would have to consult two places and agree. That is two invariants that can drift, and drift between two authorities for one fact is exactly what produced #2161.
- **No backfill, ever, from `orders.event_date_id`.** Deriving entitlement rows for existing orders would retroactively NARROW the admission window of passes guests already hold — a live regression on QR codes already in wallets. Narrowing is not a no-op; it is a refusal at a door the guest already paid for.

### I-PROPOSED-2160-B ORDER-DAY-ANCHOR-IS-LATEST-ENDING (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** `orders.event_date_id` is the **latest-ENDING** occurrence the order admits, in BOTH pricing modes, and remains the sole payout/refund anchor. Anything that writes it must satisfy `orders.event_date_id = (SELECT id FROM event_dates WHERE id IN (the order's ticket days) ORDER BY end_at DESC LIMIT 1)` whenever the order has any day-bound ticket.
- **Why latest-ending, and why this is not cosmetic.** The payout control plane builds candidates via `resolve_payout_live_occurrence(o.event_id, o.event_date_id, o.created_at)` and will not mature an NG release until `ed.end_at + interval '3 days' <= now()` for that occurrence. Anchoring on the FIRST day would release the organiser's money while day 2 was still unattended and still refundable, **and** would have required editing the live payout candidate query. Anchoring on the last means a two-day order's money matures after the SECOND day ends, and `resolve_payout_live_occurrence`, `attach_payout_release` and the NG release rule are untouched by this issue.

### I-PROPOSED-2160-C CART-CAPACITY-AGGREGATES-PER-TICKET-TYPE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Capacity compares `ticket_types.quantity_total` against the SUM of the submitted quantity for that ticket type across the WHOLE cart, never a single line.
- **Scope, stated honestly rather than inflated.** The pre-#2160 check was per line, and the session's own items are inserted AFTER the validation loop, so a second line of one ticket type was invisible to the first line's check. Under the amendment's session-level day set, lines are never expanded, so multi-day does NOT create that shape — the hole is real but **latent**, exactly as it is today. This is hardening, not the load-bearing fix an earlier spec draft described. It is kept because any future feature that sends two lines of one type (bundles, add-ons) walks straight into it, and the failure mode is an oversell.
- **The row lock is not replaced by it.** The aggregation fixes the same-cart case; `SELECT … FROM ticket_types … FOR UPDATE` is what serialises CONCURRENT sessions. Both are required.

### I-PROPOSED-2160-D OCCURRENCES-TRAVEL-WITH-THE-EVENT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A guest-facing surface obtains occurrences from the **same SECURITY DEFINER reader that served the event** (`pg_direct_event_checkout_bundle` → `PublicEventDetail.occurrences`). No guest-surface client may read `public.event_dates` directly.
- **Why widening an RLS policy is the WRONG fix and is forbidden.** Widening the anon `event_dates` policy to admit hidden events would leak the existence AND the schedule of every unlisted offering to enumeration. The defect is two access paths for one page, not a policy that is too narrow.
- **Recorded so it is not rediscovered:** the same RPC-vs-table split exists on the TRIP surface (`loadTripSidecars`). It is LATENT rather than live only because `pg_public_trip_by_slug` is `'listing'`-gated and therefore NARROWER than the RLS policy — an unlisted trip is not served at all, so the page fails whole rather than half. Widen that reader to `'direct'` and #2161 appears there immediately. It carries an explicit `issue-2160-strict-grep-allow TRIP-SIDECAR-LATENT-NOT-LIVE` marker so the exception is greppable rather than silently absent.

### I-PROPOSED-2160-E DAY-BOUND-PASS-ADMITS-ONLY-ITS-DAY (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A pass with at least one `ticket_event_dates` row scans `success` **only** inside one of THOSE occurrences' grace windows, at most once per day, and the admitting occurrence is recorded on `scan_events.event_date_id`. A pass with zero rows keeps the any-occurrence policy and the one-shot `status='used'` lifecycle verbatim.
- **ONE ENFORCEMENT SITE.** `biz_ticket_scan` and nowhere else. This must not acquire a second home.
- **Dedupe is by the LEDGER, not by status.** `tickets.status='used'` changes meaning from "has been scanned" to **"fully consumed"**: an `all_days` pass admitting 2 of its 3 days is still `valid`. `status` therefore cannot answer "already admitted today?", and a `scan_events` success row for `(ticket_id, event_date_id)` is what does — backed by the partial unique index `scan_events_ticket_day_success_once`.
- **Two readers of the status distinction were ENUMERATED, not assumed.** `biz_guest_roster_project` counts check-ins as `status='used' OR used_at IS NOT NULL` and `used_at` is set on the FIRST admission, so a partly-admitted multi-day guest counts as checked in **with that function completely unmodified**. Capacity counts `status IN ('valid','used','transferred')` — both states are inside the set, so the timing of the flip cannot move it. **If any NEW reader of `status='used'` is written, it must be re-checked against this rule.**
- **The write is legal because of a short-circuit that was verified, not assumed.** `biz_tickets_enforce_update` forbids a scanner-role caller from touching `used_at` outside a strict `valid → used` transition, which would have made this design illegal. Its FIRST statement is `IF auth.uid() IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW`, and `biz_ticket_scan` is SECURITY DEFINER invoked under the service key, so the guard short-circuits. **The trigger is relied upon UNCHANGED and must not be modified.**
- **Residual hazard, named:** the legacy RLS policy "Scanners can update tickets for check-in" still permits a client to flip `status` directly, bypassing the ledger, which would produce a pass marked used with no day recorded. Nothing uses it today (every live scan goes edge fn → RPC; `useScanStore` is local-only with no backend sync). It must stay unused; narrowing it is its own issue.

### I-PROPOSED-2160-F PRICING-MODE-IS-LOCKED-ONCE-A-PASS-EXISTS (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** `events.multi_date_pricing_mode` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'per_day'`, constrained to `('per_day','all_days')`, and cannot change once the event holds a ticket in `('valid','used','transferred')` — enforced by the trigger `events_multi_date_pricing_mode_locked`, which raises `multi_date_pricing_mode_locked`. A trigger rather than an RPC-level check because it is fail-closed against **every** write path.
- **The default is the guarantee, and it is exact rather than approximate.** On today's build a guest can select AT MOST ONE day, and with one day chosen the two modes are arithmetically identical (`qty × 1` either way). So for every selection any guest can make on today's build, on every existing event, in either mode, **the price and the pass count are unchanged**. `'per_day'` is additionally the only default that could not silently reprice: `'all_days'` would give a second day away on inventory organisers already published, across every multi-date event at once.
- **A date added AFTER a sale is not retroactively added to passes already sold.** This falls out of the model (entitlements are written at mint time) but must be stated, because "one price for all days" invites the opposite reading.

**Preserves, unchanged and re-verified through this change:** ACTIVE `I-PROPOSED-AW CHECKOUT-SESSION-NEVER-REUSED-POST-TERMINAL` and both #2150 invariants (the wrapper re-emit carries the exemption, its `total_cents = 0` scope guard and the ORCH-0791 tombstone forward verbatim); `I-PROPOSED-2117-ONE-OFFERING-VISIBILITY-GATE` (the bundle now genuinely routes through `pg_offering_visibility_gate(…, 'direct')` — see the implementation report: the SPEC asserted it already did, and it did not); `I-1860` (both new tables carry RLS); ORCH-1138 experience checkout byte-identity (`CartContext.eventDateId` and the top-level `eventDateId` body field were ADDED ALONGSIDE, never renamed); and Constitution #9 (`ticketsRemaining` stays `null` — per-day capacity remains inexpressible in BOTH modes and is explicitly out of scope).

**Enforcement:** the executed PostgreSQL 17 suites `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2160_multiday_admission.test.sql` (46 checks; H-01/H-02 prove a guest selecting two days of a three-day event is admitted on BOTH and NEITHER other, in BOTH modes; H-03 proves a zero-row legacy pass is byte-for-behaviour unchanged; H-05 proves the one-day arithmetic identity across modes; H-06 the lock; H-07 the stale non-anchor day) and `issue_2160_unlisted_occurrences.test.sql` (U-1..U-6, against the REAL reader with an UNLISTED event — a stubbed transport cannot satisfy it, which is exactly why #2161 escaped #2135's suite); the Deno suites `issue_2160_multiday_idempotency_key.test.ts` and `issue_2162_confirmation_names_chosen_day.test.ts`; the strict-grep gates `issue-2160-day-bound-scan.mjs`, `issue-2160-capacity-aggregated.mjs` and `issue-2160-occurrences-not-read-directly.mjs`; and the #2135 single-date byte-identity suite, which stays green through the change. All lanes run from `.github/workflows/issue-2160-multiday-multiselect-tests.yml`.

### I-PROPOSED-2162-CONFIRMATION-NAMES-THE-CHOSEN-DAY (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** The confirmation email, SMS and PDF name the day(s) the guest actually chose. Resolution order: the days this order's tickets admit (`ticket_event_dates`, collapsing to earliest-start/latest-end for a multi-day reservation) → `orders.event_date_id` → the master occurrence. A NULL at the last step is **legitimate** (single-date, or an order predating day selection), not an error, and the output is then byte-identical to today's.
- **The test must assert the negative.** A test asserting only "a date is present" passes on the broken implementation. Every check asserts BOTH that the chosen day IS carried and that the master day is NOT, and a source pin asserts the PRECEDENCE (`chosenDate ?? masterDate`) — `masterDate ?? chosenDate` would compile, satisfy every "a date is present" assertion, and re-ship the defect verbatim.

## DRAFT — Issue #2218 (Nigerian confirmation texts recorded `sent` and never delivered, 2026-08-18)

### I-PROPOSED-2218-A NG-GENERIC-SENDS-DEFER-INSIDE-THE-OPERATOR-EMBARGO (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** While Termii's `generic` channel is the Nigerian route, `smsAdapter.send()` MUST NOT perform provider HTTP for a destination that resolves NG between **20:00 and 08:00 Africa/Lagos**. It returns `status:"deferred"`, `provider:"termii"`, `providerMessageId:null` and `retryAfter` = the next 08:00 WAT, with **zero** HTTP, **zero** `beforeProviderIo`, and **zero** naira spent. The window lives in exactly one file (`supabase/functions/_shared/ngSmsEmbargo.ts`) and both rails read it from there.
- **Why:** Termii's own documentation — "Promotional messages sent through the generic route are subject to time restrictions in Nigeria, telecom operators do not allow delivery between 8:00 PM and 8:00 AM" (https://developers.termii.com/campaign). Every NG send rides `generic` because `dnd` returns 400 "Country Inactive" on this account (#1518, pending provider activation in #1480). Inside the window Termii still ACCEPTS the request and returns an id, so the send path recorded `sent` for a message the network never carried. The #1518 header comment named this cost — what was not intended is that it was invisible.
- **ORDER IS PART OF THE RULE.** The per-market kill switch is evaluated FIRST: a dark Nigeria must still report `provider_kill_switch_off`, not a hold that implies we will try again. The embargo check sits between the kill switch and `beforeProviderIo`.
- **A DEFERRAL IS NOT A DROP.** `ticket_order_notifications.status='deferred'` with `next_attempt_at`, `attempt_count` UNCHANGED, and `notification-retry-sweeper` honouring that instant INSTEAD of the ORCH-0788 ladder (2^attempt × 60s, three attempts — at most ~6 minutes, which a twelve-hour embargo would exhaust before dawn). The buyer's text arrives late, not never; the sibling confirmation EMAIL is unaffected and still immediate.
- **Marketing is unchanged and must stay so.** `marketing-send` has enforced NG quiet hours of 08:00–20:00 WAT since META-ORCH-1161 — the exact complement — so this guard cannot fire on that rail. The arm exists there anyway rather than falling through to `failed`.
- **REVERT CONDITION:** when #1480 activates the `dnd` route, NG transactional stops passing `generic` and this guard stops applying to it on its own. No code here needs removing, and the marketing-side protection must not be removed with it.

### I-PROPOSED-2218-B AN-SMS-MAY-NOT-REST-AT-`sent` (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** An SMS row that claims `status='sent'` with `delivered_at IS NULL` for longer than 45 minutes MUST be RESOLVED — to `delivered` with a real `delivered_at`, to `failed_terminal` **only when the provider itself reported a failure**, or otherwise to an explicitly NAMED `delivery_unverified:<reason>` — and the batch MUST surface to a human (ops email via `dispatchNotification`, the same path payout-release-sweep alarms on). `sms-delivery-reconcile` (cron `*/15`) owns this.
- **Why:** of the seven SMS rows in `notification_deliveries`, ONE carried a `delivered_at`. A Nigerian send from 2026-08-04 with an ordinary numeric Termii id sat at `sent`/NULL/NULL indefinitely. As a database state, accepted-and-dropped and delivered were the same thing, which is why a founder had to notice.
- **Positive confirmation is ASKED FOR, not waited for.** Termii reports delivery by webhook only, and `termii-delivery-status` was invoked ZERO times over the observation window while `twilio-message-status` was invoked repeatedly — the Nigerian delivery report is not arriving at all. A webhook that is misconfigured produces silence indistinguishable from success, so the sweep queries Termii History (`GET /api/sms/inbox?api_key=…&message_id=…`). **`"Message Sent"` is NOT a delivery** — it means "handed on, no report yet", which is precisely the state being distrusted; classifying it as delivered would rebuild the defect inside its own fix.
- **THE FIX FOR A SYSTEM THAT GUESSED `sent` IS NOT A SYSTEM THAT GUESSES `failed`.** `failed_terminal` may be written from ONE place, gated on a provider status that names a failure. An absence of evidence is `delivery_unverified:<reason>` — the reason is recorded, `status` is left at `sent` (which is exactly and only what is true: a provider accepted it and nobody can say what became of it), and the row is still distinguishable from a delivered one, which carries a `delivered_at` and no error. This was NOT the first design; the 08:02 WAT live-fire forced it. Every Nigerian row currently carries an unreconcilable id, so a "no evidence ⇒ failed" rule would stamp every Nigerian confirmation a failure the moment the texts started arriving again.
- **Two unverified reasons, kept distinct.** `provider_message_id_unreconcilable:<provider>` = the provider handed us an identifier its own APIs do not accept (an INTEGRATION fault, an engineer's problem). `delivery_unconfirmed:<provider>` = we asked properly and got no answer (a DELIVERABILITY fault, operations' problem). Collapsing them puts this signal back in the dark.
- **A failed lookup is not a verdict.** Any transport/auth problem yields `pending`, never a delivery decision. Silence waits for the deadline.
- **Judged once.** The recorded reason IS the "already judged" marker: both scans filter on it being NULL. Without that, an unverifiable row is re-alerted every fifteen minutes until the alarm is noise and nobody reads it — which is how this became invisible in the first place.

### I-PROPOSED-2218-C BOTH-SMS-WEBHOOKS-RECONCILE-BOTH-LEDGERS (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** `termii-delivery-status` MUST update `ticket_order_notifications` as well as `notification_deliveries`, keyed on `provider_message_id` + `channel='sms'` and PROVIDER-BLIND, exactly as `twilio-message-status` does. A non-delivered report MUST NOT null a `delivered_at` that is already set.
- **Why:** it only ever wrote the shared ledger. So the American rail stamped a buyer's own confirmation row `delivered` two seconds after the send (observed in production, 2026-08-18 05:15:23Z) and the Nigerian rail structurally could not, whatever Termii reported. A support agent looking up a Nigerian buyer saw `sent` forever.

### I-PROPOSED-2218-D A-HELD-SEND-IS-NOT-AN-ATTEMPT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** `deferred` joins `skipped` and `suppressed` in `DELIVERY_NON_ATTEMPT_STATUSES`. No provider I/O happened, so it must not increment a health tile's `total`.
- **Why:** this is #1537 P2-4's founding bug one status later. Six kill-switch skips made the termii tile read HEALTHY while nothing had been delivered; a Nigerian night of held messages would do the same. `unknown` is the truthful verdict when nothing was attempted.

**Enforcement:** the Deno suites `supabase/functions/_shared/ngSmsEmbargo.issue2218.test.ts`, `_shared/adapters/smsAdapter.issue2218.test.ts`, `notification-retry-sweeper/issue2218.deferred.test.ts`, `termii-delivery-status/issue2218.ticket_ledger_parity.test.ts`, `sms-delivery-reconcile/issue2218.reconcile.test.ts` and `ticket-confirmation-dispatch/__tests__/issue2218_deferred_contract.test.ts`, all registered in the `notification-deno-tests` job of `.github/workflows/supabase-migrations-and-stripe-deno.yml`; plus the pre-existing `issue-1541-sms-provider-sole-send-path.mjs` and `i-proposed-1227-ng-sms-via-termii.mjs` gates, which stay green through the change.

**Preserves, unchanged and re-verified:** ORCH-1227 / `I-PROPOSED-1227-NG-SMS-VIA-TERMII` (NG still routes to Termii; nothing here moves NG to Twilio, at ~290x the cost, and the US rail is untouched at 03:00 WAT); #1518's `generic`-only NG channel (this changes WHEN we send, never WHERE); #1529's destination-number routing authority; #1537's provider attribution on every return path, extended to the hold; and #1541's "branch on `status`, never on `ok`" rule, which is what keeps all eight call sites correct as the vocabulary widens.
### I-PROPOSED-2217-A CLAIM-BY-POSSESSION-NEVER-BY-KNOWLEDGE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A paid guest order is handed to an account only when **two independent possession proofs** hold. (1) The order is ARMED — `orders.attendance_identity_claim_armed_at` is set, written ONLY by `arm_order_identity_attendance_claim`, reachable ONLY from `attendance-claim-link`, which already refuses to act without the checkout session's `buyer_status_token` (the same secret #2150 chose as THE possession proof for an anonymous reservation). (2) The claimant's identifier is one the account itself has proven, read server-side from `auth.identities` for the JWT's user id. Knowing an email or phone is worth nothing: to present one you must first receive a code at it.
- **THE SECURITY PROPERTY IS AN ABSENCE.** `claim_attendance_by_verified_identity(p_user_id uuid)` takes NO identifier argument and `attendance-claim-identity` parses no request body. A guessed identifier has nowhere to enter. A signature that gained `p_email` would satisfy every "the right buyer gets their ticket" assertion and re-ship the defect, so the edge suite asserts the parameter list by COUNT.
- **`email_confirmed_at` / `phone_confirmed_at` ARE BANNED FROM THIS PREDICATE, and the reason is measured, not stylistic.** Against production on 2026-08-18: `email_confirmed_at` is set for **125 of 125** users and `phone_confirmed_at` for **125 of 125 — including 64 users who have no phone at all**. On this project those columns carry no information. The PostgreSQL suite's I-02 gives the attacker `auth.users.email = <the buyer's address>` WITH `email_confirmed_at` set — the shape every production user already has — and asserts they are handed nothing; substituting that column for the `auth.identities` predicate makes I-02 hand them the ticket. Measured, not asserted.
- **`auth.identities` is used because only GoTrue writes it.** `provider='email'` ⇒ Supabase email OTP mailed a code and the holder returned it. `provider='phone'` ⇒ a phone OTP, or `verify-otp`'s `auth.admin.updateUserById` which runs only after Twilio Verify approved. `google`/`apple` ⇒ the IdP asserted the mailbox via `identity_data.email_verified`. None of these are reachable through PostgREST.
- **Normalization has exactly one home.** GoTrue stores phones bare (61 of 61 production rows, #1529); `orders.buyer_phone_e164` keeps the `+`. The restoration happens once, inside `verified_account_identifiers`. Deleting it makes I-03/I-07 fail.
- **The existing guest path is not gated.** Arming is best-effort inside `attendance-claim-link` and never withholds the link; the confirmation button renders and reaches the right store in every claim phase including `terminal` and `rate`. A guest who never installs the app is unaffected.

### I-PROPOSED-2217-B EVENT-CHAT-TRACKS-THE-TICKET-IN-BOTH-DIRECTIONS (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Claiming an order adds the buyer to the event conversation through the SAME helper the paid finalize path uses (`add_buyer_to_event_chat` — never a second writer), and losing the ticket removes them. Enforced by `drop_unentitled_buyer_from_event_chat` behind triggers on `orders` (payment_status) and `tickets` (status/approval_status).
- **Removal was MISSING for every buyer, not only claimed ones.** Chat visibility is a plain `conversation_participants` row ("Users can view conversations they participate in"); nothing removed it, so a refunded buyer kept the room forever. This fixes the class.
- **The triggers fire in the LOSING direction only.** Firing on `'pending' → 'paid'` would race the ticket inserts: an order already `paid` while its tickets are still being written reads as unentitled and the sweep would delete a row finalize is about to rely on. There is no symmetric hazard, because nothing about losing entitlement is written before the loss is real. A scan (`valid → used`) is not a loss and is excluded by the WHEN clause — I-09 asserts it.
- **Never evicts someone in the room for another reason.** The conversation's creator and an active `brand_team_members` row are both exempt. I-12 gives the teammate a real ticket and revokes it, so only the staff exemption can save them.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2217_identity_attendance_claim.test.sql` (I-01..I-13, executed on PostgreSQL 17 with the full chain), `supabase/functions/attendance-claim-identity/__tests__/issue_2217_identity_claim_contract.test.ts` (12), `mingla-business/src/services/__tests__/issue_2217_confirmation_app_cta.test.ts` (18). All lanes run from `.github/workflows/issue-2217-confirmation-app-cta-tests.yml`.

### I-PROPOSED-2269-A A-VERIFIED-PHONE-IS-A-LEDGER-ROW-NEVER-A-PROFILE-COLUMN (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** The phone arm of `verified_account_identifiers` reads exactly two sources, UNIONed: the GoTrue `provider='phone'` identity (#2217, unchanged) and `public.verified_phone_identities`, a service-role-only ledger written ONLY by `record_verified_phone`, called ONLY from `verify-otp` after Twilio Verify returns `approved`. The email arm is untouched.
- **`profiles.phone` IS BANNED FROM THIS PREDICATE, and the reason is measured.** On production 2026-08-18 the role `authenticated` holds a **column-level UPDATE grant on `profiles.phone`**, the RLS policy is `USING (auth.uid() = id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = id)`, and no trigger guards the column. **Any signed-in user can set their own `profiles.phone` to a stranger's number.** Reading it would turn #2217's possession proof into knowledge. The PostgreSQL suite's P-03 gives `typist` — a Google-only account — `profiles.phone = <the buyer's number>` and asserts they are handed nothing; adding a `profiles.phone` arm makes P-03a fail with *"profiles.phone leaked as a verified identifier"*. Measured, not asserted.
- **#2269's premise as filed was WRONG, and the correction is the finding.** The issue reads `i.provider = 'phone'` as "signed in with a phone" and concludes 63 Google + 37 Apple accounts are excluded. They are not. `verify-otp` calls `auth.admin.updateUserById(user, { phone })`, and GoTrue mints a `provider='phone'` identity ALONGSIDE the social one — created **20-40 seconds after** it (median 29s; `last_sign_in_at` == `created_at`), i.e. the onboarding Twilio step, not a sign-in method. Measured: of 62 accounts holding a phone, **62 already have the phone identity** and **61 of those signed in with Google or Apple**. `verified_account_identifiers` returned a phone for 62 of 62 phone holders before this change. There was no excluded population of 63.
- **THE DEFECT THAT IS REAL: a swallowed write, not a narrow predicate.** `verify-otp` writes `profiles.phone` as its must-succeed source of truth and syncs GoTrue **best-effort inside a `try/catch` that only warns**. `auth.users` carries `users_phone_key UNIQUE (phone)`. When a stale account still holds the number the sync THROWS, is SWALLOWED, and the phone identity is never minted — so a number Twilio really did approve becomes invisible to the claim. Measured: **2 accounts, 3 armed-able guest orders.** `485addca` (Google-only) was blocked by `b17e3e15`, a business account from April that still holds `2348162646567` in `auth.users`; verify-otp's duplicate guard reads `profiles` only, where that account's phone is already NULL, so the guard passed and the conflict surfaced only in the swallowed sync. `87207cdb` (Apple-only) came through the ORCH-0977 reviewer bypass, which writes `profiles` and never GoTrue.
- **The ledger exists so the proof does not depend on a write that can refuse.** It carries no UNIQUE constraint shared with GoTrue. `PRIMARY KEY (user_id)` gives one live number per account so claims cannot accumulate; `UNIQUE (phone_e164)` plus the writer's `DELETE ... WHERE user_id <> p_user_id` gives one live owner per number, so a recycled number stops entitling the previous account. Both layers are proven: removing the DELETE is refused by the unique index itself.
- **It is not client-writable, at three locks.** No grants to `anon`/`authenticated`, RLS `ENABLE`d **and** `FORCE`d, and zero policies — so even a future grant leaves it unreadable and unwritable from a user JWT. `record_verified_phone` is `REVOKE`d from `PUBLIC, anon, authenticated`. P-11 asserts all four on the catalog.
- **The ledger write is FATAL where the GoTrue sync is not.** A swallowed write is the bug this issue fixes; allowing the replacement to warn-and-continue would move the same defect one table across. `verify-otp` returns 500 if `record_verified_phone` does not return `recorded`. The GoTrue sync stays non-fatal — the proof no longer rides on it — but is now logged at `console.error`, not `console.warn`.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2269_verified_phone_possession.test.sql` (P-01..P-11, executed on PostgreSQL 17 against the full chain, and run TWICE in the lane to prove it is re-runnable against a non-virgin database) and `supabase/functions/verify-otp/__tests__/issue_2269_verified_phone_contract.test.ts` (8). Both run from `.github/workflows/issue-2269-verified-phone-claim-tests.yml`, which also re-runs the #2217 and #871 SQL and Deno suites.
- **Keeps #2217's revert RED.** Substituting the confirmed-at columns for the identity lookup still makes #2217's I-02 hand the attacker the ticket — verified on a fresh database after this change. `phone_confirmed_at` remains meaningless here: set on **all 128** accounts including the **66 with no phone at all**.

### I-PROPOSED-2217-C ONE-DEVICE-AWARE-CONFIRMATION-BUTTON (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** The confirmation screen carries ONE app button, and its destination is resolved from the BROWSER (`detectClientPlatform`, the reviewed ORCH-1319 UA/platform/maxTouchPoints trio) through `resolveConfirmationAppTarget`, never from `Platform.OS`.
- **Why `Platform.OS` is banned here specifically.** This card renders on buyer-web through react-native-web, where `Platform.OS` is `'web'` for an iPhone and an Android alike. The pre-#2217 `Platform.OS === 'ios' | 'android'` branches were therefore DEAD on the only surface that shows the card, and the second badge offered an iPhone the Play Store.
- **The fall-through destination was a dead link, measured.** The `'web'` arm resolved to `https://usemingla.com/orders/{orderId}/chat`, which **returns HTTP 404** — there is no `orders` route in `mingla-marketing/app` and no rewrite to one. The ORCH-1342 suite asserted that string's PRESENCE; that assertion was updated under `[TEST-MOD-APPROVED #2217]`.
- **Verified on real engines, not in jsdom:** the compiled module resolved `ios` → `https://apps.apple.com/app/id6760440898` in Safari/WebKit on a booted iOS 26.5 simulator, and `android` → `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mingla.app.v2` in Chrome 124/Blink on a booted Android emulator.

### I-2240-EMAIL-APP-LINK-SOLE-OWNER (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** The "Open in Mingla" destination in every transactional email — URL *and* CTA markup — lives ONLY in `supabase/functions/_shared/email/appLink.ts`. No email template may carry an app-destination literal or render its own button, in either the HTML or the plain-text body, and no file in the repository may build a `usemingla.com/orders/...` URL.
- **What it replaced.** Three templates each hand-wrote `https://usemingla.com/orders/{id}/chat` twice — **six literals for one destination** — and that destination has never existed: no `orders` route in `mingla-marketing/app`, no rewrite or redirect to one. Measured 2026-08-18, `GET https://usemingla.com/orders/<order-uuid>/chat` → **HTTP 404**. Every ticket, experience and trip confirmation email ever sent carried a dead button. #2217 fixed the same literal on the confirmation *page*; copies do not know about each other, so three survived.
- **The destination is device-aware at ARRIVAL, not in the message.** Email cannot run JavaScript and cannot read a User-Agent, so `usemingla.com/download` (the ORCH-1319 smart-download route, a Next.js server component reading the request UA header) does the deciding. Measured 2026-08-18: iPhone UA → 307 → `apps.apple.com/app/id6760440898`; Android UA → 307 → `play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mingla.app.v2`; desktop → 200. Byte-identical to what the #2217 page button resolves to, because it is the same three destinations.
- **It is `resolveConfirmationAppTarget(e, 'other')`.** `'other'` is precisely the platform an email knows: none. The gate does not merely byte-compare a constant — it reads `GUEST_FUNNEL_ONELINK_URL` and requires whichever arm that resolver would take (`null` → `DOWNLOAD_PAGE_URL`; set → on the OneLink base). **At AppsFlyer go-live the flip makes CI red until the email follows the page**, which is what keeps one-destination-one-owner true across two runtimes that cannot import each other.
- **The test asks whether the URL RESOLVES, not whether a string is present.** #2240 exists because an assertion pinned the dead URL's *presence* as "the universal-link fallback behaviour is unchanged". `issue_2240_email_app_link.test.ts` instead extracts the URL from rendered template output and resolves it against a route table built from the real routing layers (`mingla-marketing/app/**`, `next.config.ts` redirects, `middleware.ts`, `vercel.json`), and proves that resolver falsifiable by requiring the dead path to come back UNRESOLVED from the same code path. Any layer it cannot model is a loud failure, never a silent pass.
- **Enforcement:** strict-grep `i-2240-email-app-link-sole-owner.mjs` (16/16 self-test cases, `batch:A`); `supabase/functions/_shared/email/__tests__/issue_2240_email_app_link.test.ts` (7 offline + 2 live-network). Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2240-email-app-link-tests.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven for each claim.
- **Established:** #2240, 2026-08-18.

### I-2272-DECLARED-APP-LINKS-ARE-SERVED (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every path family the live iOS AASA (`mingla-marketing/public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`) claims MUST be served on the apex host — `/orders/*`, `/chat/*`, `/board/*`, `/invite/*`, `/s/*`, `/p/*`. A declared deep link that 404s in a browser is a defect, whatever the app does with it. The four landings own no device decision and no store URL: `/download` is the single owner, and every string they render is a closed union of literals so no buyer input can reach the page.
- **What it replaced, measured.** `GET https://usemingla.com/orders/{id}/chat` → **HTTP 404**, on iPhone, Android and desktop User-Agents alike (2026-08-18), and the same for `/orders`, `/chat/*`, `/board/*`, `/invite/*`. Twelve of twelve probes dead. #2240 removed the last emitter of that URL, but every confirmation email already delivered still carries one and none can be recalled; #2219 fixed only the phone that HAS the app (it now lands on home instead of a dead screen). The browser population is the larger one, because ticket buyers mostly buy on the web.
- **`/board/{id}` is NOT `/b/{brandSlug}`, and there is deliberately no redirect.** `app-mobile/src/services/boardInviteService.ts` mints `mingla://board/{invite_code}` from `collaboration_sessions.invite_code`, and `deepLinkService.ts` parses `board` as `board-invite`. `app/b/[slug].tsx` is a brand page. A redirect would hand a collaboration invite code to a brand lookup that can never match.
- **Nothing in `.well-known` moved.** Adding or withdrawing a deep-link claim is #2245, a founder decision, and both files are cached by the OS and by Apple's CDN. Both files' SHA-256 are pinned at their pre-#2272 values, so an edit is a red test rather than a silent publish. A phone WITH the app is therefore unaffected: the OS still intercepts, and `+native-intent` still lands these four families on home (#2219).
- **The test asserts the RESPONSE, not a route file.** A file can exist and still not be served — `mingla-marketing/app/careers/**` is a live example in this app, 404'd on the apex by a middleware guard. `web-app-link-landings.served.test.mjs` starts the real `next build` output and reads status codes for 4 families × 2 shapes × 3 real device User-Agents, with `/nothing-serves-this-2272`, the singular/plural neighbours and `/careers` required to 404 on the same server in the same run.
- **One resolver, two issues.** #2240's route-table resolver was extracted verbatim in behaviour to `scripts/apex-route-model/apex-route-resolver.mjs` (plain ESM over `node:fs`, so the same file runs under Deno and `node --test`). Copying it would have re-created the drift it exists to prevent. #2240's falsifiability control moved from the now-served `/orders/{id}/chat` to a genuinely unserved path, and a new #2240 test pins that the #2272 landing is what answers the historical path.
- **Enforcement:** `scripts/issue-2272/web-app-link-landings.model.test.mjs` (9 tests, offline), `scripts/issue-2272/web-app-link-landings.served.test.mjs` (4 tests, real build + real HTTP), `scripts/issue-2272/web-app-link-landings.live.test.mjs` (4 tests, production, `workflow_dispatch` only — it cannot be green before the deploy it checks). Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2272-web-app-link-landings.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven for each claim.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2272, 2026-08-18; flip to ACTIVE after the merged-main deploy and a green dispatch of the live job.

### I-2267-MARKETING-BRAND-ID-CONSTRAINED-ON-UPDATE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** On `public.marketing_templates` and `public.marketing_campaigns`, the `WITH CHECK` of the UPDATE policy must constrain `brand_id` exactly as the INSERT policy does — `brand_id IS NULL OR mkt_brand_min_rank(brand_id,'event_manager')` for templates, `mkt_brand_min_rank(brand_id,'event_manager')` for campaigns, which is NOT NULL. The row an UPDATE produces is held to the same brand rule as the row an INSERT produces.
- **`USING` is out of bounds, in the other direction.** `USING` decides which rows are visible to the UPDATE, and a rank requirement there would lock an operator out of a row they already own the moment their brand membership lapsed — they could not rename or retire their own draft. Both `USING` clauses are pinned UNCHANGED by the same test that pins the `WITH CHECK` tightening, so an over-correction fails as loudly as the gap did.
- **What it replaced, measured against the live catalogue.** Verified 2026-08-18 against production `pg_policy`, not against migration files: `marketing_templates_update` was `is_starter_pack = false AND account_id = auth.uid()` on both sides — no mention of `brand_id` at all — while its INSERT sibling carried the brand clause; `marketing_campaigns_update` carried `account_id = auth.uid() OR mkt_brand_min_rank(...)`, whose first disjunct a row's own author satisfies irrespective of the resulting `brand_id`.
