Both matched `20260602000003_orch_0815_marketing_hub_phase_a.sql` exactly, so there was no drift to blame. `pg_trigger` carries ZERO user triggers on either table, so nothing downstream pinned the column either. `marketingTemplateService.updateUserTemplate` accepts a `brand_id` patch (`marketingTemplateService.ts:181-182`), so the column is a live part of the UPDATE payload.
- **`mkt_brand_min_rank` must stay caller-context.** It is deliberately NOT `SECURITY DEFINER` (per `feedback_rls_returning_owner_gap.md`), which is what makes it correct inside a `WITH CHECK`: it evaluates as the caller and returns false rather than raising when there is no membership. A `SECURITY DEFINER` rewrite would make every clause above evaluate as the definer and pass silently, so both the migration and the test assert `prosecdef` is false.
- **The test EXECUTES the UPDATE as a non-owner role.** RLS does not apply to the table owner, so a case that seeds and asserts as the migration superuser proves nothing about a policy — the gap that let ORCH-1116's RLS false-positive ship green. Every case runs under `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` with a `request.jwt.claims` / `request.jwt.claim.sub` subject, and each positive case (author edits their own row; a brand `event_manager` edits a colleague's campaign) is asserted alongside the negative so an over-tightening cannot read as a pass.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2267_marketing_brand_tenancy_update.happy.pg17.test.sql` (G-00 catalogue + 6 behavioural cases across both tables, run against the full migration chain on `supabase/postgres:17.4.1.075`). Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2267-marketing-tenancy.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven behaviourally on both tables, not only at the catalogue level.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2267, 2026-08-18; flip to ACTIVE once the migration is applied to production and the policies are re-read from the live catalogue.

### I-2267-COMPOSER-LINK-HREF-ESCAPED-AND-SCHEME-CHECKED (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** In `mingla-business/src/services/marketing/tenTapTokenBridge.ts`, a link mark's `href` is escaped at BOTH emitters, and a link mark may only carry an `http:`, `https:` or `mailto:` scheme. The allow-list is applied once, at `tryReadTag` — the boundary where an href first becomes a mark — so no later stage has to re-derive it.
- **The allow-list is `normalizeUrl`, restated.** `ComposerV2Editor.tsx:102-107` already enforces `/^(https?:\/\/|mailto:)/i` (else prepend `https://`) for every link the composer itself creates, so the parser rejects nothing the product can legitimately produce. If `normalizeUrl` ever widens, the parser must widen with it or links start disappearing — which is why the composer file is in this lane's path filter.
- **The two emitters are deliberately NOT symmetric, and that asymmetry is load-bearing.** `toBodyHtml` writes the STORED token string, and its reader `bodyHtmlToTenTapDoc` does no entity decoding at all, so it escapes `"` ONLY — escaping `&` there would add one `amp;` per save and break `I-PROPOSED-MKT-COMPOSER-V2-TOKEN-ROUNDTRIP-LOSSLESS`. `docToHtml` writes the editor's HTML, and its reader `htmlToTokenString` decodes `&amp;`/`&lt;`/`&gt;`/`&quot;`, so it applies full attribute escaping and a query-string `&` emits as `&amp;` and decodes back identically. Both are pinned, including a five-save-cycle case proving the stored string accumulates nothing.
- **A declined tag is dropped, not left as text.** The general "unknown HTML becomes literal text" rule cannot apply to a declined `<a>`, because the matching `</a>` is recognised unconditionally: keeping the opening tag as text while the closing tag is consumed would write an UNCLOSED anchor into `channel_payload.body_html`. The markup goes, the link's words stay — the same rule `htmlToTokenString` already applies to tags it does not preserve.
- **Scope note.** A general HTML sanitiser was considered and rejected: `docToHtml` is already a strict allow-list re-serializer (escaped text, `<strong>`, `<em>`, `<br>`, two chip `<span>` shapes with enum/hex-constrained attributes, `<a>`), so a sanitiser would sit in the wrong place and would risk stripping the chip spans and their `data-*` attributes.
- **Enforcement:** `mingla-business/src/services/marketing/__tests__/issue2267LinkHrefEmission.happy.test.ts`, run alongside the two Stage A round-trip suites in the same lane so an escaping change that breaks byte-identity fails where it was asked for. Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2267-marketing-tenancy.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven separately for the escape and for the allow-list, by line deletion.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2267, 2026-08-18.

### I-2267-COMPOSER-EDITORSTYLE-LITERAL-ONLY (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every property value in every `editorStyle={{ … }}` object under `mingla-business/src` and `mingla-business/app` is a plain quoted string literal or a dotted read from a frozen `as const` design-system token module. No template substitution, call, bare variable, ternary, prop/state read or spread.
- **Why it is a rule rather than a preference.** `react-native-pell-rich-editor` interpolates those values into a `<style>` block in its WebView source raw (`src/editor.js:55-70`). That is upstream's design, it is not fixable from here, and the package is effectively unmaintained — latest release 2025-07-22, the one before it April 2023, 193 open issues (#2267). Today every value is constant, which makes the raw interpolation inert; this gate is what keeps that true. The failure it guards is mundane: someone makes the composer themeable, or reads a size from a prop, and a constant quietly becomes a caller-supplied value in a diff that looks like nothing.
- **Whole-object, not a key list.** A fifth `editorStyle` key added later is covered automatically instead of arriving unguarded, and the gate FAILS if the guarded mount or the prop disappears rather than passing vacuously (#2113 — a check that cannot fail carries no information).
- **Related, same issue:** `react-native-pell-rich-editor` is pinned to exactly `1.10.0` in `mingla-business/package.json` and the lockfile root range, so a future 1.10.x cannot land silently on a package whose open upstream report no advisory database describes (`GET /advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=react-native-pell-rich-editor` returns `[]`). The existing `orch-0864-composer-v2.mjs` C1 check asserts presence, not range, and is unaffected.
- **Enforcement:** strict-grep `i-2267-composer-editorstyle-literal-only.mjs` (12 self-test groups / 22 cases, `batch:A`), also named explicitly in `.github/workflows/issue-2267-marketing-tenancy.yml` so a PR touching only the composer proves it on the change that needs it.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2267, 2026-08-18.

### I-2290-QUEUE-WORKER-HAS-CRON-CALLER (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every edge function that BOTH (a) leases work from a queue by calling an RPC whose name contains `claim`, AND (b) admits only a machine — it compares the inbound Authorization bearer against `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` or `CRON_SECRET`, so no interactive caller can open its door — MUST have a caller somewhere in this repo. A live `cron.schedule(...)` in `supabase/migrations/**` is one. Being invoked by another edge function that itself has a caller is the other. Unless it is on the frozen `HAND_KICKED` list, with a reason.
- **Why both conditions and not "any function that says claim".** `claim` alone is far too loose: `support-claim`, `claim-attendance`, `attendance-claim-identity`, `attendance-claim-link`, `claim-search-pool`, `admin-review-venue-claim` and the `venue-claim-*` family all call claim-named RPCs and are all driven by a human holding a user JWT. Condition (b) separates them — those forward the bearer to `auth.getUser()` and never compare it to a service key. A function that compares the bearer to a service key has declared, in code, that its only possible caller is a machine. If the repo does not also declare WHICH machine, the answer in production is "none".
- **Reachability is a transitive closure, not a cron lookup.** A worker cannot be laundered green by a caller that is itself unreachable. `ticket-confirmation-dispatch` has a machine-only door and is legitimately not dark because the Stripe webhook router and `reconcile-stuck-checkouts` both invoke it by name and both have callers of their own.
- **What it would have caught.** Run against `20270305001770`'s own commit the gate FAILS: `brand-person-ingest-worker` calls `biz_claim_brand_person_ingest`, gates on `Bearer ${serviceKey}` / `Bearer ${cronSecret}`, and no `cron.schedule` anywhere names it. The same run fails #2168's pre-fix tree on `checkout-sale-revocation`. This defect class has now shipped three times (#2168, #2222, #2290); nothing in the type system, no unit test, no `deno check` and no green CI run could see it, because the missing half is a row in `cron.job` rather than a line of code.
- **Two acknowledged blind spots, both pinned rather than hidden.** The model is textual and does not evaluate plpgsql control flow, so (1) a dynamic `cron.unschedule(<expr>)` is counted but not applied — assertion A-5 freezes that count at 5, forcing human review of a 6th — and (2) a `cron.schedule` inside a non-executing branch is credited as live, and 6 migrations already use `PERFORM cron.schedule` inside `DO` blocks — assertion A-4 pins #2290's own schedule to top level. A gate that names and pins its blind spots beats one that pretends it has none.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2290-queue-worker-has-cron-caller.mjs` (`batch:A`, `self-test` + `plain`, registered `selfTest: "wired"`), with `.github/scripts/strict-grep/__tests__/issue-2290-brand-person-ingest-cron.test.mjs` (10 cases, implementor) and `.github/scripts/strict-grep/__tests__/issue-2290-ingest-cron-adversarial.test.mjs` (8 cases, tester — atomicity, replay-idempotency, and both guard blind spots). Confirmed to actually EXECUTE in CI, not merely be registered: `run-batch.mjs --class A` reported `expected 890, executed 890, missing 0` with all three entries `ok`.
- **Fails-on-revert:** reproduced independently by the orchestrator in a throwaway tree — guard exits 0 with the migration present, exits 1 without it, naming `brand-person-ingest-worker — claims via biz_claim_brand_person_ingest; no cron.schedule targets it and no other edge function invokes it`.
- **Established:** ACTIVE at #2290, 2026-08-19. Migration `20270423002290_issue_2290_brand_person_ingest_cron.sql` applied to production `gqnoajqerqhnvulmnyvv` and verified live (jobid 61, `*/5 * * * *`, first tick drained 33/33).
### I-2300-ARTIFACT-REAP-GATE-IS-OWNERSHIP-PROVEN (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** No automation may delete a per-issue worktree, iOS simulator or Android AVD without PROVING the artifact is dead. For a worktree that proof is the conjunction of four facts — issue `CLOSED`, the branch's PR `MERGED`, `git status --porcelain` empty, and nothing under the worktree root modified inside the idle window. For a simulator it additionally requires state `Shutdown`; for an AVD, no `qemu` process holding `-avd <name>`. Anything the gate cannot clear is REPORTED with its reason, never removed. `sweep.sh` defaults to a dry run and accepts no argument but `--apply`.
- **Three predicates are BANNED from the gate, each because it reads a LIVE artifact as dead.** All three were measured on 2026-08-18, not theorised. **(1) `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> origin/main`** — `spawn.sh` branches off `main`, so a worktree that has not committed yet has HEAD == main and is trivially an ancestor; this flagged #2211, #2245, #2267 and #2291 as reapable while all four were live with simulators booted. **(2) `git rev-list --count origin/main..<branch>`** — this repo squash-merges, so a merged branch's commits are never ancestors and the count is always ≥ 1; `origin/2272-web-dead-paths` measured 1 commit "ahead" with its PR merged and its issue closed. **(3) `find … -newermt '<relative>'`** — `bfs`, the find on the operator's Mac, rejects a relative timestamp, writes to stderr and returns EMPTY stdout, so the idiom `[ -z "$(find … -newermt …)" ] && rm -rf` evaluates TRUE for every directory; this fired during the #2300 cleanup itself and wiped the whole npx cache instead of its 7-day-stale part.
- **A safety that always fires is a safety everyone bypasses — that is the actual root cause.** `reap.sh` shipped with predicate (2) as Safety 2, so the documented close path ALWAYS failed on a legitimately merged branch. The only way through was `--force`, which also disables the uncommitted-changes check, so operators skipped reaping instead. 46 worktrees, 53 real `node_modules`, 15 orphaned simulators and 4 AVDs accumulated until the Mac reached **3.5 GB free of 460 GB** with 11.6 GB of swap on a 24 GB machine. The fix is not a louder warning; it is a gate that says yes when the answer is yes.
- **Every probe fails CLOSED.** An issue state that is not verifiably `CLOSED` is `UNKNOWN` and authorises nothing; a `gh` that cannot answer blocks the delete; an unreadable mtime resolves to *now*, so an un-stattable path reads as freshly touched rather than stale.
- **RAM is the same root cause, and the fix must not stop at disk.** Five booted per-issue simulators measured **15.1 GB RSS** on a 24 GB machine — ~3 GB each — against 967 MB for two Android emulators and 107 MB for Android Studio. Deleting simulators at CLOSE is necessary but not sufficient; capping concurrently-booted devices is follow-on work.
- **Enforcement:** `scripts/issue-2300/orch-artifact-reap.implementor.happy.test.mjs` (5 tests) and `…tester.adversarial.test.mjs` (15 tests), plus two grep gates in the lane that fail the build if `rev-list`, `is-ancestor` or `-newermt` reappears in the gate, or if `sweep.sh` grows a blast-radius-widening flag. Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2300-orch-artifact-reap.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven: restoring the old `rev-list` Safety 2 turns H4 red.
- **Established:** #2300, 2026-08-19 (PR #2307 merged as `fcc6689`).

## DRAFT — issue #2337 (free checkout says "no more tickets" for any conflict)

### I-PROPOSED-2337-A-STATUS-IS-NOT-A-MEANING (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** No buyer-facing copy mapper decides a sentence from an HTTP status alone. `freeCheckoutErrorMessage` reads the bounded token first (`free_reservation_already_exists`, `checkout_unavailable`, `checkout_session_failed`, `checkout_finalize_failed`, `intake_schema_stale`); the status is consulted only as a last resort, and a 409 whose token could not be read resolves to a sentence that claims NEITHER that the sale is gone NOR that nothing was reserved. This is #2188's paid-rail rule applied to the free rail, using the same `readEdgeRefusal` and the same shape — not a second mapper.
- **Why it matters:** `ticket-checkout-create` answers HTTP 409 for thirteen reachable free-rail conflicts. The old first line — `if (httpStatusOf(error) === 409) return FREE_CHECKOUT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE;` — collapsed all thirteen into "this free ticket is no longer available … Nothing was reserved". The loudest of them, `free_reservation_already_exists`, means the guest ALREADY HOLDS the reservation, so a guest with a ticket in hand was told the event was full — on an event whose ticket type is `is_unlimited: true, quantity_total: null`. It looked intermittent because it depended on whether a prior attempt had already reserved, never on capacity.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/functions/ticket-checkout-create/__tests__/issue_2337_free_409_honest_copy.test.ts` drives the REAL handler into all thirteen arms and runs each REAL response through the REAL mapper in one process (possible only because the mapper now lives in the dependency-free `mingla-business/src/services/checkoutErrorCopy.ts`); `mingla-business/src/services/__tests__/issue_2337_free_409_token_mapper.test.ts` covers the browser transport shapes, totality, and `invokeOrThrow`'s status/token/detail carry. Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2337-free-409-honest-copy-tests.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven by execution: restoring the deleted line turns 10 of 17 Deno tests and 19 of 64 jest tests red.

### I-PROPOSED-2337-B-SOLD-OUT-MUST-BE-EARNED (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** The only sentence that tells a guest there are no tickets left is reachable from exactly one fact — the database raising `ticket_capacity_exceeded` — carried to the client as the 409 body's `detail`. No status, and no other token, may produce it.
- **Why it matters:** The capacity guard is `IF v_ticket_type.quantity_total IS NOT NULL AND v_sold + v_reserved + v_cart_qty_for_type > v_ticket_type.quantity_total` (latest definer `20270420002160_issue_2160_multiday_multiselect.sql`). An unlimited tier has `quantity_total IS NULL` and is skipped, so it CANNOT raise the exception and therefore cannot reach the sentence. Before #2337 the client discarded the body's `detail` entirely, so a genuinely sold-out sale and a broken RPC were indistinguishable — which is why the mapper guessed, and guessed the same way every time.
- **Enforcement:** the two suites above (`NO free-rail 409 claims the tickets are gone unless the DATABASE raised ticket_capacity_exceeded`, exhaustive over every arm), plus a source assertion that reads the LATEST definer of the create-session wrapper so a re-emit that drops the NULL guard reds the lane.

### I-PROPOSED-2337-C-POSSESSION-TRAVELS-WITH-THE-APP-SESSION (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** Where a free reservation's buyer status token exists in this app session, it is presented on a resubmit. `sessionStorage` is preferred; the cart's own `result.buyerStatusToken` (#2323) is the fallback. The SERVER decides whether the presented token belongs to the reservation — the client never guesses at identity, and never discloses an order it did not prove it owns.
- **Why it matters:** #2150's storage read is gated on `Platform.OS === "web"`, so on iOS and Android `storage` is `undefined` and NO token was ever presented. Every native resubmit of a completed free reservation therefore took the `free_reservation_already_exists` 409 — the exact arm #2337 was mis-rendering. With the fallback the server replays the existing reservation and the guest lands on the confirmation screen holding their real pass, which is what "take them to it" means on this rail.
- **Enforcement:** `issue_2337_free_409_token_mapper.test.ts` pins the fallback by ORDER at the call site (stored token preferred, cart token second, both resolved before the request is built) and pins the already-reserved arm ahead of the generic mapper in BOTH free rails. Fails-on-revert proven: deleting the fallback, or either buyer screen's arm, reds one test each.

## DRAFT — issue #2353 (the Ari lifecycle migration relabels hybrid events, and its revoke has no shipped caller)

### I-PROPOSED-2353-A-FORMAT-IS-READ-NOT-DERIVED (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** No SQL in `supabase/migrations/**` may emit a business event `format` by testing `is_online`. Every site that produces a `format` value reads the stored enum first — `COALESCE(theme#>>'{business_event,format}', theme#>>'{business_draft,format}')`, or the caller-supplied `format` argument — accepts it only when `lower(btrim(...))` of it is one of `in_person` / `online` / `hybrid`, emits that **normalised** value, and falls back to the `is_online` derivation **only** when no stored or supplied value is valid. This is the exact shape the client has always used (`asFormat`, `businessEvents.ts:267-272`; `asDraftFormat`, `serverDraftEventMapper.ts:252-257`) — the server is being brought to the client's model, not given a new one.
- **Why it is a rule rather than a preference.** `is_online` is a two-valued projection of a three-valued enum: `is_online = format === "online" || format === "hybrid"` (`serverDraftEventMapper.ts:708`, duplicated at `:662`). Inverting it cannot distinguish `online` from `hybrid`, so every `CASE WHEN is_online THEN 'online' ELSE 'in_person' END` both destroys `hybrid` and makes `'hybrid'` unreachable as an output. #2089 shipped four such sites (`20270422001972` lines 601, 882, 1374, 1453). The one at line 601 is the dangerous one: `business_unpublish_event_to_draft:979` installs its output with `theme = v_payload->'theme'`, a wholesale replace, so a host who taps Unpublish or Duplicate on a hybrid event has the true value **overwritten**, not merely misreported, and the client cannot recover it.
- **The key is durable, and that was measured rather than assumed.** Production census over `events` where `deleted_at IS NULL`: 11 of 11 business event **drafts** carry `theme.business_draft.format`, 7 of 7 **published** business events carry `theme.business_event.format`, and the two namespaces are mutually exclusive (the publish RPC's theme rewrite does `(v_theme - 'business_draft') || jsonb_build_object('business_event', …)`, and `format` is not in its strip list). Coverage for `event_type='event'` is 18/18. `COALESCE` between the two is therefore unambiguous, not a guess between two live candidates.
- **Fails closed.** An absent, null, non-string or unrecognised value falls to the `is_online` derivation — the pre-#2089 behaviour — never to a fabricated `hybrid`. A caller-supplied value that is unrecognisable **after** normalisation is a NO-OP at every writer, never a silent default: #2353's own first revision entered `ari_execute_event_operation`'s live arm on key PRESENCE (`IF p_args ? 'format'`) and resolved such a value to a definite `'in_person'`, rewriting live hybrid events on a call that had previously done nothing at all. Entry must be the membership test, not the key test.
- **Normalisation is part of the rule, and that was decided against the SPEC.** SPEC §9 asked for a bare `IN (…)` with no `lower()`/`btrim()` on the premise that "every writer emits a bare literal". That is true of the shipped TypeScript client and **false of the server contract**: `business_create_event_draft(uuid,jsonb)` and `business_update_event_draft(uuid,jsonb,integer)` both hold `authenticated=X` and neither validates `theme.business_draft.format`, so an `event_manager` calling PostgREST directly can store `'Hybrid'` — the word the app's own UI shows a host. Un-normalised, that row missed the canonical list, fell to the `is_online` derivation, and one Unpublish/re-publish rewrote it to `'online'` (the theme write is a WHOLESALE replace, so the original was gone), at which point #2333's discovery carve-out — which tests `lower(format)='online'` — broadcast a venue-backed Lagos event into every market. Proven by execution on the combined #2333 + #2353 stack.
- **Enforcement:** strict-grep `.github/scripts/strict-grep/i-2353-format-is-read-not-derived.mjs` over `supabase/migrations/**` (registered `batch:A`, so it runs on every PR and not only when #2353's own paths change), comparing the occurrence **set** against a frozen allowlist of the four pre-existing sites in `20270422001972`, not a count of a constant declared inside the gate (#2113 — and specifically the failure mode the #2333 tester proved in `issue-2333-online-event-publish.mjs:163-168`, where an array-literal length check passed with a third live copy injected). The set comparison runs in BOTH directions: an occurrence outside the allowlist fails, and an allowlisted occurrence that has VANISHED fails too, because that means the merged, frozen migration was edited. **The detectors are anchored on the VALUE, not on the `'format',` label.** The first revision anchored on `'format'\s*,\s*CASE` and the #2353 tester proved it evadable by six trivially-equivalent rewrites of the same defect — a parenthesised CASE, a CASE-free boolean (`is_online = (p_patch->>'format' = 'online')`, the original bug minus the keyword), a CASE laundered through an intermediate variable, the simple-CASE form, and a double-quoted JSON key; 6 of 8 injections passed. All eight are now caught, each by name in `--self-test` (31 cases) and re-proved by injection into the real tree. The gate's header states in full what it still cannot catch — a derivation laundered through a variable that hides the column name, one that never writes both literals in one expression, dynamic SQL, and anything outside `supabase/migrations/**` — because a gate that quietly means less than its name is the #2113 family. The gate additionally requires that every canonical-membership test in the #2353 migration is normalised with `lower(btrim(…))` and that there are at least seven of them, that `ari_execute_event_operation`'s live arm enters on that test rather than on key presence, and pins LAST-WRITER order: #2353 must be the highest-timestamped migration that creates each of the three corrected functions, or PostgreSQL keeps a later, buggy definition and every test stays green until a hybrid event exists. Behaviour is proven by `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2353_format_truth.implementor.pg17.test.sql` (T-6..T-10, T-12b, T-14, T-15, T-15b) and by the tester's `…tester.adversarial.pg17.test.sql` (X-1's five-hop lifecycle, X-2's Ari live arm), both run by `.github/workflows/issue-2353-format-truth-and-edit-grant.yml`. Fails-on-revert proven by true line deletion at `7236ff27c`: restoring the `is_online` derivation at S2 reds T-6/T-9/T-10/T-12b and X-1 hops 1-3; stripping `lower(btrim(…))` reds nine T-12b/T-15b assertions; putting the live arm back on key presence reds X-2.
- **S0 guards ONE direction, and that is a known limit.** Applying `20270422001972` *after* `20270429002353` silently reverses the entire migration — the tester proved it by execution: `authenticated_on_taxonomy` goes true→false and the corrected read goes present→absent, with no error and both files recorded as applied. `20270422001972` is applied BY HAND (production's head is drifted higher), so a human ordering mistake is the live risk. The apply order is therefore a hard, verified step, not a note: `20270422001972` surgically FIRST, then `20270429002353`, then the SC-1 `pg_proc.proacl` query run AFTER BOTH.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2353, 2026-08-19; amended at REWORK 2026-08-19 (`7236ff27c`) after the adversarial TEST REPORT.

### I-PROPOSED-2353-B-IS-ONLINE-IS-A-PROJECTION-NOT-A-SOURCE (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** `events.is_online` is derived from `format`, never the reverse, and the two may not be written apart. **Scope: every writer in `supabase/migrations/**` that DERIVES either value from the other or from a caller argument.** Within that scope, both directions are covered and both are enforced:
  - **(a) format → is_online.** A writer that takes a supplied `format` computes `is_online` as `format IN ('online','hybrid')` and, in the same statement, persists that **normalised** `format` into the row's business namespace — **creating that namespace when the row does not carry it**, because `jsonb_set` creates only the final element of a path.
  - **(b) is_online → format.** A writer that takes a supplied `is_online` reconciles the stored `format` in the same statement **whenever, and only whenever, the two would otherwise disagree**. `is_online=true` on a stored `hybrid` already agrees, so `hybrid` is **preserved**; flattening it to `online` would satisfy a naive agreement test and destroy the exact value this invariant exists to protect.

  Neither value may be updated without the other being brought into agreement.
- **Why (b) is stated and enforced rather than left implicit.** The first version of this stanza had the headline "a writer may not update one without the other" over a clause that reached only writers setting `is_online` **from a format**. The #2353 retest falsified it by execution on `ari_execute_event_operation`'s **draft** arm: `is_online:false` on a hybrid draft left `format=hybrid, is_online=false`, and the disagreement **survived publish into a live row**. `is_online` is an *advertised* tool parameter (`agentTools.ts:753`), so that path needs no out-of-schema key — it is reachable by a host saying "this one isn't online any more". The headline forbade it; the clause did not catch it. Rather than narrow the headline to fit, `S6` was added to `20270429002353` so the draft arm upholds it, and the clause was widened to say both directions out loud. **An invariant that is false is worse than no invariant**, and a headline that outruns its own clause is the #2113 family in prose form.
- **What this rule does NOT cover, stated rather than implied.** `business_create_event_draft(uuid,jsonb)` and `business_update_event_draft(uuid,jsonb,integer)` accept a client-supplied `is_online` **and** `theme.business_draft.format` verbatim and reconcile neither — they are transport, not derivation, and both hold `authenticated=X`. A caller hitting PostgREST directly can therefore store a disagreeing pair, which no rule here prevents. Production holds **0** such rows (`rows_where_is_online_and_format_disagree = 0`, measured read-only at the #2353 retest). Validating those writers is outside #2353's scoped allowlist and is registered as a follow-up. **A third writer belongs in this same exclusion, found by the #2353 final retest and named here rather than left for the next reader to discover:** `business_publish_event_draft(uuid,jsonb,integer)` — reached in production through `issue_1719_publish_event_with_poster`, **both `authenticated=X`** — sets `is_online = COALESCE((p_draft_payload->>'is_online')::boolean, false)` straight from the caller's payload while carrying `theme.business_draft.format` through untouched (`format` is absent from the publish strip list), reconciling neither. A payload pairing `is_online:true` with `format:'in_person'` therefore persists a disagreeing pair **onto a live, published row** — the same shape as the two draft writers above, but with a live-row consequence, and it was not named in the first version of this exclusion. It is transport of a supplied pair, not derivation of one value from the other, so no clause of (a) or (b) reaches it. Until the follow-up lands, this invariant is true of every *deriving* writer and silent about all three *transporting* ones. **This correction is required BEFORE the DRAFT→ACTIVE flip and is not a blocker on applying the migration** — the stanza's own words are that an invariant which is false is worse than no invariant, and the first draft of this paragraph was false by omission.
- **Why the second half is not optional.** `business_update_live_event` (`20270422001972:882`) sets `is_online=CASE WHEN p_patch ? 'format' THEN p_patch->>'format'='online' ELSE is_online END` and its `theme` assignment writes only `{business_event,settings}`, `{business_event,clientRevision}` and `{coverHue}` — **`{business_event,format}` is never written.** The client ships `format` on every core patch (`ISSUE_1972_CORE_PATCH_KEYS`, `EditPublishedScreen.tsx:231-246`), so a hybrid save sets `is_online` FALSE against the client's own contract, and an `in_person`→`hybrid` change updates the derived column while leaving the stored enum stale. Fixing only the read side (invariant A) would then faithfully return the **stale** value: a wrong-derivation bug converted into a stale-data bug, which is harder to see and harder to attribute. The two sites move together or neither is fixed.
- **Why the namespace half is not optional either.** `jsonb_set` creates only the FINAL element of a path. On a live row whose `theme` carries no `business_event` object, the format PERSIST was a silent no-op while the `is_online` projection still fired: the host set Hybrid, `is_online` flipped true, nothing was stored, and the very next read reported `online` — the original defect, intact, on that one row shape. Production exposure is 0 today (7 of 7 live business events carry the namespace, measured read-only), but #2333's carve-out consumes exactly this value.
- **Enforcement:** the same strict-grep gate as A — which requires the `IN ('online','hybrid')` projection, the namespace-creating merge, the normalised `format` PERSIST, and (rule A10) S6's three draft-arm clauses — the `format` write, the `is_online` reconciliation, and the `IS DISTINCT FROM` condition that makes it fire *only* on disagreement — as SEPARATE rules, so deleting any one alone reds it — plus the pg17 behavioural suite `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2353_format_truth.implementor.pg17.test.sql`, which drives a real published-hybrid → live-edit-to-`in_person` → unpublish round trip (T-13), a namespace-less live row (T-12c), and normalisation at both the write and the read (T-12b), asserting `is_online` and `theme.business_event.format` agree at every hop; the draft arm's full precedence table (T-21: format wins over a contradicting `is_online`; a bare `is_online` that already agrees preserves `hybrid`; an unrecognised format is a no-op; the pair still agrees after a real publish); and the tester's five-hop lifecycle (X-1), driven namespace gap (X-4) and draft-arm probes (X-8, X-8b) in `…tester.adversarial.pg17.test.sql`. Fails-on-revert is measured by true line deletion, not comment-out, and the halves were proven red INDEPENDENTLY at `7236ff27c`: reverting the projection reds 13 implementor assertions, all of them about `is_online` (including a `null value in column "is_online"` crash on a JSON-null patch) plus X-2 and X-4; deleting the persist reds 9 implementor assertions, all about the stored format, plus X-1's hops 4-5; and reverting only the namespace creation reds exactly T-12c ×2 and X-4 ×2 and nothing else — three disjoint sets, none of which the others would have caught.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2353, 2026-08-19.

### I-PROPOSED-2353-C-A-REVOKE-SHIPS-WITH-ITS-CALLER (DRAFT)
- **Rule:** A migration may not revoke `EXECUTE` from `authenticated` on a function that a **shipped** client build still calls, unless the same release lands the replacement owner AND the client change that uses it, and the two are applied as one unit. Where the replacement owner is created by the same migration as the revoke, the revoke is split into a follow-on migration so that the expand step is safe to apply on its own.
- **Why it is a rule rather than a preference.** #2089 did this correctly in code and incorrectly in time. It revoked `business_patch_event_taxonomy` and `business_patch_event_when` from `authenticated`, created `business_update_live_event_atomic` as the single transactional owner, granted it to `authenticated`, and migrated `EditPublishedScreen` onto it — all in one commit, `0d9476573`, with a regression test pinning the client half. The architecture is sound and the file states it plainly: *"Business and Ari must call `business_update_live_event_atomic` instead"* (`20270422001972:838-840`). What it did not account for is that the `CREATE` and the `REVOKE` are in the **same migration** while the client half reaches devices by OTA. Apply before the OTA lands and every shipped build gets `permission denied for function business_patch_event_taxonomy`; ship the OTA before the apply and every build gets `function does not exist`. Both close published-event editing for **every** event, and no ordering of the two avoids a window.
- **What it is NOT.** This is not a rule against revoking `authenticated`. The revoke is correct and should end up applied: the leaves already carry full containment (`auth.uid()` null-check, `biz_brand_effective_rank ≥ event_manager`, status gate), and `business_patch_event_when` genuinely carries a stray live `anon=X` grant that the revoke removes. The rule governs **when**, not whether.
- **Enforcement:** strict-grep `.github/scripts/strict-grep/i-2353-format-is-read-not-derived.mjs` (invariants A and C share one gate; there is no separate `i-2353-revoke-ships-with-its-caller.mjs`). It requires the `authenticated` GRANT on BOTH `business_patch_event_when` and `business_patch_event_taxonomy` — each as its own rule, so losing one is caught — bans any GRANT in that migration reaching `anon` or `PUBLIC`, and requires the `[TRANSITIONAL]` tag and a written `EXIT CONDITION` as two separate rules. It also pins the apply-order guard as the FIRST executable statement and pins its `to_regprocedure` probe, since a guard that runs after one `CREATE OR REPLACE` has already done the damage it exists to prevent. Fails-on-revert proven at `7236ff27c`: deleting the GRANT reds T-1/T-2/T-3 (7 implementor assertions) and X-7 (2), all of them by `42501 permission denied` rather than by the containment errors they assert, which is what distinguishes a lost grant from a lost guard. Runtime proof is `SC-1` in `.github/workflows/issue-2353-format-truth-and-edit-grant.yml`, read straight off `pg_proc.proacl`, plus T-1..T-5 in `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2353_format_truth.implementor.pg17.test.sql`, which prove by EXECUTION that the grant restores reach and not authority: an `event_manager` succeeds, a `scanner` and a manager on another brand are both refused inside the body, and `anon` is refused at the ACL. **SCOPE, stated rather than silently narrowed:** the gate enforces this for the two functions #2089's revoke actually targeted — the only two with a shipped client caller. The general sweep this Rule describes would cover 255 `REVOKE … FROM … authenticated` statements on `main`, the overwhelming majority deliberate server-only demotions with no caller to strand; it needs its own frozen allowlist and is outside #2353's scoped allowlist. Decide it at the DRAFT→ACTIVE flip.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2353, 2026-08-19.

### I-2333-CITY-GUARDS-ARE-FORMAT-AWARE-NOT-ONLINE-AWARE (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** Every server-side `city_required` guard keys on the same canonical format normalisation owned by #2353 — `lower(btrim(value, E' \t\n\r\f\v' || chr(160))) = 'online'` — read from `theme.business_draft.format` (publish-time) or `theme.business_event.format` (post-publish). No `city_required` guard may key on `is_online`, `p_draft_payload->>'is_online'`, or `events.is_online`.
- **Why `is_online` is the wrong identifier, and why it is dangerous rather than merely imprecise.** `is_online` is written as `draft.format === "online" || draft.format === "hybrid"` (`mingla-business/src/utils/serverDraftEventMapper.ts:708`). A guard keyed on it silently exempts HYBRID from a city that the client REQUIRES for hybrid (`draftEventValidation.ts:382-406` demands venue name + address + city on the in_person|hybrid branch). That re-creates, in the opposite direction, the exact client/server divergence that produced #2333 — and the naive fix and the correct fix are one identifier apart, both compile, and both pass an online happy-path test. Only a hybrid-boundary test separates them.
- **Absent or unrecognised format FAILS CLOSED** — an unknown format demands a city. A stale client, a hand-built payload, or a legacy row can never widen the guard.
- **The two read paths are deliberately different objects, and that asymmetry is load-bearing.** `business_publish_event_draft` reads `format` from the SAME `theme.business_draft` node it reads `city` from, so guard and value can never disagree about which payload they are judging. `business_patch_event_taxonomy` has no payload and no format argument at all — it reads `theme.business_event.format` off the row it already holds under `FOR UPDATE`. Publish carries `format` from one node to the other: it is NOT in the strip list (`- 'tickets' - 'category' - 'partyTypes' - 'vibeTags' - 'musicGenres' - 'city' - 'locationGeo'`).
- **Enforcement:** SC-3 and SC-6 of the #2333 SPEC (hybrid-with-no-city still raises, at BOTH guards), SC-4 and T-7 (absent format fails closed), plus a strict-grep gate over `supabase/migrations/**` asserting no `city_required` raise sits inside a condition that mentions `is_online`.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2333, 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE once migrations `20270427002333` and `20270427002334` are applied to production `gqnoajqerqhnvulmnyvv` and the bodies are re-read from `pg_get_functiondef`.

### I-2333-ONLINE-ONLY-CARVE-OUT-IS-FORMAT-SCOPED (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** The market-independence carve-out in `pg_discover_business_events`'s location predicate matches `e.is_online IS TRUE AND lower(btrim(COALESCE(e.theme->'business_event'->>'format',''), E' \t\n\r\f\v' || chr(160))) = 'online'`. It may never be widened to a bare `e.is_online`, and it must use #2353's canonical trim set so publish, edit and discovery recognise the same stored values.
- **Why:** Seth's decision (2026-08-19) was that ONLINE events surface in every market. Bare `is_online` also broadcasts every HYBRID event — which has a real venue, a real city and a real catchment — into every market on earth. The two predicates differ by one conjunct and produce feeds that look plausible in both cases, so nothing but a targeted negative test distinguishes them.
- **The carve-out widens LOCATION and nothing else.** `visibility='public'`, the `status IN ('scheduled','live')` gate, `issue_1931_event_ordinary_read_blocked`, the date window, the party/vibe/genre facets and the `pg_brand_can_collect` paid-online gate are all untouched. It is added as a THIRD arm, last, so the existing city and geo arms keep first-match short-circuit and the common path is byte-identical.
- **What it fixes.** `city = NULL` makes `NULL = ANY(p_cities)` evaluate to NULL, not TRUE, so arm one fails; `location_geo = NULL` fails arm two. Both false means the row was returned by NO market, ever, with no error and no admin signal — publish would have traded a loud failure for a silent one.
- **It repairs zero rows that exist today, and the ship log must not claim otherwise.** The full prod census on 2026-08-19 found exactly one published `city IS NULL` row (`18210000-0000-4000-8000-000000000302`), and it is `visibility='private'`, `rsvp_discoverable=false`, `is_online=false` — excluded by three other gates and untouched by this arm. The value is entirely forward-looking.
- **Enforcement:** SC-8 / T-9 of the #2333 SPEC (a hybrid event outside the browsed market is NOT returned), SC-9 / T-11 (one negative case per unrelated gate), SC-10 / T-12 (`total` and pagination stay correct across a mixed row set), plus the same strict-grep gate.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2333, 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE once migration `20270427002335` is applied to production and verified with a live `pg_discover_business_events` call.

### I-2333-UNMAPPED-SERVER-GUARD-NEVER-INVITES-RETRY (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** No publish or edit error path in `mingla-business` may render copy that invites a retry for a server-raised guard it does not recognise. An unrecognised guard is either named — when it is a bare `snake_case` token matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,63}$` — or acknowledged honestly, and is always `console.error`-logged. Publish and published-event-edit fallbacks are operation-specific: an edit failure may never claim publishing failed or that a draft was saved. The literal string `"Could not save this publish. Try again."` must not exist under `mingla-business/src`.
- **Why this is a class bug and not one bad string.** `EventCreatorWizard.tsx:698` was the terminal `else` for EVERY server guard the client did not know. `city_required` was live and unpublishable for at least two days while the app told a paying customer to try again — and retrying could never succeed, because the field the server demanded is not rendered for his format. Every future typed guard is a silent dead end by default until the fallback is structural. Constitution #1 (no dead taps) and #3 (no silent failures).
- **A raw `error.message` is untrusted input.** It can be a PostgREST envelope, a constraint name, or a stack fragment, so the token shape is checked BEFORE anything is shown; anything that fails the shape test gets the generic honest copy and is never echoed verbatim into a toast.
- **Enforcement:** SC-12 / T-15 (a snake_case token is named, no "Try again", log fired) and T-16 (envelope, empty string, 4 KB string and a token carrying markup are all handled without echoing), plus a strict-grep gate on the banned literal.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2333, 2026-08-19.

### I-2333-ONLINE-FORMAT-IS-DURABLE (ACTIVE)

- **Rule:** `theme.business_event.format` is load-bearing for `business_patch_event_taxonomy` and `pg_discover_business_events`. Any new or changed RPC that writes `events.theme` for a standard event must MERGE (`jsonb_set` / `||`) rather than wholesale-replace.
- **Why:** losing that key is not a visible error. It silently un-publishes online events from Discover in every market and simultaneously re-bricks their editing — both of which look exactly like #2333 before the fix, and neither of which raises anything.
- **Verified true at the time of writing, by enumeration rather than assumption.** Every live function that writes `events.theme` was listed from `pg_proc` (`UPDATE public.events` + `theme =`): the three publish RPCs, the three `biz_update_live_*`, `biz_create_experience` / `biz_publish_experience`, and `biz_set_event_guest_privacy`. That last one is the only post-publish theme writer for a standard event and it is `jsonb_set(v_theme, '{business_event,settings}', v_settings, true)` — a deep merge. Confirmed live on the one published online event in production (`74aa0f76-34b5-4e7e-a239-cda439d5e2fb`, `theme.business_event.format = 'online'`).
- **Both dependents degrade fail-closed, not fail-wrong.** A missing key means the patch demands a city again and the event stops surfacing — recoverable and loud-ish — rather than a hybrid event leaking into every market.
- **Enforcement:** merged #2353 is authoritative for every writer that can affect this key: `.github/scripts/strict-grep/i-2353-format-is-read-not-derived.mjs` scans `supabase/migrations/**`, freezes the derivation occurrence set in both directions, pins #2353 as the last writer of the corrected functions, and separately requires the format projection and persist; its implementor and adversarial PostgreSQL suites drive publish, Duplicate, Unpublish, Ari live and Ari draft hops. #2333's gate additionally pins the publish namespace merge and refuses `format` in its strip list. Together they catch both a writer that derives the wrong value and the #2333 publish writer dropping the key.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2333, 2026-08-19.

## DRAFT — issue #2305 (buyers whose name differs from an existing record are dropped from the contact book)

### I-PROPOSED-2305-CONFLICT-QUEUE-HAS-A-RESOLVER (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A table that models a resolution lifecycle — a `status` column whose CHECK admits a terminal state alongside its initial one, paired with a nullable `resolved_at`/`resolved_by`-shaped column — must have, somewhere in this repo, code that ADVANCES it: a statement that `UPDATE`s that status column to a non-initial value, AND at least one `SELECT … FROM` the table outside its own DDL. A table with N INSERT sites, zero readers, and a status no statement advances is a **write-only sink**.
- **Why this is a rule and not a preference.** `brand_person_identity_conflicts` shipped in `20270305001770` with ten INSERT sites across four ingest paths, a three-state CHECK (`open` / `resolved_merge` / `resolved_separate`), a `resolved_by` FK, and `CONSTRAINT brand_person_conflict_resolution_shape CHECK ((status='open' AND resolved_at IS NULL) OR (status<>'open' AND resolved_at IS NOT NULL))`. The string `resolved_at` appears nowhere else in the entire repo — only inside that constraint. The schema is a blueprint for a resolution path that was never built, and the constraint is the proof it was intended. `open` is not a starting state; it is the only state.
- **Same class as #2168, #2222 and #2290, one layer up.** #2290 was a worker with no caller — a switch nothing flips. This is a write with no reader — a form nobody collects. Both survive the same way: the write path is fully tested, the constraint is correct, the types line up, `deno check` is clean, CI is green, and the feature is dead in production. The `I-2290-QUEUE-WORKER-HAS-CRON-CALLER` gate structurally cannot catch it — its unit of analysis is an edge function and its evidence is a `cron.job` row; this defect's unit is a table and its evidence is the absence of a `SELECT`.
- **What it would have caught.** Run against `20270305001770`'s own commit the gate fails on `brand_person_identity_conflicts`. Measured cost of the miss: 6 open conflicts on production, 3 distinct buyers, **3 of 13 confirmed paid orders (23%)** orphaned with no source link, the oldest filed 2026-06-27 and dropped 2026-08-13 with the brand never told.
- **Anti-vacuity is mandatory** (#2113 — a check that cannot fail carries no information): the gate asserts it parsed at least one qualifying table, and fails against a fixture reproducing the pre-fix shape. A frozen `WRITE_ONLY_BY_DESIGN` allowlist carries a reason and an issue number per entry, matching `issue-2290`'s `HAND_KICKED` idiom.
- **Scope, measured rather than assumed.** The gate's unit is the LIFECYCLE TABLE, and it discovers **23** of them in this repo. For each it demands (A) a reader, (B) an `UPDATE` advancing the status off its initial value, and (C) that the function CONTAINING that `UPDATE` is itself invoked from production code — reachability, the #2290 lesson applied one layer up. Condition (C) is what catches `biz_reverse_brand_person_merge`, the third instance of the class this session: fully implemented, writes a complete `reversal_manifest`, called by nothing. **The wider rule the REVIEW floated — "any SQL function with no caller" — was measured and REJECTED: 27 `SECURITY DEFINER` functions in this repo are never invoked from production today, so that scope would red `main` on day one behind a 27-entry allowlist**, which is the frozen-list-nobody-re-checks failure mode #2290 warns about. 20 of the 23 tables already satisfy all three conditions; the 3 that do not are named in a frozen `WRITE_ONLY_BY_DESIGN` allowlist with a reason and an issue number each — `brand_person_merge_events` (#2305, Split has no caller and no UI), `ad_app_acquisition_canaries` (#2015, a 7-state lifecycle whose only `UPDATE`s reset it to `not_started`) and `event_private_media_transition_jobs` (#1931, an 8-state machine with **no `UPDATE` anywhere in the repo**). A stale exemption, or one whose table has since gained a reachable resolver, FAILS the gate.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2305-status-table-has-a-resolver.mjs` (`batch:A`, `self-test` + `plain`, registered `selfTest:"wired"`) with `.github/scripts/strict-grep/__tests__/issue-2305-status-table-has-a-resolver.test.mjs` (15 cases, implementor) and an adversarial sibling to follow from the tester. Confirmed to actually EXECUTE, not merely be registered: `run-batch.mjs --class A` reported `expected 898, executed 898, missing 0` with all three entries `ok`. Lane: `.github/workflows/issue-2305-conflict-resolution-tests.yml`.
- **Fails-on-revert:** proven by TRUE LINE DELETION (never a comment-out) of BOTH `UPDATE public.brand_person_identity_conflicts SET status=…` statements in the resolve RPC — the terminal one and the vanished-source one. Guard exits **1** naming `brand_person_identity_conflicts (20270305001770…) — nothing UPDATEs status off 'open'`; restored byte-identical (`shasum -a256 -c` OK) it exits **0**. Exit codes read from `$?` directly, never after a pipe. Deleting only ONE of the two statements leaves the gate green, which is correct: the table still has an advancer.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2305 SPEC 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge, and merged-main verification.

### I-PROPOSED-2305-RESOLUTION-MUST-LINK-THE-SOURCE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Closing an identity conflict must leave its source linked to exactly one active person. A `brand_person_identity_conflicts` row at `status='resolved_merge'` or `'resolved_separate'` with **no** active `brand_person_source_links` row for its `(source_kind, source_id)` is a **false resolution** and must fail the gate.
- **Carve-out, amended at #2305 REWORK — exactly one, and narrow on purpose.** A resolution must link its source **unless the source is provably absent** — the row does not exist, or the ledger provably holds no payload — in which case the conflict resolves as **`resolved_dismissed`**, links nothing, and records why. **Absence must be demonstrated, never assumed from a failed lookup.** `biz_brand_person_conflict_absence` probes raw row existence independently of every business predicate, so a source that merely fell out of a status filter reports as PRESENT and stays un-dismissable; accepting "the lookup returned nothing" would convert a query bug into silent data loss, which is the defect this issue exists to end. `resolved_dismissed` exists because a conflict whose subject cannot be produced otherwise has NO exit, and with no exit it wedges the badge — this feature's only notification mechanism. It covers both shapes the tester proved: a deleted source row, and a `manual` add whose payload was only ever hashed.
- **Why it is separate from the invariant above.** The first invariant makes the queue readable and drainable. This one makes draining it mean something. A resolve path that sets `status` and `resolved_at`, satisfies the CHECK, empties the badge and never writes the link would pass every catalogue assertion, look completely fixed to the operator, and leave the buyer exactly as gone as before — a UI that hides the bug rather than a fix. This is the field that separates the two.
- **A separation is a statement about a PAIR, so it is recorded from both sides.** Writing only *(candidate, incoming name)* left `resolved_separate` half-stuck: the ORIGINAL buyer re-conflicted on their next order, and at that point BOTH controls were wrong — merge folded back together the two humans just separated, and separate created a THIRD record while severing the original from their own name. The reverse row, plus every active alternate the candidate answers to, is written too; and the AUTOMATIC chain-merge — which has no human behind it — refuses to collapse any pair the ledger already calls different people.
- **The proof obligation is behavioural, not structural.** It is not enough to assert the RPC contains an INSERT. The binding tests re-run `biz_resolve_brand_person_source` against the same source AFTER resolution and require `linkOutcome='already_linked'` — never `'conflict'` — with the link still active and still attached. That closes four proven recurrence paths: the pre-conflict detach block strands an existing link (the `already_linked` fast path is the only thing standing between a resolved buyer and being unlinked again); the fast path's `(v_user IS NULL OR p.linked_user_id = v_user)` clause fails unless resolution sets `linked_user_id`; the conflict test reads only `brand_people.display_name` and never `brand_person_names`, so a new order from the same buyer re-conflicts forever; and the chain-merge that follows a passing conflict test will silently re-merge two people a human deliberately separated.
- **Shipped shape.** The resolve RPC is `biz_resolve_brand_person_conflict(uuid, uuid[], text, uuid, uuid)` — it takes an ARRAY of conflict ids and closes the whole group in ONE transaction, all or none. Production carries 11 open conflicts resolving to only 3 distinct buyers, with one buyer accounting for 5 rows, so per-source resolution would let an operator answer the identical identity question five times inconsistently and leave one human simultaneously filed under an existing person, duplicated as a new one, AND carrying a separation row blocking the correct future link.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2305_conflict_resolution.test.sql`, executed against a full-chain PostgreSQL 17 (not asserted from source). Nine blocks pass: catalogue/RLS/grants, merge (T-1/3/4/5/7/8/15/16), separate (T-2/6/7), the F-3 detach proof, grouping, the `graph_only` boundary (T-9), typed errors (T-10), reversibility (T-14) and G-3. T-3, T-5, T-6 and T-7 are the spine — the only cases that can tell a real fix from a queue that refills.
- **REWORK enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2305_conflict_resolution_rework.test.sql` — six blocks, each re-proving a finding the tester proved by execution: P1-1 (their exact sequence — after a separate the ORIGINAL buyer's next order links back to the ORIGINAL person, no conflict, no third record, no merge), P1-1(b), P1-2 (the dismissing write COMMITS), the absence rule, P2-1 and P2-4/P3-1. Five independent fails-on-revert proofs by true line deletion; notably, inferring absence from a failed lookup turns the suite red with *"a PRESENT row was reported absent — that is silent data loss"*.
- **Fails-on-revert, four independent proofs, all by TRUE LINE DELETION.** Deleting the source-link `INSERT` fails the suite; deleting the status advance fails `T-2305-01 conflict status/resolved_at/resolved_by wrong`; deleting the A-1 alternate-name clause fails `T-2305-05 a new order from a resolved buyer … the queue would never empty`; restoring the pre-fix ordering so the detach block runs BEFORE the conflict decision fails `F-3 a conflicting re-ingest DETACHED a person already in the book`. Deleting the A-2 separations exclusion is caught EARLIER still — by the migration's own `DO $assert$` block, which refuses to install a resolver body missing the amendment (`people_resolver_amendments_missing`).
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2305 SPEC 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge, and merged-main verification.
### I-PROPOSED-2322-EVERY-IOS-PICKER-DECLARES-ITS-OWN-COLOURS (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every `<DateTimePicker>` call site under `app-mobile/src` that can render on iOS MUST set both `themeVariant` and `textColor` explicitly. A picker that inherits the device trait is a defect regardless of what `app.json` declares.
- **Why the app-level setting is not the guarantee.** `app-mobile/app.json` declared `"userInterfaceStyle": "light"` throughout the incident and it was not honoured — a `dark` key in the `expo-splash-screen` plugin config silently rewrote the native `UIUserInterfaceStyle` to `Automatic` (see the sibling invariant below). Any rule of the form "the app is always light, so pickers need no colours" rests on a config value that a plugin can overwrite from a different part of the file. The colours must be stated where the control is.
- **The failure mode is silent and looks like success.** A near-white wheel on Mingla's white card still scrolls, still haptics, still fires `onChange`, and still displays a legible value in the field AFTER commit. Nothing throws, nothing logs, and the user has no signal that they read nothing — they simply saved a birthday they never chose. No unit test, type check or green CI run could see it; only pixels could.
- **Coverage, not a string match.** The gate walks all 12 call sites in the tree and fails any iOS-reachable one lacking either prop, so a 13th picker added later is covered automatically rather than arriving unguarded. It must also fail if the guarded call sites disappear, rather than passing vacuously (#2113 — a check that cannot fail carries no information).
- **Scope note.** A shared themed wrapper was considered and REJECTED at SPEC: the five pre-existing themed call sites deliberately split across light and dark tones, so a wrapper relocates the per-site decision instead of removing it, and refactoring five shipped surfaces to fix none of them is risk for no gain. The "nobody ships an unthemed picker again" guarantee comes from this gate, not from a component.
- **Enforcement:** `app-mobile/src/components/__tests__/issue_2322_ios_picker_theming.implementor.happy.test.mjs`, registered by explicit filename in `.github/ci-batch/MANIFEST.json` (`issue-2322-ios-picker-theming-tests`, `expectedSuites` 20→21).
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2322, 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS on a real onboarding screen, all-green merge, and merged-main verification.

## DRAFT — issue #1971 (canonical Ari trip lifecycle)

### I-PROPOSED-1971-TRIP-GRAPH-ONE-COMMAND (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Business web/iOS/Android and Ari mutate one canonical trip graph through the same six SQL commands. No client and no agent executor may `insert`/`update`/`delete` `events`, `event_dates`, `trip_days`, `trip_inclusions`, `ticket_types`, `trip_pricing_tiers` or `trip_intake_schemas` directly for a trip lifecycle operation. Publish loads the PERSISTED graph server-side and never accepts a caller-assembled payload.
- **What this replaced:** a three-statement client create that could orphan a draft or leave a ticket without a tier; delete-then-insert day/inclusion replacement that erased the itinerary if the insert failed; split `ticket_types`/`trip_pricing_tiers` writes; a direct `trip_intake_schemas` upsert; and an Ari `publish_trip` that sent `{}` to a publish contract requiring a full graph and therefore could never succeed.
- **The trap this rule exists to keep closed:** the shared Business `LiveTripPatch` vocabulary is TOP-LEVEL (`title`, `theme`, `pricing_tiers`, …) while Ari's `TripDraftGraphV1` is grouped (`event`, `tiers`, …). An earlier attempt allow-listed only the grouped keys, and independent QA proved that made published-trip editing dead on web, iOS and Android at once. `biz_update_trip_live_command` forwards the top-level vocabulary byte for byte to `issue_1719_update_live_trip_with_poster` and TRANSLATES the grouped keys into that same owner.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-1971-ari-trip-lifecycle.mjs` (24 mutants, each required red for its own assertion), `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_1971_trip_lifecycle.implementor.happy.pg17.test.sql`, `supabase/functions/_shared/__tests__/issue_1971_ari_trips.implementor.test.ts`, and `mingla-business/src/services/__tests__/issue_1971_trip_command_contract.implementor.test.ts`.
- **Status:** DRAFT until independent deployed runtime proof on Business web, iOS and Android.

### I-PROPOSED-1971-TRIP-WRITES-IDEMPOTENT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every trip command commits its domain mutation and its receipt in ONE transaction. The receipt binds actor, tenant, command, resource, canonical arguments AND the expected revision. An identical replay returns the recorded result; any changed member fails closed with `idempotency_conflict`. A stale expected revision is a typed `trip_revision_conflict` with zero writes. Ari additionally passes the immutable confirmed pending-action id, never a model-supplied value, and consumes #1972's shared recovery receipt.
- **Why `expected_updated_at` is inside the hash:** without it, reusing one operation id with a materially different expected revision returns the EARLIER result instead of conflicting — the caller believes it edited revision B and is handed the outcome of editing revision A. Independent QA found exactly that.
- **Enforcement:** `biz_trip_command_begin`/`_finish`, `ari_execute_trip_operation`, and sections C/E/J of the #1971 PostgreSQL 17 guard.
- **Status:** DRAFT pending independent runtime proof of concurrent and retried confirmation.

### I-PROPOSED-1971-TRIP-DELETE-NO-CONFIRMED-ORDERS (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A trip may be soft-deleted only when NO order sits outside `failed`/`cancelled`, on any payment rail. `biz_trip_has_web_purchases` is a notification-only predicate — it sees card/Apple Pay/Google Pay only — and must never be the deletion guard. Delete and confirmed-order arrival serialize on one advisory key so neither can win a race: a deleted trip also refuses a new confirmed order.
- **Enforcement:** `biz_soft_delete_trip`, the `trg_biz_trip_order_delete_lock` BEFORE trigger on `public.orders`, and section I of the #1971 PostgreSQL 17 guard (which uses a DOOR sale — the exact order the web-purchase predicate would have missed).
- **Status:** DRAFT pending independent adversarial race proof.

### I-PROPOSED-1971-TRIP-SIDECAR-EVENT-MANAGER (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Direct write access to `trip_days`, `trip_inclusions` and `trip_pricing_tiers` requires effective rank `event_manager` or higher. The deployed policies used a brand-membership-for-READ predicate, which let scanner-class members attempt graph mutation. Reads are unchanged.
- **Enforcement:** the `*_write_event_managers` policies in `20270509001971_issue_1971_ari_trip_lifecycle.sql`, plus `biz_trip_require_manager` on every command.
- **Status:** DRAFT pending an independent scanner-role denial proof against a deployed database.

### I-PROPOSED-1971-TRIP-ORDER-MONEY-NO-PII (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** The trip order/money capability is read-only, `finance_manager`+, trip- and brand-scoped, and fail-closed. It returns counts, gross and refunded totals in canonical integer units, sold counts by package, and instalment counts/amounts by status and due bucket — and never a buyer name, email, phone, address, payment instrument, note or raw order payload. A read failure raises; it never degrades to zero.
- **Why "never degrades to zero" is part of the rule:** the pre-#1971 `aggregatePaidOrdersByEvent` silently converted a read failure into an empty map, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty trip.
- **Enforcement:** `biz_get_trip_order_money_snapshot`, its `finance_manager` declaration in `agentToolAuthorization.ts`, its entry in the #2013 tenant-scoped read registry, and section H of the #1971 PostgreSQL 17 guard (which asserts the absence of each named PII key).
- **Status:** DRAFT pending independent runtime inspection of the raw tool response.

- **Enforcement:** `business_unpublish_experience_to_draft`, `business_discard_experience_draft`, the shared Business action, and issue #1973 lifecycle regressions.

### I-PROPOSED-1973-EXPERIENCE-MEDIA-PROVENANCE (DRAFT)

### I-PROPOSED-2322-DECLARED-APPEARANCE-EQUALS-BUILT-APPEARANCE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** The `userInterfaceStyle` declared in `app-mobile/app.json` MUST equal the `UIUserInterfaceStyle` in the generated native `Info.plist`. No plugin config may silently override it.
- **The concrete regression this pins.** PR #2065 (`a5e567565`, merged 2026-08-14) added `"dark": { "backgroundColor": "#FAFAFA" }` to the `expo-splash-screen` plugin config. Expo treats the presence of that key as dark-mode support and writes `Automatic`, contradicting `"userInterfaceStyle": "light"`. The dark launch colour itself cannot be deleted: active invariant #2050 requires Explorer launch to state `#FAFAFA` explicitly in both themes. The final owner is therefore `plugins/withForcedLightAppearance.js`, registered **before** splash because Expo executes same-mod interceptors in reverse registration order; it restores `Light` without weakening #2050. Consumer 1.1.4 was clean; 1.1.5 shipped the pre-repair `Automatic` value to both stores.
- **The probe matters as much as the rule.** `npx expo config --type prebuild --json` reports `light` here and is the WRONG probe — it does not run the plugin's native `withInfoPlist` mod, so it returns a false green. Verification must read the generated or built `Info.plist`. This cost a full verification round during REVIEW and is recorded so it is not repeated.
- **Orchestrator-verified at the strongest available layer:** every Mingla bundle built on the operator's machine reported `UIUserInterfaceStyle = Automatic` — `Mingla.app`, `MinglaHost.app` and `MinglaBusiness.app` — while `app.json` said `light`. `MinglaBusiness.app` sharing the value is why #2343 exists.
- **Known live consumer of the appearance value.** `app-mobile/src/components/share/UnifiedShareProvider.tsx:95` reads `useColorScheme() === 'dark'`. Under the `Automatic` regression this rendered the share sheet dark for dark-mode users; restoring forced-light returns it to its 1.1.4 appearance. Any future change to the app's appearance mode must re-check this call site — it is currently the only live one.
- **Enforcement:** T-2 in `issue_2322_ios_picker_theming.implementor.happy.test.mjs` retains #2050's exact dark launch block, requires the Mingla owner before splash (reverse execution order), and executes its pure mutation helper against an `Automatic` plist while proving unrelated keys survive. Release proof reads `UIUserInterfaceStyle` from a freshly generated or built `Info.plist`; `expo config` alone is not accepted. A general warning gate remains tracked as #2342.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2322, 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge, and merged-main verification.

### I-PROPOSED-2343-HOST-NATIVE-APPEARANCE-IS-FIXED-LIGHT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Mingla Host iOS and Android must build with a fixed Light native appearance regardless of the device setting. Each platform has one final native appearance owner, while the #2050 Host splash remains explicitly orange `#eb7825` in both device themes. Intentionally dark Host compositions remain locally owned; in particular, `PaymentPlanEditor`'s iOS inline picker declares `themeVariant="dark"` and the established light-on-dark `text.primary` token.
- **Enforcement:** the append-only #2343 implementor and tester suites inspect the real Host config and picker source, execute the pure Info.plist owner, pin plugin order and #2050 splash bytes, and are explicitly registered in `.github/ci-batch/MANIFEST.json`. Release proof must inspect generated/built `UIUserInterfaceStyle=Light` and Android `expo_system_ui_user_interface_style=light`, then compare settled Light/Dark-device runtime pixels on the exact replacement artifacts.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2343, 2026-08-21; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge, exact replacement Host artifact inspection, and Light/Dark runtime verification.

### I-PROPOSED-2399-MULTIDAY-CHOICE-LIVES-WITH-PURCHASE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A buyable multi-day event must place its day chooser first inside the Tickets purchase container, keep the displayed box and floating-bar totals synchronized with the selected-day pricing mode, and fail closed while no valid day truth is selected. Single-day callers that omit the optional purchase context preserve their rendered tree and checkout request.

## DRAFT — issue #2060 (Ari reliability and exact-release certification)

These invariants remain DRAFT until #2060 is merged, both Ari functions and
Business surfaces are deployed from the exact merge SHA, every ledger row is
certified, cleanup reaches zero residue, rollback is rehearsed, and the
independent tester returns PASS.

### I-ARI-LOGICAL-TURN-ONCE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** One caller, tenant, and `client_turn_id` produces at most one durable user turn and proposal; every retry replays its current or terminal server state.
- **Enforcement:** #1985 owns the durable client-turn constraint and atomic task turn. Issue #2060's shared response/recovery contract, 116-row certification validator, and `issue-2060-ari-reliability-foundation.mjs` gate require stable correlation and reject a second-ID retry after ambiguity.

### I-ARI-EXECUTION-ONCE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** One immutable confirmed action version has one `execution_id`, propagates its idempotency identity to the canonical domain owner, and replays terminal truth without a second side effect.
- **Enforcement:** #1972 owns the generic atomic operation receipt; each Pass 4 domain owns its mutation/readback adapter. #2060's finalization seam refuses success without a durable receipt and matched readback, while the certification plan requires duplicate-confirm and lost-ack replay for every write row.

### I-ARI-RESULT-HONESTY (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Ari may display a completed action only after durable terminal state and matching canonical readback. Missing, mismatched, or lost results remain `RESULT_UNKNOWN` or `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` and never invite a new write ID.
- **Enforcement:** `agentReliability.ts` on edge and Business, the typed error registry, exact-release evidence validator, and the issue #2060 implementor/tester regression pair.

### I-ARI-RECOVERY-PARITY (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Business web, iOS, and Android restore the same server-authoritative sending, pending, executing, reconciling, and terminal state after offline, retry, refresh, relaunch, or a second session.
- **Enforcement:** the platform-neutral Business recovery reducer, shared network-state integration after #1985 merge, per-row cache/readback ownership, and exact-artifact runtime evidence on all three Business surfaces.

### I-ARI-CORRELATED-RELEASE-TRUTH (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** Every Ari response, operation phase, log, and certification record carries safe request/client-turn/execution correlation and the independently verified release SHA/function version, with no prompt, args, result, PII, JWT, exception, SQL, or configuration payload.
- **Enforcement:** the versioned #2060 envelope, allowlisted telemetry event, immutable `ari_cert_release_artifacts`, bundle-hash attestation, and CI gate. Missing `MINGLA_RELEASE_SHA` resolves to `unattested` and blocks certification.

### I-ARI-LEDGER-CERTIFICATION (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** No canonical Ari capability row becomes `verified` without exact-SHA evidence for every required scenario, tenant/role negative, Business surface, canonical readback, cleanup, rollback, and independent tester PASS.
- **Enforcement:** `docs/contracts/ari-capability-ledger.json` is the only row inventory; `scripts/ari/certify-capabilities.mjs` derives and validates all 116 rows; `ari_cert_finalize_run` fails closed on missing evidence/artifacts/residue/rollback; the CI gate rejects a second inventory or unbound domain owner.

### I-PROPOSED-2322-AN-UNTOUCHED-PICKER-IS-NOT-AN-ANSWER (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** In onboarding, tapping Done on a birthday wheel the user has never interacted with MUST NOT commit a value, and MUST NOT unblock the step's CTA. The wheel may seed at a default for display; the default may not become the stored answer.
- **Why this is a correctness rule and not a preference.** The stored birthday feeds `buildOccasions()` in `OnboardingFlow.tsx` and seeds the user's Birthday occasion, which the app then surfaces to them and to people they are paired with. A value the user never chose, arriving through a control they could not see, is fabricated data (Constitution rule 9) with a durable downstream consequence.
- **Measured behaviour before the fix:** opening the field and tapping Done immediately committed `01/01/2000` and unblocked "Let's go" — with the wheel invisible, so the user never saw the value they were agreeing to.
- **Accepted cost, recorded deliberately:** a user genuinely born 01/01/2000 must now scroll away and back to register an interaction. Seth accepted this on 2026-08-19 when choosing "make Done inert until they scroll" over leaving the silent default in place; making the birthday skippable was rejected as an onboarding-consent scope change needing its own issue.
- **Enforcement:** the OQ-1 assertions in `issue_2322_ios_picker_theming.implementor.happy.test.mjs`, which extract and EXECUTE the real handler bodies out of the shipped source rather than matching strings.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2322, 2026-08-19; flip to ACTIVE only after independent tester PASS, all-green merge, and merged-main verification.
