## DRAFT — issue #2492 (a migration on main fails the #1931 clean replay, blocking unrelated PRs)

### I-PROPOSED-2492-FILTERED-REPLAY-SKIP-CLOSURE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A CI lane that replays a filtered subset of the migration chain is closed under its own skip list. No non-skipped migration may reference an object — function, view, table or column — defined only by a skipped migration, in any context PostgreSQL validates at `CREATE` time. A migration that re-emits an object defined by a skipped migration belongs on that lane's skip list, by **exact filename**, never by an issue-number infix. A skip entry is never removed to green a lane. **Lane discovery is itself fail-closed: a lane whose apply loop contains a `continue` but yields zero parsed skip globs is an error, never an unfiltered lane.**
- **Scope boundary:** governs the *addition* direction only — a reference added to an object a skipped migration supplies. The *removal* direction, where a re-emission drops a control an earlier migration installed, is **#2499** and must stay separate.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2492-replay-skip-closure.mjs` (manifest `batch:A`, self-test then live), checks C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4(a) and C-4(b) with lane-discovery rules R-1…R-4, its eight mutants M-1…M-8, and the paired `…implementor.test.mjs` and `…tester.test.mjs` suites in the same class. `.github/workflows/strict-grep-mingla-business.yml` triggers on `supabase/migrations/**`, `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/scripts/strict-grep/**`, which are the only three routes by which a skip-closure violation can be created.
- **Declared limits:** the guard keys on object names, so signature/overload drift is not detected; and it does not cover the removal direction (#2499).
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2492; activate at CLOSE once the `#1931` `postgres-replay` lane is green from a clean replay on the merged branch and the tester's adversarial cases pass.

## DRAFT — issue #2489 (address privacy is enforced at the server boundary)

### I-PROPOSED-2489-WITHHELD-PRECISION-NEVER-LEAVES-THE-SERVER (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** When an offering's `hideAddressUntilTicket` is set — or ABSENT — no **anon-reachable path** may return its exact coordinate, its combined address string, or the structured street address nested in its theme JSON. "Path" includes the **base relation and every PostgREST embedding of it**, not only derived views and RPCs, and the guarantee must hold against **filtering** as well as projection: privilege to reference a column in a predicate turns a withheld value into something a caller can search for.
- **The venue NAME is part of the address surface.** The stored combined string is `"<venue> · <street>"`, so any field that falls back to it — including a field named for the venue rather than the address — is a second door to the street and must sit inside the same gate.
- **The predicate is defined ONCE** (`public.issue_2489_address_withheld`) and FAILS CLOSED: an absent key, a NULL theme, and any non-boolean value all withhold, and none of them raises. **Every guarded branch must additionally be TOTAL** — no jsonb delete on a non-object, no cast on a non-boolean. A guard that cannot fail protecting a body that can is fail-loud, not fail-closed, and on a list reader one malformed row answers an entire market's request with an exception.
- **A client-side check is never sufficient evidence of compliance** — the assertion must be made against an UNAUTHENTICATED read of the server object.
- **SCOPE LIMIT, stated explicitly:** this invariant binds the `anon` role only. Authenticated non-members retain base-relation read access; that residual is tracked separately and this invariant must NOT be worded as though it covers them until it does.
- **SECOND SCOPE LIMIT, added when the base-relation half shipped:** the base-relation grant withholds the **coordinate** and the **combined address string** from `anon`. It does NOT withhold the theme column, so the **structured street address nested in the theme JSON is still readable by an anonymous caller directly off the base relation**, along with the host's unpublished draft blob. That column is deliberately still granted because two live anonymous buyer-web resolvers read it and cannot render without it, and no gated object serves them a scrubbed theme without withholding an address that is legitimately public for their offering kind. Closing it requires new anonymous read surface and is its own piece of work. **Until it lands, this invariant is true of the coordinate and the address string on every anon path, and true of the theme''s street address only on the DERIVED paths — not on the base relation.** Do not word it, or #2489, as though the anonymous disclosure is fully closed.
- **Structural note.** For objects that respect row-level policy, enforcement belongs on the base relation, where it also protects every caller-rights view for free and cannot be undone by re-emitting a projection. For objects that run with the definer's rights no such protection exists — they bypass policy and column grants by construction — so for those, DETECTION is the defence: a pinned registry of objects required to carry the gate, compared for SET EQUALITY in both directions against what the catalog actually references, at the end of a true-order full-chain replay, with a guard that fails if a declared object does not exist so the check cannot pass by finding nothing.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2489_address_privacy_server_gate.test.sql` — every read executes as `anon`; the reveal-case twins mean an implementation that withholds unconditionally fails rather than passes; a permanent negative control stages a real revealing gate and requires the suite to catch it; and an executed-assertion ledger fails the suite if any scenario stopped running, because a suite that silently stops asserting still reports green and thereby vouches for the hole.
- **Fails on revert:** restoring the ungated projection makes the anon read return a non-NULL coordinate and the fixture raises at SC-1, naming the leaked column.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2489; flip to ACTIVE only after the base-relation half is live as well, independent tester PASS, the reviewed migration apply, an all-green merge, and merged-main verification. **Do not flip while only the projection half has shipped** — the wording above would then certify something untrue.

### I-PROPOSED-2489-A-COLUMN-REVOKE-IS-A-NO-OP-UNDER-A-TABLE-GRANT (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** To withhold a column from a role, **revoke the table-level `SELECT` and grant back the permitted columns.** `REVOKE SELECT (col) ON tbl FROM role` withholds NOTHING while the role still holds table-level `SELECT` on that relation — the table-level grant continues to authorise every column, including the one just named. Any change that means to close a column must assert `has_table_privilege(role, rel, 'SELECT') = false`, not merely `has_column_privilege(...) = false`.
- **Why:** this was specified as a column-level revoke and would have shipped that way. It applies cleanly, exits zero, passes review, and changes nothing — the most expensive shape a privacy fix can take, because the issue then reads as resolved while the disclosure stays open. Verified in both directions on a disposable cluster before the shape was changed.
- **The consequences of the correct shape are real and must be handled BEFORE the grant moves, not discovered after:**
  - `SELECT *` raises `42501` for that role. Every star-select consumer must first be narrowed to an explicit column list.
  - **A caller-rights (`security_invoker = true`) view fails ENTIRELY** — permission denied on the base relation — when its **body** references a withheld column, even if the caller's own query never projects it and even if the column appears only in the view's `WHERE`. The permission check is against the view's rangetable, not the outer projection. Every anon-granted caller-rights view over the relation must therefore be given owner rights (only if it carries its own gate AND its own `WHERE` is a subset of the row policy it stops inheriting) or have its anonymous grant withdrawn. Owner-rights views and `SECURITY DEFINER` functions are unaffected either way — they are protected for free and rely entirely on their own gate.
  - A column added by a later migration is **not** granted to the role until someone grants it. That fails closed, which is correct for a relation carrying location data, but it means a new column is invisible to that role until deliberately opened.
- **Enforcement:** `supabase/migrations/__tests__/issue_2489_phase2_base_relation_grant.test.sql`. NC-2 stages the no-op form inside a savepoint — restore the table-level grant, then revoke the columns the way it was originally specified — and requires the anonymous read to STILL SUCCEED. NC-1 restores the table-level grant alone and requires the suite to see both vectors return. The anti-vacuity scenarios re-run the two live anonymous resolvers' exact column lists, so a grant set that closes the hole by closing the product fails instead of passing.
- **Fails on revert:** deleting the `REVOKE SELECT ON public.events FROM anon` line leaves the table-level grant in place; P2-1 raises immediately, naming the no-op, and P2-2 through P2-5 then read the withheld values.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2489 phase 2; flip to ACTIVE with the invariant above.

### I-PROPOSED-2489-A-COMMENT-IS-NOT-A-GATE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A client comment asserting that a server enforces a privacy guarantee is not evidence that it does. Any renderer relying on a server-side gate must point at the specific object that implements it, and that object must carry a test proving the withheld value is absent from an unauthenticated read.
- **Why:** introduced because a buyer-web renderer asserted, in a comment, a server-side gate that the read path it actually used had never implemented. The comment was true of the sibling RPC and false of the fallback view, and nothing in the codebase could tell the two apart.
- **Enforcement:** the same fixture; every assertion in it executes as `anon` rather than inspecting source text.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2489; flip to ACTIVE on the same conditions as the invariant above.

## DRAFT — issue #2664 (editing a sale window crashes on Android)

### I-PROPOSED-2664-ANDROID-NEVER-DATETIME-PICKER-MODE (DRAFT)

- **Rule:** A `@react-native-community/datetimepicker` element that can reach **Android** must never resolve `mode` to `"datetime"`. Android needs the two real modes sequenced — present `date`, then present `time`, then combine — and the value is committed **once, from both halves, or not at all**: cancelling either dialog leaves the previous value untouched and must never persist a half-set date. Only a **positive** `Platform.OS === "ios"` guard lexically enclosing the element makes it unreachable on Android.
- **Why:** the library registers exactly two Android pickers in `src/picker.android.js` — `date` and `time` — and `materialPickers` in `androidUtils.js` carries the same two keys, so `design` does not route around it. There is no `datetime` entry on Android at all. But `constants.js` still declares `datetime: 'datetime'` in the **shared** mode union, so `mode="datetime"` type-checks, builds clean and ships. The failure is deferred to **unmount**: `datetimepicker.android.js:46` registers `return () => DateTimePickerAndroid.dismiss(mode, design)` and `dismiss` does `pickers[mode].dismiss()` against `undefined`. The picker opens, appears to work, and throws when it closes — which is why it read as "it crashed when I changed the sale window" rather than "the picker never opened". Sentry `MINGLA-BUSINESS-18`, SM-A725F / Android 14, production, `com.sethogieva.minglabusiness@1.1.6+37`. iOS is unaffected: `datetime` is a real iOS mode and the iOS implementation has no equivalent unmount effect.
- **Why the rule is stated as an iOS PIN and not as an "android guard":** #2664 had **two** instances. The reported one was guarded `Platform.OS === "android"`. The second, `BookingDeadlinePicker`, was guarded `Platform.OS !== "web"` — which reaches Android just as surely, and which any sweep keyed on the literal string `Platform.OS === "android"` would have walked straight past. That is exactly how the second instance went unnoticed until this issue. So the invariant inverts the question: an element is Android-reachable **unless something pins it to iOS**. `=== "android"`, `!== "web"`, `!== "ios"` and an unguarded render all reach Android. Note that `Platform.OS !== "ios"` *contains* the substring `ios`; the pin must be matched on the `===` operator, never by searching for the platform name.
- **Enforcement:** `.github/scripts/strict-grep/issue-2664-android-no-datetime-picker-mode.mjs` (manifest `batch:A`, `self-test` then `plain`). C-1 literal `mode="datetime"`, C-2 the same reached through a `mode={…}` expression, C-3 a **per-root** census — each sweep root must exist, must yield a floor of walked files, and must resolve a floor of picker elements — plus a per-file floor for the two fixed files, so a parser that has gone blind fails instead of passing vacuously. A single GLOBAL element floor was not enough and shipped blind: measured contributions are 20 / 0 / 12 / 1, so a global floor of 20 was cleared by `mingla-business/src` alone and three of four roots could vanish with the run still green — breaking one root path silently dropped 781 files and 12 elements. `mingla-business/app` legitimately contributes zero elements (Expo Router routes render no picker today); it is kept in the sweep so a picker added to a route is covered, with `minFiles` rather than `minElements` proving it was walked. The success line is built from what was ACTUALLY walked and reports per-root counts, never from the `SCAN_ROOTS` literal — the previous line named every configured root whether or not it had been opened. Files are selected by **what they import**, never by filename — `BookingDeadlinePicker.tsx` is not a name any filename-keyed sweep would have picked. Comments are stripped before any match — measured honestly, today's source passes even without stripping, so the stripping guards the *next* comment rather than this one: a developer documenting the bug by pasting the offending element into a comment would otherwise have the gate fire on their documentation (M-10 fixtures exactly that, and fails when stripping is removed). Twenty-one mutants M-1…M-21 cover each Android-reachable guard shape, the ternary-else branch, an aliased import, the `!== "ios"` substring trap, a longer component name that must not match as a prefix, a vacuity case where a reassuring comment must not rescue a real violation, a broken root path, a root that exists but was not walked, the knife-edge case where one root goes blind while the total still clears a global floor, and the declared-zero root. Each was verified load-bearing by mutating the GATE itself: removing the newline guard reds M-16, replacing per-root accounting with a global floor reds M-18…M-21, and forcing a minimum of one element per root reds M-21. The strict-grep workflow already triggers on `mingla-business/**`, `app-mobile/**`, `packages/**` and `.github/scripts/strict-grep/**`, which are the only routes by which a violation can be created — **no new workflow lane was added** (`I-PROPOSED-2148-CI-TOPOLOGY-BOUNDED`).
- **Also enforced by the scanner:** an apostrophe in JSX text is not a string delimiter. Treating every `'` as one desynchronised comment-stripping — `Brand's local time` opened a zone running to the next apostrophe, and comments inside it were never stripped, so a commented-out picker was scanned as live code. Measured on real source, the old scanner left 18 comment lines unstripped in `CreatorStep2When.tsx` and 2 in `ComposerStepWhen.tsx`; both are now 0. The rule: a JS string literal cannot contain a raw newline, so a quote that does not close on its own line is prose.
- **Declared limits:** the gate requires the **positive** `Platform.OS === "ios"` form. A hypothetical `Platform.OS === "android" ? X : <Picker mode="datetime"/>` is genuinely iOS+web-only but is still flagged; that shape does not exist in the repo, and requiring the positive form keeps the guard readable at the call site. The gate reasons lexically about enclosing JSX conditions and does not follow a platform decision through a variable or a helper function.
- **Fails on revert:** restoring `mode="datetime"` at either call site turns the gate red naming that file and line, and turns the two happy-path suites red on the rendered `mode` prop.
- **Established:** DRAFT at #2664; flip to ACTIVE at CLOSE once the independent tester's adversarial suite passes and the fix is verified on a physical Android device.
